desc: A Decision that allows a character to lose the Celibate Trait at will.
name: Abandon Celibacy

desc: An Interaction allowing you to abandon a Hook you have in exchange for losing Stress Loss Stress.
name: Abandon Hook Interaction

desc:
Absolute is the second-highest level of Dominance. At this level Migration can target De Jure Empire Titles within the The Great Steppe.

Independent Rulers may settle outside of the steppe using the Settle the Steppe Decision
name: Absolute

desc:
Absolute Control is a special state of Control enabled by the Absolute Control Perk, denoting that the ruler has an iron grip over the population.

Whenever Control is at 100, it will instead display as 'Absolute' and give additional bonuses to Taxes and Levies.
name: Absolute Control

desc:
Absolute Crown Authority is the highest level of Crown Authority. Vassals have a -30 Opinion penalty toward their Liege.

At this level — in addition to the effects of High and Limited Crown Authority — the ruler can pick a Designated Heir at a Prestige cost.

Furthermore, vassals cannot declare war even against foreign rulers.
name: Absolute Crown Authority

desc:
Absolute Tribal Authority is the highest level of Tribal Authority. Vassals have a -30 Opinion penalty towards their Liege.

At this level, in addition to the effects of Limited and High Tribal Authority, rulers can now settle and become Feudal.

Unreformed Tribal Pagan rulers require this law to reform their Faith.
name: Absolute Tribal Authority

desc:
The Knight holding an Accolade.

To be an Acclaimed Knight, a Knight must be Unlanded or a Baron, with at least … or more Prowess. An Acclaimed Knight must be eligible for at least one Accolade Attribute which is not already possessed by another of their Liege's Acclaimed Knights.

Acclaimed Knights are less likely to be killed or taken prisoner in battle. They may improve their Glory principally by fighting Wars and attending Activities like the Grand Tournament.

Acclaimed knights may occasionally gain Skills and Traits related to their Accolade's Attributes
name: Acclaimed Knight

desc:
Accolades are honors given to Knights by their Liege.

The Knight who holds an Accolade becomes an Acclaimed Knight.

As the Acclaimed Knight gains Glory, their Squires Aptitude increases (improving Accolade Succession) and Accolade Ranks may be gained. These allow more Accolade Attributes to be unlocked, offering stronger bonuses.

When an Acclaimed Knight dies, Accolade Succession takes place and the knight is immediately replaced with a successor whose skills are modified by Squires Aptitude.

Innovations and higher Tiers allow Rulers to have more Accolades simultaneously.
name: Accolade

desc:
An Accolade has up to 3 Attributes, which provide scaling bonuses as their higher levels are unlocked. Each Attribute has 3 Levels. When an Accolade increases its Accolade Rank, its owner may either increase the level of an existing Attributes or add a new Attribute to the Accolade. The Acclaimed Knight, however, must satisfy any new Attribute's requirements.

Each Knight is only eligible for certain Attributes, which may be based on Traits, Skills or experiential unlocks while serving as a Knight.

Every Accolade must have unique Attributes: a Liege cannot duplicate Attributes between Accolades. Each Accolade may also specialize in only 1 Men-at-Arms-type Attribute.
name: Accolade Attribute

desc:
An Accolade has 6 progressive Ranks which allow its owner to unlock and improve Accolade Attribute bonuses, such as Knight Army Modifiers.

Gaining Glory unlocks each Rank, while losing Glory can cause them to be lost. When an Accolade loses a Rank, one level of one Accolade Attribute will become disabled. Regaining the Rank will cause the Attribute and its bonus to be restored.
name: Accolade Rank

desc:
Accolade Succession happens when an Accolade's Acclaimed Knight dies or becomes invalid.

The former Acclaimed Knight is immediately replaced. Young Courtiers and Knights trained due to the Accolade's Squires Aptitude are first favored as Successors; then other knights, other courtiers, wanderers, and finally newly-created Characters. Based on the Aptitude of the Accolade's Squires, the new Knight will receive increased Prowess Skill, Martial Skill, Hastiluder Trait Experience, and possibly other Skills.

After Accolade Succession, a small amount of Glory may be lost and the Accolade's Squires Aptitude is reset to now reflect the skills and experience of its new Acclaimed Knight

The Acclaimed Knight dying in battle, a duel or another honorable manner will negate Glory loss and improve the Accolade's Squires.
name: Accolade Succession

desc: When the host and guests have arrived and are engaged in an Activity it is considered to be active.
name: Active

desc:
An Activity is a special occasion hosted for a specific purpose, such as going on a Hunt to relieve Stress.

The Host holds the Activity in a specific Location, which affects it in various ways, and everyone who attends must Travel there.

Every attending Character interacts with each other by setting an Intent, which they try to pursue during the Activity.…
name: Activity

desc:
A Guest at an Activity is any Character invited by the Activity Host.

While they usually cannot affect the Activity as much as their Host, they can still pursue their Intent.
name: Activity Guest

desc:
The Host of an Activity is the Ruler that started it.

They choose the Activity Type, Location, Activity Options and which Guests to invite.
name: Activity Host

desc: All Activities have Options that allow you to customize the planning of your activity. Options have various costs and requirements.
name: Activity Option

desc: An action phase of an activity such as a Contest in a Grand Tournament, Stop on a Tour, or destination of a Pilgrimage during which events occur.
name: Activity Phase

desc:
Every 7 days while in an Activity there is a chance of something happening outside of regular events. These happenings are shown in the top-right corner of the Activity window.

What can happen depends on the Activity Type, for example: the Activity Host can gain Prestige or Activity Guest Opinion in a Feast.

There is always a chance of nothing happening, this is especially likely before the current Activity Phase is Active.
name: Activity Phase Action

desc:
Some Activities and Grand Activities have different types corresponding to special variants of the activity.

For example, when planning a Hunt, you may choose between Standard, Falconry, and Legendary if you fulfill the requirements for that type.
name: Activity Type

desc:
Administrative is a Bureaucratic Government Form that appoints Characters as Governors, to manage and preside over land, called Provinces, on behalf of their Liege.

Administrative Characters have access to Influence and some also have a personal Family Estate.

Only Independent Rulers of an Administrative Realm have Legitimacy, while Vassals do not.

Governor Vassals cannot declare War against each other — Instead, they are encouraged to spend Influence for Appointment Succession and use Schemes to acquire Titles
name: Administrative

desc: Adoption is the act of bringing another Character into your House and Dynasty.
name: Adoption

desc: An Adult is a character of at least 16 years of age.
name: Adult

desc:
Certain Traits, such as Ill, are more dangerous for Adults.

Any penalty to Adult Health stacks with regular penalties to Health, even from the same Trait.
name: Adult Health

desc:
An Adventurer is an Unlanded Character who leads a Camp.

They do not have Vassals, nor do they earn income passively in the usual fashion — instead, they must take Contracts to earn their coin, or call in favors from their Roll of Patrons.

Adventurers may freely roam the map. Their main concern is making sure they have enough Provisions to survive on the move.

Instead of Crown Authority, most Adventurers will set a Camp Purpose. This indicates what type of group they have and why they stick together.

Driven seventh sons with no inheritance, ambitious nomads, petulant run-aways, curious scholars, vicious sell-swords, and deposed nobles alike all flesh out the ranks of these tireless wanderers.

Their sole uniting factor is a hunger for something more than a quiet life of obscurity, and the will to do something about it.
name: Adventurer

desc: A Casus Belli which allows an Adventurer to declare War to attempt to carve out a new Realm
name: Adventurer Invasion

desc:
The Aftermath phase of a Battle occurs whenever one side has won. The victor will attempt to run down as many Retreating Soldiers as possible.

Men-at-Arms with high Pursuit are able to kill more Soldiers during the Aftermath, while Men-at-Arms with high Screen will protect friendly Soldiers.
name: Aftermath

desc: Discovered Secret Scheme Agents may be seen as Criminals by their Liege, and are likely to be Imprisoned if so.
name: Agent Discovery

desc:
An Agent is a participant in a Scheme, who can provide one of three benefits. They can increase Success Chance, reduce Phase Length, or improve Secrecy. Only the target's Courtiers, Guests, and Direct Vassals can be recruited as Agents.

For Hostile Schemes, having agents close to the target is very important. For example Councillors or Close Family of the Scheme Target contribute more to Phase Length and Success Chance.

Being an Agent in a Hostile Scheme is a Crime, and Agent risk being Discovered.
name: Agents

desc: A Aligned Bloc Member House is a House that has joined a House Bloc, and has the same House Aspirations as the Leading House.
name: Aligned Bloc Member House

desc:
An Alliance is a diplomatic relation between two Rulers. Independent Rulers can call on Allies to join each others Wars.

Alliances are created and maintained through a Marriage or Betrothal, as long as the two characters that are wed are closely enough related to the two Rulers. For example, if a King marries off his daughter to another King's son, the two Kings become Allies.

Lieges can also create Alliances with their Vassals. The Liege cannot call the Vassal to War, but it prevents them from joining Factions.
name: Alliance

desc: The Ancestral Claim Casus Belli allows you to annex all lands within a title with which you have a claim gained through a Legitimizing Legend.
name: Ancestral Claim

desc:
Anointment is one type of a Coronation, where the Ruler will seek out the Head of Faith to bless their ascension to the throne. In certain faiths this is necessary to truly be considered a Legitimate ruler of their lands.

To ensure the support of their Head of Faith, the Host can use the Request Anointment Interaction.
name: Anointment

desc:
An Appointment Level is used by some Appointment Succession Laws as a requirement for Characters to become eligible candidates.

Levels are based on the level of a specific currency and each law can use a different currency as a requirement. A higher tier Title will typically require a higher level.

For example: Celestial Appointment Succession requires Merit - A Duchy requires a Merit Rank of 7th Rank or above, while a Kingdom requires 5th Rank or above.
name: Appointment Level

desc:
Under Appointment Succession Law, the Title and its associated Holdings will be inherited by the Candidate with the highest Candidate Score.

The types are:
•Appointment Succession
•Acclamation Succession
•Celestial Appointment Succession
•Celestial Commander Succession
•Minister Appointment
•Grand Marshal Appointment
•Meritocratic Appointment Succession
•Meritocratic Commander Succession
•Ritsuryō Appointment Succession
name: Appointment Succession Law

desc:
The Aptitude of a Character determines how efficient they are at a various roles at Court. Such roles include Court Positions, Diarchs, and, Tax Collectors.

Aptitude is measured in 5 levels, ranging from Terrible to Excellent. A Character's Aptitude level decides the bonuses the Liege gets for employing them in a role at Court.

For example, a Character that is a Physician will naturally be better equipped to serve as a Personal Physician.
name: Aptitude

desc:
Archer Cavalry are mounted Men-at-Arms equipped with ranged weapons.

While each kind of Archer Cavalry is unique, they generally Counter Heavy Infantry, and are in turn Countered by Archers equipped with crossbows.

Archer Cavalry are also often strong on flat Terrain, particularly Steppe.
name: Archer Cavalry

desc:
Archers are Men-at-Arms who fight on foot with ranged weapons.

While each kind of Archer is unique, they generally Counter Skirmishers, and are in turn Countered by Heavy Cavalry and Light Cavalry.
name: Archers

desc:
Armies are used to win Wars by engaging in Battle with other armies, and to Besiege and Occupy enemy Fortified Holdings. Armies are raised in Rally Points and primarily consist of Levies and Men-at-Arms, but can also be bolstered by Mercenaries and Holy Orders.

Armies can move across water by spending an amount of Gold to secure transport. They can suffer losses from Attrition if the local Barony is unable to adequately Supply them.
name: Army

desc:
An Army Commander is a Character in command of an Army. Any of your Courtiers or direct Vassals can potentially be assigned as a Commander (subject to age, Health, and Doctrines).

In Battle, the Martial Skill of the Commander heavily influences the Advantage. As long as there is a Commander present, additional Rolls will be made in attempt to increase the Advantage.

In addition, Commander Traits can provide an Army with many different perks, both in and out of Battle.
name: Army Commander

desc:
An Artifact is a noteworthy object that provides bonuses to the Character who uses it.

…

Some Artifacts are more special than others, and have a higher Rarity

Just like with Titles, Characters can get Artifact Claims on an Artifact, and try to take that Artifact for themselves.

Artifacts also have a Durability: when it reaches zero, the Artifact is destroyed.

Artifacts are always inherited by the owner's Player Heir. If an Artifact is inherited by someone who is not a Close Family Member, it will lose Durability or even be destroyed outright.
name: Artifact

desc:
An Artifact Claim represents someone's legal rights to an Artifact.

Having a Claim on an Artifact means that you can take various actions towards that artifact, and its owner, if you do not currently possess it (for example using the Steal Artifact Scheme).

There are Personal Artifact Claims for Character, and House Artifact Claims for Houses.

Artifact claims are simpler than those for Title Claims; they either exist, or they don't. They are also not inherited past the first generation.
name: Artifact Claim

desc:
Every Artifact has a Durability. When all Durability is lost, the Artifact is destroyed.

Durability decays over time, but can also be lost in certain events, such as Sieges and on Succession.

Durability can be restored by choosing to Reforge or Repair the Artifact.
name: Artifact Durability

desc:
Some Artifacts are rarer than others, which is reflected in their Rarity.

The levels are, from lowest to highest:
•Common (never shown since it is the default)
•Masterwork
•Famed
•Illustrious
name: Artifact Rarity

desc: In Crusader Kings III, this character experiences little or no attraction to other characters regardless of gender.
name: Asexual

desc:
With the promise to boost production and incur abundance for their followers, the Creation Aspect give bonuses to economical and organizational undertakings.
•Focuses on Stewardship
•Chaining construction awards Aspect of Creation stacks
•Regular construction awards Piety
•Rearing Legitimate Children awards Piety
•Has access to the Coerce Contribution Scheme
•May only die from Natural Cause or Religious Deaths
name: Aspect of Creation

desc:
Fear and dread is the way to rule. True power lies in the ability to extinguish life. The Destruction Aspect provides bonuses to those who divide and conquers.
•Focuses on Martial
•Has bonuses to military modifiers
•Has access to the Plunder for Contribution Casus Belli
•May only die from Natural Cause, Religious or Combat Deaths
name: Aspect of Destruction

desc:
A peaceful realm is a prosperous realm — the Serenity Aspect cherishes tranquility and diplomatic dealings, awarding bonuses to those who align with its cause.
•Focuses on Diplomacy
•Avoiding Offensive Wars is premiered by Aspect of Serenity stacks
•Sway and Befriend Schemes are more successful
•May also Request Great Project Contributions from Allies
•May only die from Natural Cause or Religious Deaths
name: Aspect of Serenity

desc:
Benevolent or devious; the Trickster Aspect rewards being able to control others without them knowing it. What is godhood for if not to shape the world in your image?
•Focuses on Intrigue
•May use Piety to bribe Agents in Schemes
•Has access to the Leverage Contribution Scheme
•May only die from Natural Cause, Religious or Murder Deaths
name: Aspect of Trickery

desc: An Assault is when a Besieging Army attempts to storm a Fortified Holding at the risk of losing a lot of Soldiers. Assaults can only be attempted if the walls of the Holding have been Breached, which requires that the Army contains Siege Weapons.
name: Assault

desc:
This Faith differs in a way that is not particularly significant.
Intermarriage may still happen.

Effects:
…
name: Astray

desc:
Characters who have the Warmonger Tenet as part of their Faith will have the 'At Peace Opinion' instead of the Offensive War Opinion penalty.

If you are at peace for too long, your Vassals will think less of you (if they share your Faith).
name: At Peace Opinion

desc:
Attraction is a type of Opinion that only affects characters whose Sexual Orientation matches your gender.

For example, a Homosexual man would experience this Opinion towards other men, an Asexual character would not experience it towards anyone, and a Heterosexual woman would experience it towards men.

This type of Opinion stops having an effect for women above … years of age, and for men above … years of age.
name: Attraction

desc:
Armies can suffer from Attrition, which is when Soldiers are lost due to desertion, disease or starvation.

Attrition occurs when an Army is out of Supplies, besieging a Fortified Holding, or moving from one hostile County into another if the target location doesn't border a County already under control.
name: Attrition

desc: 'Autonomous Vassals' is the lowest level of Crown Authority. At this level, Vassals have no Opinion penalty toward their Liege, and the liege only has basic power over them.
name: Autonomous Vassals Crown Authority

desc:
In order to serve on a ruler's Council, a Spouse must be available to carry out the responsibilities of that role.

Various circumstances can prevent a Spouse from fulfilling these responsibilities, but several of the most common ones include:
•Being the Ruler of their own Realm
•Residing in another Ruler's Court
•Being Imprisoned, either at home or abroad
•Having the Incapable Trait

If an unavailable Spouse becomes available again, they will automatically resume their duties on the Council.

Spouses who are Rulers in their own right can still serve on the Council if they are your Direct Vassals, but otherwise will never be considered available.
name: Available Spouse

desc:
Imprisoned Characters can be Banished from the Realm, which is arguably the harshest form of punishment. Banished Landed Rulers are deposed, while Banished Courtiers have their assets seized.

Banishment without a reason (e.g. some severe Crime) is considered extremely Tyrannical.
name: Banishment

desc: A Banishment Reason gives a Liege the opportunity to freely Banish any subject they have in their Dungeon. They are most often gained from the subject being a Criminal.
name: Banishment Reason

desc: The Activity Phase in a Grand Wedding in which food and drinks are offered, and the guests enjoy the entertainment and mingle.
name: Banquet

desc:
This special Interaction is available to Involved Rulers who are in a defensive War.

The War Leader asks a neighboring higher-Rank Ruler to join their war in exchange for becoming their Vassal.
name: Bargain Fealty

desc:
A Baron is a Ruler whose Primary Title is a Barony.

Their Rank is the lowest possible, directly below Counts. As such, they cannot have Vassals and any non-Baron can be their Liege.
name: Baron

desc:
A Barony is a Title of the lowest Tier.

Baronies have the smallest footprint on the map, organized into larger Counties.

Barony Titles must always have a Holder if they contain a Holding.
name: Barony

desc:
Wanua Rulers can raise Barterers to gain Gold through peaceful means. Bartering works similarly to Raiding, with some key differences — it is not a Hostile action, and you need Barter Goods.

You need 2 Barter Goods to gain 1 Loot from a Holding. If you have too little, nothing will happen.

Bartering is a friendly action, and the targeted holding will gain Recently Bartered upon completion. Unlike Raiding, you can freely Barter in the lands of your Tributaries and Suzerain.
name: Barter

desc:
Barter Goods — which represents various types of island wares such as dried fish or … crafts — are used to Barter and upkeep Armies by Wanua Rulers.

Barter Goods are produced by the Tribal Hold and other Buildings.
name: Barter Goods

desc:
Wanua Rulers can Barter by raising their Armies as Barterers. They work similarly to Raiders, except that they will not be Hostile to the Holder of the targeted Holding.

Raiding Armies of other Rulers can fight Barterers and steal their Loot.
name: Barterer

desc:
A Modifier may change the Base Contribution of your Vassals Obligations. This is not the same as Contribution.

If you have a … that has a total Income of 10 Gold and pays you 1 … per month, and you gain a … that increases Base Contribution by 10%, then the … instead pays you 2 ….
name: Base Contribution

desc:
Bastards are illegitimate children born out of wedlock. As such, they are barred from inheriting Titles. However, their parents can legitimize their child with the approval of their House Head.

Which House a bastard belongs to is determined by the Doctrines of their parents' Faiths when they are born.

If Bastards are granted Titles or have children of their own, they will found a new Dynasty.
name: Bastard

desc:
Battles start when two opposing Armies enter the same Barony.

At the start of a Battle, one side usually starts with Advantage dependent on factors like Terrain, Commander and Commander Traits.

Armies take Casualties based on the amount of Damage sustained. The Battle enters its Aftermath when no Soldiers remain for one side.

The winner of a Battle is awarded War Score dependent on the magnitude of the victory.
name: Battle

desc:
Battle Advantage makes one side in Battle do more damage. The higher the Advantage, the more damage the Soldiers will do.

Battles often start with one side having a higher Advantage based on Terrain and the Martial Skill and Commander Traits of the Commander. Either side may then gain additional Advantage from Commander Rolls.
name: Battle Advantage

desc: A Battle Phase is one part of a Battle. Battles have three distinct phases; Maneuver, Main Phase, and Aftermath.
name: Battle Phase

desc: Advantage Rolls are made by each Commander during Battle. These are done on a scale from 0-10 and are completely random, but can have a decisive effect on the outcome of the Battle.
name: Battle Roll

desc: A Decision unlocked by certain Traditions which allows a Ruler of a small Realm to voluntarily leave and become an Adventurer
name: Become Adventurer Decision

desc:
Every participant in a Great Holy War can select a Beneficiary from their Dynasty. Upon victory, the Beneficiary will receive lands in the targeted realm proportional to the War Contribution of their patron ruler.

The largest contributor can force their Beneficiary to receive the main title being fought over.
name: Beneficiary

desc: A Best Friend is a Special Relation indicating lifelong dedication and support. It is a stronger Special Relation than a Friend. A Character can only have one Best Friend.
name: Best Friend

desc: A Councillor Task performed by the Chancellor, which increases the opinion a chosen Vassals in the Realm has towards their Liege.
name: Bestow Royal Favor

desc: In Crusader Kings III, this character is attracted to characters of either the same or opposite gender.
name: Bisexual

desc:
If you know another Character's Criminal Secret, you may use a Blackmail Character Interaction to potentially gain a Hook on them.

The strength of this Hook varies with the severity of the Secret, which in turn is often determined by Doctrines.
name: Blackmail

desc:
Cohesion measures the unity of a House Bloc, with higher levels granting increasing benefits to members of Bloc Member Houses, based on the Leading House's House Aspiration.

The main source is House Relations between Bloc Member Houses, which can affect Cohesion positively and negatively. Additionally, the Bloc's overall size or mismatched House Aspirations or Government of members can reduce Cohesion.

Maintaining a level of Bloc Cohesion will bestow various bonuses on Member Houses, based on the Aspiration of the Leading House.

Upon reaching 0 Cohesion a House Bloc will automatically dissolve.
name: Bloc Cohesion

desc:
A Bloc Expansion War is a special type of War waged by a Bloc member.

If victorious, the winner may appoint a Ruler to the contested Titles, or retain them for themselves.

Appointing a Ruler in this way will add a Hook on the recipient, add them to the winner's Bloc, and found a new House if the recipient is not a House Head.
name: Bloc Expansion War

desc: A Bloc Member House is any House that has joined a House Bloc, including its Leading House.
name: Bloc Member House

desc: A Bloc Member Ruler is a Ruler who is a member of a House Bloc.
name: Bloc Member Ruler

desc:
A Bloc Supremacy War is a special type of War waged between the Leading Houses of two Sōryō House Blocs.

Unlike other Wars, all members of both Blocs will join.

The victorious Bloc will gain Cohesion, while the losing Bloc will lose a third of its Cohesion.

In addition, any Sōryō Member Houses of the losing Bloc whose House Head is not Loyal, Hooked by, a sub-Vassal of, an Ally of, Friends with, or Terrified of the losing Leading House's House Head, will join the victorious Bloc.
name: Bloc Supremacy War

desc:
A Blood Brother is a special form of Friend and Ally. Characters may only have one Blood Brother: this Blood Brother becomes a symbolic member of their family (and, thus, must not already be Family). If a Blood Brother's call to War is refused, the Special Relation will break and the two will become Rivals.

Blood Brothers, their Children, and their Primary Spouses have increased mutual Opinion and may negotiate Alliances with one another.

Blood Brotherhood is available through Nomadic Government, the Way of the Nomad Trait, or via Tradition.
name: Blood Brother

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

Available games are:
• Chess
• Pachisi
• Hnefatafl
• Tabula
• Go
• Fidchell
name: Board Game Type

desc:
This is a special type of War available between Involved Rulers of the Iberian Struggle where the attacker aims to Siege a specific enemy County bordering their Realm.

The War Leader gains Gold for capturing the War Target, which will lose Development and Control. Buildings may also be destroyed, yielding more Gold, the chance increasing with Development and Siege Army size.

War Score will be gained rapidly by the attacker upon Occupying the War Target.
name: Border Raid

desc:
A Diarch in an active Power Sharing has access to special Borrowed Powers.

These are special Character Interactions that mimic those their Liege have, or are other abuses of power. Examples include Revoking Titles from fellow Vassals, or siphoning away Gold from their Liege.

Many Borrowed Powers give the Liege an opportunity to Veto them.
name: Borrowed Power

desc:
By arranging Marriages between characters with good Congenital Traits, it is possible to breed children with the same Traits. Lucky offspring might even get a reinforced version of such Traits.

However, the same is true of bad Congenital Traits like Ugly.

It might be tempting to arrange marriages between closely related characters in order to produce better Traits in your children, but this also carries the risk of Inbreeding defects.
name: Breeding

desc: The amount a standard recipient of a Budget Category receives. Recipients may receive more or less than the base rate depending on their Rank, Merit Rank, or other modifiers.
name: Budget Base Rate

desc: The monthly amount of Treasury available for Treasury Budgeting. Consists of the treasury income minus any regular expenses that are not managed by budgeting, such as Vassal Development and Court Amenities.
name: Budget Capacity

desc: One distinct part of Treasury Budgeting that can receive budget allocation. Each budget category can have different recipients, and might pay out in Gold instead of Treasury.
name: Budget Category

desc: The difference in Treasury that a Budget Category will receive compared to the previous budget enactment.
name: Budget Category Trend

desc: A Decision where you build roads to make life easier for pilgrims.
name: Build Pilgrim Roads

desc:
A Builder wants to invest all of their Gold into the Realm. They will empty their treasury to fund Buildings and Men-at-Arms, and often construct more Economic Buildings and Holdings. They only save up gold if directly threatened, such as by a strong Faction.

Builder rulers are slightly less likely to create and promote Legends.

Bold Rulers with a propensity for building and no particular inclination for War tend to be Builders.
Common Traits include Calm, Patient, Diligent, Generous, Stubborn, and Profligate. Rulers with the Domain Focus also tend to be Builders.
name: Builder

desc:
Buildings are improvements that can be constructed in Holdings.

Many types of Buildings can only be constructed in specific Baronies or in certain Terrain.

Each holding has a limited amount of Building slots, so a holding cannot contain all Building types. County Capitals have access to an additional Building slot.

Duchy Buildings and Special Buildings use their own slots.
name: Building

desc: A Bully is a cruel Child who picks on another Child (their Victim), for fun, profit, or just boredom. Upon reaching Adulthood, a Bully may become a Rival, or they may grow out of their childish hate.
name: Bully

desc:
Some Governments are Bureaucratic. Which are highly centralized Governments that typically rely on Governors, Appointment, and landless Noble Families to manage Provinces within the Realm.

Other common features include Domiciles, Influence, and Title Men-at-Arms.

There are several Bureaucratic Governments:
•
•
•
•
•
name: Bureaucratic

desc: An Interaction that allows a character to buy Personal Artifact Claims in exchange for Piety or Prestige.
name: Buy Artifact Claim

desc:
An Interaction that allows a character to buy Unpressed Claims in exchange for Piety.

•A Vassal may not buy a claim on any Liege's Title, and a Liege may not buy a claim on any Vassal's Title
•A King or Emperor may not buy claims on Kingdom Titles, and Emperors may not buy claims on other Empires
•No one may buy a claim on their Head of Faith
name: Buy Claim

desc:
Dynasties always have a founding House, but in order to become House Heads themselves, House members can choose to create their own new House — a Cadet Branch.

Members of such offshoot Houses are free to do the same, eventually leading to a tree of Houses within the larger Dynasty.
name: Cadet Branching

desc:
Camel Cavalry are mounted Men-at-Arms that, similar to Light Cavalry, excel at scouting and pursuing the enemy.

They generally Counter Light Cavalry and are in turn Countered by Spearmen.

Camel Cavalry are often strong in Desert and Dryland Terrain.
name: Camel Cavalry

desc:
Camps are a portable mess of tents, pack animals, and people. They vary in size from just a small circle to great roving armies.

Each Adventurer has a Camp Domicile which moves across the map with them.

Camp Upgrades may be built here, which provide powerful bonuses to the Adventurer in lieu of Counties of their own. Followers, like their Family and Knights, travel with the Camp, and may be appointed as Officers.

Like Courts, Camps include some nameless Characters not important enough to portray — albeit less of them.

Even when not Traveling between Counties, Camps are generally not static in the Location they're in, and will move around every few nights.
name: Camp

desc:
Camp Purposes are what passes for law in the free-spirited anarchy of Camps.

They represent the binding force that motivates the Camp to stay together, whether that be scholarly inclination, sellswording skills, or a burning desire to put a rightful ruler back on their throne.

Different Purposes unlock different Camp Upgrades (and in turn unique Officers), lead to different events or event options, and affect which Contracts are spawned.

Camp Purpose also affects the Adventurer's title and the clothing of their Followers.
name: Camp Purpose

desc:
Unlike the rigid hierarchy of a Court, Camps are largely informal places where grumbling from important Characters other than the leading Adventurer can matter a great deal.

Steadfast Camps confer positive Character Modifiers on their Adventurer. They require the majority Opinion of all named Characters to be … or more.

Mutinous Camps apply negative Character Modifiers to their Adventurer. They require the majority Opinion of all named Characters to be … or less.

Placated Camps are any where the range of Opinions fall between these two extremes. They apply no Modifiers.

The effects of Camp Temperament scale with an Adventurer's Level of Fame. The more famous the Adventurer, the more dramatic the possible benefits — and drawbacks — of the atmosphere in their Camp.
name: Camp Temperament

desc:
Camp Upgrades are unique improvements to a Camp.

Mechanically, they are Domicile Buildings — though many represent social customs or simply areas of focus for the Camp, rather than being literal structures.

The bonuses they can confer include:
• Unlocking new Officers
• Powerful Skill buffs for Followers
• Boosting the strength of Men-at-Arms
• Unlocking actions that Landed Rulers take for granted.

When an Adventurer becomes Landed, their Camp Upgrades are liquidated and a portion refunded as Gold.
name: Camp Upgrade

desc:
A Candidate List contains all potential Characters who are eligible to gain Titles with certain types of Appointment.

Candidates are sorted based on their Candidate Score. Some Appointment Succession Laws use Merit, which will sort the candidates by their Merit Rank first and Candidate Score second.

When the Holder of a Title with Appointment dies, the Title will pass to the highest ranking character in the list. If the character holds a Title already, the Title must have higher a higher Prominence, otherwise it will pass to the next character.
name: Candidate List

desc:
Characters in the Line of Succession for a Title with Administrative Government have a Candidate Score.

This score dictates who will receive the title(s) upon Succession and can be changed through various means from Scheming to spending Influence.
name: Candidate Score

desc:
The Capital Duchy Modifier increases the amount of Levies you get out of all Holdings you hold within the same De Jure Duchy as your Capital. It also gives a bonus to all Stationed Men-at-Arms. For this modifier to be active, you need to personally hold the associated Duchy.

This modifier does not stack with Realm Capital bonus.
name: Capital Duchy

desc: Castles are the most heavily fortified Holding Type and the standard type for Feudal, Clan and Tribal Rulers, as well as Holy Orders. They tend to provide more Levies than Taxes.
name: Castle Holding

desc:
Armies will sustain a certain amount of Casualties during a Battle dependent on the amount of Damage taken.

When Soldiers are removed from a Battle, they will be considered to be either Routed Casualties or Fatal Casualties.
name: Casualty

desc:
A Casus Belli ('Cause for War') required to declare War on another Ruler.

The Casus Belli specifies what the War is about, usually a specific territory — the War Target. It is not possible to gain anything more than the Casus Belli allows, regardless of how soundly the enemy is defeated.

One of the most important Casus Bellis are Claims, whether they come from Succession or the Fabricate Claim on County Task.
name: Casus Belli

desc:
A Cautious Ruler wants to be prepared for War to be declared upon them. They are somewhat averse to declaring offensive Wars, instead preferring a slow buildup. They keep a buffer of Gold to help defend themselves, and invest into Buildings and Men-at-Arms to help them feel safe.

Cautious rulers are less likely to create and promote Legends.

Reserved and careful Rulers tend to be Cautious.
Common Traits include Patient, Calm, Craven, Paranoid, and Content. They will never be Fickle.
name: Cautious

desc:
A Decision that enables you to improve Development, Control, Building costs, and defensive Advantage in Counties from different Cultures with a Cultural Acceptance of 75% or more.

Taking the Decision will also increase your Prestige Prestige and Levies.

All Counties in the Realm are affected. The Gold cost scales with the number of affected Counties.
name: Celebrate Other Cultures Decision

desc:
Celestial Bureaucracy represents a Celestial Realm's level of centralization and the general power that the Ruler wields over their Vassals.

Only the Top Liege can change Celestial Bureaucracy. Celestial Vassals use the same level as their Liege.

There are four levels of Celestial Bureaucracy:
•Autonomous Provinces
•Limited Civil Service
•Centralized Ministries
•Divine Mandate

Increasing Celestial Bureaucracy costs an amount of Prestige depending on Realm Size and the ruler's Learning Skill.
name: Celestial Bureaucracy

desc:
Celestial is a Bureaucratic Government Form in which the Liege appoints characters as Governors, of which there are two types, Civilian and Military.

Characters have access to Influence, Noble Families, Family Estates, and Treasury.

Independent Rulers have Legitimacy, while Vassals focus on obtaining Merit.
name: Celestial Government

desc: The Claimant Faction seeks to install a particular Claimant as Ceremonial Monarch. If successful, the incumbent Ceremonial Liege will have to relinquish their Title to the Claimant. All Faction members will gain a Hook on the Claimant.
name: Ceremonial Claimant Faction

desc: The Ceremonial House refers to the House of the Ceremonial Monarch of a Realm.
name: Ceremonial House

desc:
In certain Realms (such as Japan) a powerful bureaucrat or commander may have taken true power as a Ruling Regent, leaving a nominally reigning Ceremonial Monarch as a mere figurehead and Vassal in practice. All members of a Ceremonial Monarch's House are considered part of the Ceremonial House.

Despite not ruling directly, the Ceremonial House is the most esteemed bloodline in a realm, and other Houses will gain more Prestige for marriages with them, with such connections strongly influencing the succession of the Ruling Regent.

The Ceremonial Monarch may take back true power if they somehow regain the Primary Title of the realm, such as by Faction demand or competing for the Ruling Regent Title using Influence.
name: Ceremonial Monarch

desc: The Activity Phase in a Grand Wedding in which the Spouses exchange vows and get Married.
name: Ceremony

desc: Your Chance of Infection determines how likely you are to contract Diseases from an ongoing Plague.
name: Chance of Infection

desc: The Chancellor is the Councillor in charge of diplomatic efforts, both inside and outside the Realm.
name: Chancellor

desc:
Chaotic Era Types present times when the Empire is shattered, and the Mandate of Heaven is lost - potentially to be regained by those worthy.

There is only one Chaotic Era: …
name: Chaotic Era

desc: Characters are either Noble or Lowborn, Landed or Unlanded, each with their own set of Skills and Traits, goals and aspirations. They come in the form of Rulers, Courtiers and Guests. As long as they are within Diplomatic Range, they can be interacted with.
name: Character

desc:
Death triggers Succession, which is important for Rulers.

If a Player Character dies, the player will continue playing as their Player Heir — or be faced with a Game Over, if they have no valid heir.
name: Character Death

desc: Modifiers held by a Character, affecting their personality, Skills, and even Income. Unlike Traits, Character Modifiers tend to represent temporary effects.
name: Character Modifier

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

In Chess:
• Martial counters Learning
• Learning counters Intrigue
• Intrigue counters Martial
name: Chess

desc: A Child is a character younger than 16.
name: Child

desc:
Certain Traits, such as Measles, are especially dangerous to Children.

Any penalty to Child Health stacks with regular penalties to Health, even from the same Trait.
name: Child Health

desc:
Every child gains a Childhood Trait as they are growing up, such as Rowdy or Charming.

The gained trait is indicative of which Education Focus would suit them best.
name: Childhood Trait

desc: The first level Civil Service Examinations, taken from the age of …. Parents can send their children to the examination through the Send to Children's Examination Interaction.
name: Children's Examination

desc:
Church Holdings are Temples under the control of a Realm Priest.

In Faiths with the Lay Clergy Doctrine, there are no Church Holdings and Temples can be directly held by secular Rulers without penalty.
name: Church Holdings

desc: Cities are the wealthiest Holding Type, favoring Taxes over Levies. They are associated with Republics, and holding them as any of the playable Government Forms will always incur a penalty.
name: City Holding

desc:
The Civil Service Examinations hold a key role in the Administrative functions of Celestial and Meritocratic Governments. 

Through the examination system, bureaucrats are appointed by Merit over lineage, ensuring that the brightest scholars, regardless of heritage, may gain Governorship appointments. 

The examination levels are: 
•Children's: Parents can have their children take the examination from the age of … through the Send to Children's Examination Interaction. 
•Provincial: Characters who are not Landed may attempt the second level of Examinations through the Local Examination Activity. 
•Metropolitan: Held by the Celestial Government through the Capital Examination activity. 
•Palace: The final … entrants at the Capital Examination are invited to a feast at the royal palace, to meet and show their worth to the Son of Heaven.
name: Civil Service Examination

desc:
A War where one or more Vassals and/or Counties rise in revolt against their Liege. They are most commonly the result of a Faction whose demands have not been met.

Losing a Civil War often has consequences that are more severe than the original demands of the rebelling faction.
name: Civil War

desc: Rulers who pursue a Civilian Career Path focus on administrative skills over martial cunning. They are appointed to Civilian Circuits and their Merit will grow according to their success in developing the land with Buildings and increasing the Taxes paid to their Liege.
name: Civilian Career Path

desc:
A Civilian Governor is a Governor with civilian Vassal Obligations. Unlike Military Governors, they are unable to field Title Men-at-Arms and focus solely on administrative tasks and to develop the land they govern.

Characters who pursue a Civilian Career Path can become Civilian Governors.
name: Civilian Governor

desc:
A Claimant is a person with one or more Claims to Titles. Ruler Claimants can press these by using the Claim Casus Belli to declare Wars.

This Casus Belli can also be used to press the Claims of Vassals and even Unlanded characters in your Realm.

Claimants can also lead Factions — even if they do not reside in your Realm.
name: Claimant

desc: The Claimant Faction seeks to install a particular Claimant on the throne of a Title held by their Liege. If successful, the Liege will have to relinquish the Title to the Claimant and the Vassal structure will be updated accordingly. All Faction members will gain a Hook on the Claimant.
name: Claimant Faction

desc: Clans are a Government Form in which the amount of Levies and Taxes given to a Liege by their Vassals is determined by the Aptitude of said Liege's Tax Collector. Clans also make use of House Unity.
name: Clan

desc:
A Clan House Head is in many ways like a normal House Head, but differs in some notable ways.

Clan House Heads do not get a Weak Hook on all the members of their House. They have more influence over House Unity than other house members. Additionally, any house member may challenge a Clan House Head for superiority to become the House Head themself.
name: Clan House Head

desc:
Court Chaplains, Realm Priests, Theocratic Rulers, and anyone with the Devoted trait are considered members of the Clergy.

The Doctrines of the Faith determine who can be a member of the Clergy, and whether members of the Clergy can marry, inherit land, etc.
name: Clergy

desc: This type of Opinion only affects Clergy of your own Faith.
name: Clergy Opinion

desc:
A Cloistered Emperor is a retired Ten'nō who govern as de facto Ruling Regent for the reigning Emperor.

To become Cloistered Emperor, an Emperor must abdicate the Chrysanthemum Throne and become a Monk.
name: Cloistered Emperor

desc:
The Close Family of a character includes:
•Parents
•Grandparents
•Children
•Grandchildren
•Siblings
name: Close Family

desc:
Co-Monarchies are a type of Power Sharing that provides Feudal rulers with a way to select a Designated Heir even in earlier Eras.

The cost for this is entering into a permanent Power Sharing agreement with them, where they will have easier access to many of the same powers as an Entrenched Regent.

Co-Monarchs are only available to Kings and Emperors.
name: Co-Monarchy

desc:
Co-Rulers are a form of Power Sharing where the Diarch is considered to officially and permanently share the rule of the Realm.

They are always the Designated Heir (though may still lose elections), and can only be removed from office by Execution — unless their Liege has an appropriate Cultural Tradition, in which case they can be maimed instead.

Uniquely, when a Co-Ruler executes their Liege or defeats them in a war, they Usurp their Titles. In Cultures where maiming is an acceptable way to remove a Co-Ruler, then the Co-Ruler may also maim their Liege to Usurp them.

Examples of Co-Rulerships include:
•Duumvirates
•Nominal Duumvirates
•Co-Monarchies
name: Co-Rulership

desc:
Collect Taxes is a Councillor Task performed by the Steward.

It increases all taxes in a character's personal Domain.
name: Collect Taxes

desc: Receiving a fatal blow while partaking in a battle, dueling or other martial-related contests, such as Tournaments, are the main ways of passing on in a Combat manner.
name: Combat

desc:
Combat Width indicates how many Soldiers from each side may fight each other concurrently in Battle, and may be affected by factors such as Terrain.

This prevents one side from completely overwhelming the other and is determined at the start of the Battle.
name: Combat Width

desc:
This Modifier is only active for Commanders.

If a character with a Command Modifier commands an Army, it will get this effect.
name: Command Modifier

desc:
Commander Traits are special Traits that confer useful perks to characters when acting as Army Commanders.

Commander Traits are typically acquired by children raised with the Martial Education Focus, but can also be gained through the Martial Lifestyle and other means.
name: Commander Trait

desc:
A Decision that lets a character trade Gold for an Artifact, by commissioning a family epic.
The epic will give Renown and can give also give other bonuses depending on your choices.
name: Commission Epic

desc:
A Commoner or Lowborn Character is not a member of a Noble Dynasty. They can, however, still be powerful Rulers of Theocracies and Republics.

If a Commoner becomes Landed, they immediately become Nobles and found their own Dynasties (except in Republics and Theocracies, which are largely run by Commoners).
name: Commoner

desc: This condition is fulfilled when all De Jure vassal Titles of the targeted title are held by either the Ruler or by their Vassals and none of its Counties are Occupied by hostile Armies.
name: Complete Control

desc: This condition is fulfilled when all Counties in the targeted Region are held by either the ruler or by their Vassals and none of its Counties are occupied by hostile armies.
name: Complete Control

desc:
Whether through sickness with the strife of the Hostility Phase or deft escalation during the Conciliation Phase, the Compromise Phase represents a growing accommodation between the peoples of Iberia. Differences fall by the wayside and shared history and heritage binds former foes together.

The peninsula stands at a cross-roads: if conflicts reappear, then the Opportunity Phase awaits.
name: Compromise Phase

desc: Over time, as tensions in Persia calm down and both supporters and detractors of the Caliphate tire of constant bloodshed, the Iranian Intermezzo might come to end naturally: not with a bang, but with a whimper.
name: Concession

desc:
The product of a notable Compromise Phase, during this Phase, relations between the peoples of Iberia grow so cordial that outsiders find their permissiveness difficult to parse. Inter-Faith Marriages are particularly common.

This can't last forever, though, and abuses of trust will eventually bring the Iberian Struggle back around to the Compromise Phase.
name: Conciliation Phase

desc:
A Concubine is of lesser status than a Spouse, allowed in Faiths with the Concubines Doctrine.

Unlike Marriage, Concubinage does not yield Alliances. Concubines can also be set aside at will, without the complications of a Divorce. The children of Concubines are considered Legitimate.

Concubinage is mutually exclusive with Polygamous.
name: Concubinage

desc: A Ruler who is in a Confederation. They will automatically join the Defensive Wars of their fellow Confederates, and are restricted from attacking or Raiding them.
name: Confederate

desc:
A relation that binds Tribal or Nomadic Rulers in mutual defense, similar to an Alliance. Formed through the Call for Confederation Decision, a confederation requires its members to join each other's Defensive Wars. Confederations are visible in the Diplomacy tab.

Fellow Confederates also may not attack or Raid one another. They are restricted from high levels of Tribal Authority and Dominance, and may not create new Titles.

Confederates may use the Abandon Confederation Decision or Migrate to become Independent. If a confederation is left with only one member, it is destroyed.
name: Confederation

desc: As a Clan Government Ruler you can decide to assign either your Vizier or any of your Spouses as your Confidant. Whoever you choose will support you in your daily tasks.
name: Confidant

desc:
Certain Traits are Congenital and can be inherited by offspring. Through proper Breeding, it is even possible to reinforce some such Traits.

For example, if both parents are Quick, there is a chance that their children will get the even better Intelligent Trait.

Base Skills are not congenital.
name: Congenital

desc:
A Conqueror wants to expand their Realm through War, at any cost. They will invest all of their Gold into the War Chest or to buy Men-at-Arms.

They tend to declare many more Wars than normal, and are rather untrustworthy Allies. They forsake most frivolous pleasures in life, such as hosting or going to Activities and sponsoring Inspirations — to save Gold for crushing their enemies. They will only use Activities to gain enough Prestige and Piety to go to War.

Any non-Cautious Ruler has the potential to become a Conqueror, but normally there are no more than a handful of Rulers worldwide with this archetype.
name: Conqueror

desc:
A Grand Tournament is comprised of a series of Contests, selected by the Activity Host, where Qualifying Contestants can compete to win Prizes and other rewards.

Each Contest uses one of four different ways to determine a winner: Knock-Out, Turns, Teams, and Race.

Your chance of winning a Contest is determined by your Skills, Traits, preparation, and other factors. Eligibility to enter physical Contests is determined by health and sex, based on the Culture and Faith of the Activity Host.
name: Contest

desc:
Different Contests require different talents: Foot, Horse, Bow, Wit, or a combination.

Your aptitude is derived from your Skills, Health, Traits, and Hastiluder Trait Experience.

For example, a Giant with high Prowess has a natural advantage in a Wrestling contest.
name: Contest Aptitude

desc:
Knock-Out Contests determine a winner by pairing all Qualifying Contestants against each other in knock-out bouts until only one remains.

There are three rounds: quarter-finals, semi-finals, and the final.
name: Contest Round

desc:
In order to compete in Grand Tournament Contests, you must fulfill its requirements. Board Games allow all characters to compete, while others, like Wrestling, depend on Martial rules.

Non-competing characters will be Spectators, and potential Contestants may opt-out of participating if they wish to spectate.

Eligibility to enter Contests is determined by gender and health, based on the host's Culture and Religion.
name: Contestant

desc:
Contracts are the primary way that Adventurers make Gold or Prestige. They can also award Provisions, Piety, and even Artifacts.

Each one is a task put out by a local Ruler — generally requiring the Adventurer to perform a Scheme, complete a Travel, or help them in War — and can be undertaken for a reward and to put the Contractor on the Roll of Patrons.

More Contracts are spawned by traveling either long distances or to new Kingdoms.

The higher the Tier or the Ruler offering a Contract, the higher that Contract's Tier. Higher tiers pay substantially better.

Beware Criminal Contracts: their rewards are often excellent, but the world has far less understanding for the petty crimes of some homeless vagrant than a Landed Liege.
name: Contract

desc:
Many Contracts require Adventurers to successfully complete a Scheme.

These can be harmful (like murdering a Contractor's Rival), pleasant (like simply telling stories to entertain their Court for a few months), or innocuous (like transcribing texts for them).

If the Scheme is failed or abandoned for any reason, the Contract is failed too.
name: Contract Scheme

desc:
Contract Tier is reflective of the Tier of the Contractor.

Barons and Counts are one star, Dukes are two stars, and Kings and Emperors are three stars.

Contractors won't offer work to Adventurers with insufficient Level of Fame for their Rank. If you're only Established, then Kings and Emperors won't even consider you.

The higher the Contract Tier, the higher the pay is scaled to be — though the difficulty of the task is generally also higher.

Personality also affects pay: Greedy Characters will pay under the going rate, Generous or Profligate Characters will pay far over it.
name: Contract Tier

desc:
A Contractor is the Character putting out a Contract.

The Contract will generally chiefly affect them, and they are usually the one paying an Adventurer's wages.

Criminal Contracts are generally not put out by their Contractor, and instead focus on exploiting them — for instance, tricking someone into giving you Gold because they signaled their gullability.
name: Contractor

desc:
Contributions allow multiple Rulers to assist in the development of a Great Project, gaining various benefits in return.

Some Contributions are mandatory for progress on the Great Project to start, while others are optional. Remaining optional Contributions can still be made while progress has started, up to certain point in time.
name: Contribution

desc:
A Modifier may change the Contribution of your Vassals Obligations. This is not the same as Base Contribution.

If you have a … that pays you 1 Gold per month, and you gain a … that increases Contribution by 10%, then the … instead pays you 1.1 ….
name: Contribution

desc:
Contributors Rulers that committed to cover at least one Contribution of a Great Project, gaining various benefits in return.

For most Contributions any Subject in the Realm can become a Contributor.
name: Contributor

desc:
A Councillor Task performed by the Court Chaplain which targets a County of a different faith than the Liege.
Progress increases each month, and at 100%, the majority of the Target County has changed from their previous Faith to the Liege's Faith.

Conversion speed is affected by many factors, including the Councillor's Learning Skill and the Fervor of the two Faiths.
name: Convert Faith in County

desc: A Councillor Task performed by the Steward. It targets a De Jure County of the councillor's Liege that is owned by an Independent Ruler. When the county is persuaded, they will ask their Ruler to release them to their De Jure Liege.
name: Convince De Jure Territory

desc:
The Coronation is an Activity wherein a Ruler invites Vassals, peers, and Guests from far and wide to witness their ascension to the throne.

The Coronation comes in two forms, a regular Coronation and an Anointment, with the latter providing better rewards, but at greater costs.

Anticipated rewards:
•Crowned Sovereign or Anointed Sovereign Law
•While the Coronation exists, Factions cannot Press Demands
•Opinion Opinion
•Prestige Prestige
•Legitimacy Legitimacy
•A potent Oath Decision

 Factions and other foes will harm the Coronation's Magnificence
name: Coronation

desc: The Council consists of six Councillors who assist their Ruler in the administration of the Realm. As the heads of their respective departments, they can be assigned various important Councillor Tasks.
name: Council

desc:
Councillors are the primary assistants of any Ruler, and make up the Council. There are six positions on the council: Chancellor, Marshal, Steward, Spymaster, Court Chaplain (or Realm Priest), and finally your Spouse.

Each is in charge of a department that can be given different Councillor Tasks to perform.

Powerful Vassals will be upset if not appointed to one of these positions, meaning you often have to make a choice between placating a powerful vassal or appointing someone who is actually competent.

Serving as a Councillor to your Liege gives you a bonus, which increases with the Rank of the Liege.
name: Councillor

desc:
Councillor Tasks are important jobs that can be given to your Councillors. These tasks can either be general or specifically target a County or Court.

If you have a Special Relation with a Councillor, Tasks with a completion time may take more or less time.

Note that councillors are not physically present to perform these tasks, but merely lead the efforts.
name: Councillor Task

desc:
A Count is a Ruler whose Primary Title is a County.

Their Rank is only above Barons and directly below Dukes, and as such they can have Barons as Vassals, and a Duke or above as their Liege.
name: Count

desc:
When you suspect that a Scheme is targeting you, you can do something about it by directing all your defenses against one type of Scheme at the cost of others.

Because of this, only one can be active at a time. Strengthening defenses in one area involves drawing attention away from another.

They can be used to reduce Secrecy or adjust the Success Chance of different groups of Schemes. They may buy you time or shore up your defenses, but come with drawbacks that mean you do not want to have one active at all times.
name: Countermeasure Focus

desc:
A County is a Title one Tier below a Duchy and one above a Barony.

The Title includes the County Capital in the County, as well as De Jure rights to all the Baronies in the County.

Counties always have Holders because County Capitals cannot be destroyed.
name: County

desc:
The County Capital is the main Holding of a County. This Holding can never be destroyed or Leased out and is always owned by the Ruler who holds the County Title.

County Capitals allows the construction of an additional Building compared to a lesser Holding.
name: County Capital

desc:
County Control measures the grip that the government has on the population of a County. It is crucial especially for collecting Taxes from the Holdings.

When a County changes hands through War, Control goes down drastically, which is a good reason to vassalize the current Holder instead (if the Casus Belli allows). County Control can also be damaged by Sieges and Peasant Uprisings.

Low Control may lead to County Corruption, and the primary way of increasing Control is a Councillor Task available to your Marshal.
name: County Control

desc:
While a County has low Control or its Holder is in Debt, the County might acquire County Corruption. These are various kinds of negative County Modifiers.

County Corruption will fade over time, but if the root cause persists (Debt or low Control), it may reappear.

The Marshal's Increase Control in County Councillor Task can clear out County Corruption faster.
name: County Corruption

desc:
County Fertility exists in Counties located within the The Great Steppe, and can be grazed by Nomadic Rulers to increase their Herd.

A County's Fertility represents the quality of its pastures.

Fertility stabilizes around the Fertility Equilibrium, allowing Nomadic Rulers with a large Domain Limit to sustain their Herd growth. Fertility is affected by the Steppe Seasons and slowly replenished by Herders.

When a Realm's fertility is low, it is a sign to Migrate.

County Control slows down the rate at which Fertility grows by a percentage equal to the current control.
name: County Fertility

desc:
County Modifiers are modifiers that affect a County's various values.

Baronies can have modifiers of their own, and they can be viewed in the Holdings of the County.
name: County Modifier

desc:
Every Ruler has a Court, consisting of various Unlanded Characters who serve their Liege.

Usually, these Courtiers consists of the Ruler's family and a mix of unrelated but potentially useful Nobles and commoners.
name: Court

desc:
Court Amenities are the set standards of living in the Royal Court.

These are set by the Ruler of the Royal Court, with each category (fashion, food, lodging, and servants) having several levels. Spending more on your Amenities typically yields more Court Grandeur Value.

Rulers with the Tribal are barred from choosing higher Amenities.
name: Court Amenities

desc:
A Court Artifact is an Artifact that is put on display in a Ruler's Royal Court, such as tapestries or beautifully illustrated books.

Court Artifacts are one factor determining the Court Grandeur of a Royal Court.

There is no limit to how many Artifacts a Character can have, but only those displayed in a slot of its type has any effect.

You can create new Court Artifacts from Inspired Characters, from the Commission Artifact Decision, or from choosing to Reforge an Inventory Artifact
name: Court Artifact

desc:
The Court Chaplain is the Councillor in charge of religious and spiritual affairs in Faiths with the Lay Clergy Doctrine.

Faiths with the Theocratic Doctrine have the far more powerful (and troublesome) Realm Priest instead of a Court Chaplain.
name: Court Chaplain

desc: A Court Event is an event involving the members of your Court, they are viewable in the Royal Court.
name: Court Event

desc:
A Royal Court's Court Grandeur Value shows how famed the Court is, and unlocks new Court Grandeur Levels as it increases.

The value ranges from 0 and 100, and over time will settle at its Baseline value. The Baseline is affected by things like Dynasty Legacies, how much you're spending on Court Amenities, and if you have any magnificent Court Artifacts.

A portion of Grandeur is lost upon Succession.
name: Court Grandeur

desc:
You are expected to have a Court Grandeur Level that is high enough compared to your Realm Size.

As your Realm becomes larger, your subjects and the world at large expect your Royal Court to be equally grand.

If you do not meet expectations, various penalties will apply. On the other hand, if you exceed expectations, you will instead gain various bonuses.

The Expectations of Tribal Rulers are always the same as their current Grandeur.
name: Court Grandeur Expectations

desc:
A Royal Court's Grandeur Level gives bonuses to its owner, and is unlocked as the Court's Court Grandeur Value increases.

In addition to each level's effects, large Realms are expected to have reached higher Grandeur Levels. This is known as Court Grandeur Expectations.
name: Court Grandeur Level

desc: Wanderers sometimes show up in Court as Guests. They will only stay for a limited time, but can be recruited as permanent Courtiers by the Ruler.
name: Court Guest

desc:
A Court Host is a Ruler who is not the liege of a character, yet still has them in their ….

There are several possible reasons this can occur, such as Wanderers visiting a Ruler or Wards staying in the same Court as their Guardian.
name: Court Host

desc:
A Court Language is the official Language of a Royal Court, spoken by the nobility and used by the bureaucracy.

The Court Grandeur Baseline is increased for each Realm County that shares the Language, for each Royal Court which speaks the same Court Language, and if it is the Ruler's native Language.
name: Court Language

desc:
Court Positions are specialized roles Courtiers and Vassals can be granted in order to aid their Liege.

The benefits you gain from a Court Positions are dictated by the holder's Aptitude for the position.

Giving out Court Positions is free, but you have to pay a monthly salary in Gold, and revoking them costs Prestige.
name: Court Position

desc:
Some Court Positions can perform an additional task, often giving more benefits at an extra cost.

Only one task can be active at a time per Court Position.
name: Court Position Task

desc:
As a part of their Royal Court, Rulers can have a designated Court Type.

Each Court Type provides the Ruler and the Court with their own set of bonuses, depending on Court Grandeur Level.

The Ethos of a Ruler's Culture decides which Court Types they can have.

The different Court Types are:
•Diplomatic Court
•Warlike Court
•Administrative Court
•Intrigue Court
•Scholarly Court
•Tribal Court
name: Court Type

desc:
After serving … years in a Royal Court a Courtier receives a Trait reflecting the Court Type of that court.

The quality of this Trait is decided by how long the Character has served as a Courtier in the Court.
name: Court Type Trait

desc:
A Courtier is an Unlanded character who serves a Ruler in their Court.

Courtiers can:
•Serve as Councillors
•Serve in Court Positions
•Serve in Armies as Commanders or Knights
•Become their Ruler's Vassal if granted a Title
•Let their Ruler press their Claims in War

Adventurers have Followers instead of Courtiers — they serve the same role, albeit generally smellier and with more mud.
name: Courtier

desc:
A Decision that lets a character trade Gold for an Artifact, by commissioning a travel itinerary describing places they have visited.
The itinerary Artifact will give different effects depending on where you have been and what choices you make.
name: Create Travel Itinerary

desc:
Crimes are actions that society views as objectionable enough to be worthy of punishment.

Crimes may be secular (such as a Vassal Revolting against their Liege) or religious (any kind of Shunned behavior that is made illegal by Doctrine). Secular crimes can only be punished by the character(s) who were harmed by the offense, but any Ruler can punish their subjects for religious Crimes.

All crimes give Rulers a valid reason to Imprison Criminals, and, depending on the severity of the Crime, to Revoke their Titles, Banish, Torture, or Execute them. Each Crime can only be punished by a Ruler once, though some Crimes will give the Criminal a negative Fame Trait that they will carry to their grave.

Sometimes characters get away with Crimes, which are then Secrets that can be uncovered by other characters and used for Blackmail.
name: Crime

desc:
A Criminal Contract typically involves seedy contracts that may be lucrative, but will award you Gallowsbait Trait Experience.

Levelling the Gallowsbait Trait will make most of the world hate you more and respect you less, and eventually cause Followers of yours who disapprove of your brigandry to dramatically leave your employ.

Gallowsbait is a highly negative Trait, meaning a character is a petty criminal of the lowest order — at least a murder at court has some kind of class to it.

It can be scrubbed clean with the Wipe Slate Decision.
name: Criminal Contract

desc:
Some Schemes have the possibility of Critical Failure during execution.

Exact outcomes vary, but include the Scheme backfiring on the Owner, or preventing them from attempting the same Scheme against the same Target for some time.
name: Critical Failure

desc:
Crown Authority represents the general power that a Ruler wields over their Vassals.

There are four levels of Crown Authority; Autonomous Vassals, Limited, High, and Absolute. Increasing Crown Authority costs an amount of Prestige depending on the level and the ruler's Learning Skill.

Vassals dislike higher levels of Crown Authority, and lowering it is the primary goal of Liberty Factions.
name: Crown Authority

desc: A Crush is another Child that this Child is developing their first (rather painfully-awkward) feelings for. Upon reaching Adulthood, if the Crush is mutual, it may blossom into becoming Lovers, or the Character may move on with their life.
name: Crush

desc:
Cultural Acceptance measures how accepting two Cultures are of each other.

Primarily, it affects how much Opinion is reduced between Characters of different Cultures. It also affects Popular Opinion, and the cost of forming a Hybrid Culture.

Cultural Acceptance can change from many actions, most notably Wars, granting and revoking Titles, and the Promote Cultural Acceptance Councillor Task.

Over time, Acceptance will return to the Cultural Acceptance Baseline if exceeded.
name: Cultural Acceptance

desc:
Cultural Acceptance has a baseline which it will decay towards if exceeded. The baseline depends on:
•Shared Heritage
•Shared Language
•Shared Faith and Religion, especially if Pluralist or Dharmic
•Shared Ethos within the same Region
name: Cultural Acceptance Baseline

desc:
Each Culture is always Fascinated by a specific Innovation, which greatly increases the speed of discovery at a rate depending on the Skills of the current Culture Head. Each Innovation benefits from a specific Skill.

The Cultural Head can change the Cultural Fascination freely.
name: Cultural Fascination

desc: An Activity Phase during a Royal Tour in which a Vassal is expected to entertain their Liege, which often results in an increase in Popular Opinion and Cultural Acceptance.
name: Cultural Festival

desc: Contact with other Cultures that have undiscovered Innovations will cause one of those Innovations to be discovered more quickly. Among eligible Cultures the one with the highest Cultural Acceptance will be selected to Spread Innovation progress.
name: Cultural Spread

desc:
Traditions represent the practices, habits, values, and ethics of individual Cultures.

Each Tradition grants some type of bonus or special ability to Characters or Counties of that Culture.

…

Cultures can have up to 6 Traditions, but most have fewer.
name: Cultural Tradition

desc:
Culture represents the language and customs of a Character or County.

Characters of different Cultures will have lower Opinions of each other. This penalty can be reduced by increasing Cultural Acceptance.
name: Culture

desc:
A 'Culture Head' is the Ruler who has the most influence over their own Culture.

Specifically, the ruler with largest total number of same-culture Counties within their Realm will become the Cultural Head, regardless of where their Domain is or what other-culture Counties they may possess.…

The Cultural Head can influence which Innovation should be prioritized for discovery by setting the Cultural Fascination.

…
name: Culture Head

desc: The more of two Cultures that coexist in the same Realm, the more intermingling will happen and the Cultures will increase their Cultural Acceptance.
name: Culture Intermingling

desc:
A Soldier's Damage determines how many Casualties they can inflict upon the enemy during a Battle.

A Levy Soldier does … Damage.
name: Damage

desc:
On your Travels you might pass through dangerous lands, for example deserts or swamps, that might impede your journey.

You can mitigate the risks of Danger by improving your Safety. You do this by investing in Travel Options or by hiring a Caravan Master.

Several Cultural Traditions reduce or remove the risks of certain types of Danger.
name: Danger

desc:
Most Titles of are considered part of a higher-Tier Title De Jure ('by law').

For example, a Ruler may be King of England, but their Realm does not yet contain all the lands that are legally considered to be part of England.

The Holder of a Duchy, Kingdom, or Empire always has a Casus Belli to seize control of its De Jure constituent titles.

Vassals will also decide who their Rightful Liege is based on what Title their Primary Title is De Jure a part of.
name: De Jure

desc: The De Jure Capital of a Title is the County that was its historical capital. You can always choose to move your Realm Capital to your Primary Title's De Jure Capital, even if it has already been moved.
name: De Jure Capital

desc:
A slow process by which a Title's De Jure Liege can change. It occurs naturally when a Duchy or Kingdom is completely controlled by a Ruler who does not hold the territory's de jure liege title.

This process can be sped up by assigning your Chancellor to the appropriate Councillor Task (Integrate Title). Duchies can only De Jure Drift into Kingdoms, and Kingdoms can only Drift into Empires.

Letting titles De Jure Drift into your Primary Title is a good way to get rid of the Rightful Liege penalty.

Example: The Duchy of Northumbria is de jure part of England, but the territory of the duchy is entirely within Scotland. Since the King of Scotland does not also hold England, the duchy will start to De Jure Drift toward becoming a part of Scotland.
name: De Jure Drift

desc:
Realms that have been De Jure Partitioned have been split into two same-Tier Titles, but can still be reunited easily.

Either Title can Drift Completely Controlled Duchies from the other Title into its De Jure instantly via Decision.

If either Title is ever destroyed or loses the last of its De Jure Counties, then the remaining Title absorbs all of its De Jure.
name: De Jure Partition

desc:
Debt is the state of having a negative amount of Gold Gold. This typically happens when a Ruler at war hires Mercenaries without having enough Gold to cover the full cost, or when they are at war for too long.

 While in Debt you cannot declare new Wars, your Men-at-Arms do not reinforce, and your enemies will have an Advantage over you in battle. The deeper into debt you fall, the more penalties you will get — fewer Levies, reduced Popular Opinion, and your Vassals will like you less.

In addition to this, various other minor destabilizing events may occur, such as gaining County Corruption in your Domain Counties. 

It is generally a good idea to strike your enemies while they are in Debt, as they will fight with reduced Advantage!
name: Debt

desc:
A Decision is a special action that a Character can take at their leisure.

Each decision has its own set effects, which can range from minor Character changes to Empire-shaking impacts.

Decisions that move a Character to a specific location for a period of time are called Activities.
name: Decision

desc: Defeat is one of three possible Peace Offers. The exact outcome of Defeat in a War depends on the Casus Belli, but defeated Defenders typically lose Titles within the War Target region, whereas defeated Attackers instead lose things like Gold, Prestige and Piety.
name: Defeat

desc: Rulers who have a subject of another Faith may Demand Conversion to change their subject's Faith to their own. The Ruler's Learning skill and the subject's Opinion of their liege are major factors in determining if the subject accepts the demand, or refuses it.
name: Demand Conversion

desc: A Diplomatic Interaction that allows a character to demand payment of Gold in exchange for any Hooks they have.
name: Demand Payment

desc: Demand a Character's loyalty in the form of a Hook by using piety, guile, or intimidation.
name: Demand Submission

desc:
A Dynasty Head may denounce a member of their Dynasty for a cost of Renown.

Any member of the same dynasty (including the Dynasty Head themselves) will gain an Imprisonment Reason against the denounced member.
name: Denounce

desc: Rulers can be Deposed as a result of Faction demands or special events. Their Heirs will inherit their Titles even though the old ruler is still alive.
name: Depose

desc:
When holding a grand sacrificial festival, Characters may designate one of their Prisoners to be the primary sacrifice. This Prisoner is killed first, and may cause the sacrificing character to gain more Piety.

Preferable sacrifices are:
• Landless Characters whose Faith is either … or …
• Landed Characters of at least Count-Rank
• Heads of Faith (though this may have repercussions)
name: Designate Chief Sacrifice

desc: The Designated Heir takes priority when deciding who becomes the Realm Heir.
name: Designated Heir

desc:
A Decision unlocked from the Wandering Lifestyle tree, where you can choose a Terrain group to specialize in. Certain Perks will provide different boons to the terrain group chosen.

Terrain groups one can choose from:
• Forests / Jungles / Taiga / Wetlands
• Mountains / Hills / Desert Mountains
• Plains / Steppe / Farmlands / Floodplains
• Deserts / Drylands / Oasis
name: Designated Terrain

desc: The Destination is the objective whilst Traveling, or one of several objectives. For a Pilgrimage it would be the Holy Site that is Traveled to, whereas for a Tour every single Vassal that is being visited would be considered a Destination.
name: Destination

desc:
Details Map
The Details Map gives you an overview of Terrain and your Domain, and is ideal for moving Regiments and constructing Buildings.

In this mapmode, clicking the map will select Holdings
name: Details Map

desc:
Detractors are Guests at the Coronation Activity opposing the Host in their ascension to the throne. They will attempt to foil the Ruler and ruin their Legitimacy.

They are directly opposed to the Supporters, guests who are attempting to aid the host.
