name: Detractor

desc: A Decision allowing you to improve your Capital. Grants Development in exchange for Stress.
name: Develop Capital Decision

desc:
Development is a measure of the local infrastructure and technological advancement in a County. 

Higher Development increases the Levies, Taxes, and Supply Limit gained from a County.
name: Development

desc:
Development Growth measures how far along the County is towards increasing its Development.

At 100 Development Growth, the Development increases by 1.
name: Development Growth

desc: Each point of Devotion a character gets increases their progress towards the next Level of Devotion. When a character gains Piety they also gain an equal amount of Devotion.
name: Devotion

desc:
The junior partner during Power Sharing, a Diarch helps their Liege run the Realm.

The Diarch has access to Borrowed Powers, and gain more of these as the Scales of Power tip in their favor.
name: Diarch

desc:
Diarch Aptitude governs how well a Diarch achieves each Mandate set by their Liege.

Both Skills and Personality Traits play a role. For instance, a Greedy Diarch tasked with the 'Fill Coffers' Mandate may not send as much Gold to their Liege.

Diarchs are well-suited to a Mandate when they have around 40+ Aptitude for it.
name: Diarch Aptitude

desc: When a Diarch uses their Borrowed Powers, their Liege may use their Diarchy Veto to stop them, at the cost of Prestige
name: Diarchy Veto

desc: A Diplomacy Contract typically involves settling local disputes or negotiating advantageous deals using your wit.
name: Diplomacy Contract

desc: The Diplomacy Lifestyle is suitable for Characters who want to gain Claims and Casus Bellis, increase their Prestige, or gain boons from Family and Friends.
name: Diplomacy Lifestyle

desc:
Diplomacy is a Skill representing a Character's ability to charm, negotiate and persuade.

Diplomacy directly affects the Opinions other characters have of you. It is also used to further Diplomatic Schemes.

The corresponding Lifestyle is the Diplomacy Lifestyle.
name: Diplomacy Skill

desc: You can only interact with characters who are within Diplomatic Range. However, neighboring Realms are always in range.
name: Diplomatic Range

desc: Your Direct Vassals are the Vassals that serve under you personally. Vassals-of-vassals are not included.
name: Direct Vassal

desc:
A Directed Great Holy War is declared by a Temporal Head of Faith with the intention of bringing a Kingdom under their own rule.

Rulers of their Faith might choose to assist the Head of Faith, and may get rewards from doing so. Rewards include Piety and potentially having their Dynasty become Landed within the conquered Kingdom.

Rulers of the targeted Religion may choose to defend against this war without the need for an Alliance.
name: Directed Great Holy War

desc:
Natural Disasters encompasses Floods and Earthquakes.

A Natural Disaster will result in the Death of many Characters in the affected Counties, and will further have a significant negative impact on Development, Popular Opinion, and Control in accordance with the disaster's severity.

The devastation caused by a Natural Disaster can be undone and the land revitalized with the completion of a Relief Great Project.
name: Disaster

desc:
Disciples are Characters that respect the high status of an Elder and follow their teachings, up to a Limit.

They can access to the Request Mentorship Character Interaction (Scheme) to increase their Skills, and the Make a Request Character Interaction to obtain Gold, Courtiers and more.

A Disciple and an Elder:
•Obtain more Merit
•Are less likely to use Hostile Schemes against each other
•Are more likely to accept Interactions sent by the other
•Are more likely to use friendly Interactions on the other (i.e. Send Gift, Council Invitation, etc.)
•Will both belong to the Elder's Movement
name: Disciple

desc:
The Disciple Limit is a capacity on how many Disciples an Elder can have at a given time.

The limit is … by default. It can be increased by, for example, improving a Domicile with certain Domicile Buildings.
name: Disciple Limit

desc:
Discontent is a measure of how close a Faction is to issuing an ultimatum.

If a Faction's Military Power is at the threshold, Discontent will increase every month. If Military Power is below the threshold, Discontent will decrease. Very powerful Factions will have their Discontent rise quickly.
name: Discontent

desc:
A Dynasty Head may disinherit a member of their Dynasty at the cost of Renown.

This will remove the dynasty member from any regular Line of Succession of any titles that are currently held by other dynasty members.
name: Disinherit

desc: An Interaction allowing you to dismiss a Hook targeting you in exchange for Prestige.
name: Dismiss Hook Interaction

desc:
In Nomadic Realms, obedience determines the loyalty of a Character to their Liege, Suzerain or owner of their Court. Characters can only be obedient to one Ruler at a time.

Obedient characters are less likely to participate in Hostile Schemes, join Wars or join Factions against their liege. They will always support their liege's preferences during Succession and won't press their Claims on them. Non-obedient Tributaries may try to break free.

When a character's score surpasses the Obedience Threshold they become obedient.
name: Disobedient

desc: Disparate Tribes is the lowest level of Tribal Authority. At this level, Vassals have no Opinion penalty towards their Liege, and the liege lacks any power over them other than the ability to demand Levies and Taxes.
name: Disparate Tribes Tribal Authority

desc:
Disrupt Schemes is a Councillor Task performed by the Spymaster.

It increases a Ruler's Scheme Discovery Chance and slows down the hostile Spymaster actions of other Rulers, such as Find Secrets.
name: Disrupt Schemes

desc: The Dissolution Faction seeks to destroy the Realm of their Liege. If they are successful, all the vassals in the realm become Independent, and their liege loses their Primary Title.
name: Dissolution Faction

desc: A Divergent Bloc Member House is a House that has joined a House Bloc, but a different House Aspirations as the Leading House.
name: Divergent Bloc Member House

desc:
Divisive Actions towards your House members will decrease your House Unity.

House Heads can use the Steer House Unity Decision and the Accuse of Decadence Interaction to greatly decrease Unity.

Some examples of divisive actions are:EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Revoke Title
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Declare War
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Imprison
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Move to Dungeon
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Force to Join Faction
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Disinherit
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Denounce
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Expose a Secret
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Blackmail
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Break Betrothal
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Join Independence Faction
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Accuse of Violating Sumptuary Law
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Claim Liege Title
name: Divisive Actions

desc:
Married Spouses can arrange a Divorce, although the rules, requirements and consequences depend on the Doctrines of their Faiths.

Concubines can simply be set aside at will.
name: Divorce

desc: Doctrines could be considered religious laws that determine what is acceptable behavior within a Faith.
name: Doctrines

desc:
A Ruler's Domain is the collection of all Holdings that they personally own.

The fairly static Domain Limit means that Rulers have to rely on Vassals to increase the size of their Realm beyond a certain point.
name: Domain

desc: Domain Fertility is the total County Fertility of all your held Counties.
name: Domain Fertility

desc: Your Domain Income consists of the Taxes that you collect from your own Domain. The amount collected depends on the local Control and Development levels.
name: Domain Income

desc:
The Domain Limit determines how many Holdings you can legally have in your Domain. The Domain Limit is affected by many things, such as your Succession Law and the tier of your Primary Title.

Although you can go above your Domain Limit, doing so will lower your Income and Vassal Opinions.
name: Domain Limit

desc: A Councillor Task performed by the Chancellor, which increases the opinion Vassals in the Realm have towards the Liege.
name: Domestic Affairs

desc:
A Domicile is the private property of certain Characters who have a particular Government Form, such as Administrative and Adventurer.

The Domicile acts as the owner's primary powerbase instead of Holdings, and can be improved with Domicile Buildings.

Every Domicile is located within a designated Barony, and may be moved to a new location. Restrictions may apply depending on the Domicile Type.

Each Domicile has a special landless Title and follows its Succession.
name: Domicile

desc:
All Domiciles can be upgraded with certain Domicile Buildings, which grant income, resources such as Prestige, and many other benefits to the owner.

The availability of buildings depends on the type of Domicile, as each type has a vastly different set of buildings.

Some Domicile Buildings can have Internal Upgrades.
name: Domicile Building

desc:
Each Domicile has only a limited number of potential Slots for new buildings.

New Slots can be unlocked by upgrading the central Domicile Building, like an Estate's … or a Camp's ….

Locked Slots are shown in the Domicile view — there is no way to get extra Slots beyond these.
name: Domicile Building Slot

desc:
Dominance represents the projected power of a Nomadic Ruler. It can be increased by Herd size and will unlock additional Migration options.

There are five different levels of Dominance: Unruly Nomads, Limited, High, Absolute and Unrestricted.

The last level can only ever be obtained by one ruler per playthrough.
name: Dominance

desc:
A Dominant Family is a Powerful Family that has spread their control far and wide. They are considered the most influential House within a Realm.

A member of a Dominant Family is even better at Political Schemes and is even more likely to get what they want when Interacting with other Characters.

A House must control at least … of the Realm to become Dominant.
name: Dominant Family

desc:
Nomads who want to gain a Title of a higher Tier without Migrating have the alternative of fighting the local inhabitants of an area over a title, as long as they have the right Dominance level.

If there is someone holding the title in question, they will begin a war against that target, to usurp the title from them. If there isn't anyone holding the title in question, they will instead fight every single non-Tributary, non-Ally in the De Jure area of the title.

On a victory, the aggressor will gain the title in question, and all defenders will become their Tributary. On a loss, the aggressor will pay Gold Gold to the defender, and lose a significant amount of Dread Dread.

If the Decision taker holds the whole De Jure area, they will simply gain the title immediately, as there are no defenders to be fought.
name: Dominate Title

desc:
Dread is a measure of how feared a Ruler is.

Rulers increase Dread by performing cruel and heinous acts such as torturing and executing Prisoners.

Dread makes it viable to play as a Tyrant, because unruly Vassals can become Intimidated or Terrified, making them too scared to oppose you.

A character's Dread can range from 0 to 100, except for Nomads, who can achieve 150. Over time, their Dread will tend towards their Natural Dread, which is defined by their Personality Traits.

A Dreadful … reaps the following benefits:
•… are discouraged from joining Factions
•… are discouraged from Scheming
•Increases … acceptance (E.g. Title Revocation)
•Increases Offer Vassalization acceptance
•Makes Electors more likely to vote as you do
•Makes vassals unlikely to oppose Law changes

Note that brave and bold … are less affected by Dread!
name: Dread

desc: A Casus Belli that allows the seizure of Counties required to create an Uncreated Title of Duchy rank.
name: Ducal Conquest Casus Belli

desc:
A Duchy is a Title one Tier below a Kingdom and one above a County.

The Holder of a Duchy has De Jure rights to its constituent Counties and can have Counts as Vassals.

Duchies may be dormant and have no current Holder. Such Title Succession can be created by a Ruler who controls at least half of its Counties.
name: Duchy

desc:
Duchy Buildings are powerful Buildings that can only be constructed in the De Jure Capital of a Duchy. Only one type can be constructed in each Duchy.

Duchy Buildings are only active if the owner also holds the associated Duchy Title.

Many Duchy Buildings have modifiers that affect all Holdings in the Duchy, making them powerful tools for specializing your Domain.
name: Duchy Building

desc:
As Characters Duel, they may gain temporary advantage, such as by leveraging Terrain or special Traits. This increases their Prowess for the duration of the current bout, and is lost immediately after.

The opposite of Duel Edge Bonus is Duel Edge Penalty.
name: Duel Edge Bonus

desc:
As Characters Duel, they may be afflicted with temporary disadvantage, often due to their opponent severely hurting or intimidating them. This decreases their Prowess for the duration of the current bout, but is regained immediately after.

The opposite of Duel Edge Penalty is Duel Edge Bonus.
name: Duel Edge Penalty

desc:
A Duke is a Ruler whose Primary Title is a Duchy.

Their Rank is directly above Counts and directly below Kings, and as such they can have Counts as Vassals, and a King or above as their Liege.
name: Duke

desc:
Imprisoned Characters kept in the Dungeon or Stockade suffer from increasing Stress as well as a Health penalty. In time, they are likely to die from Illness or suffer mental breaks.

For Landed Rulers, Commoners are automatically imprisoned in the Dungeon, but can be moved to House Arrest.
name: Dungeon

desc:
A Duumvirate is the rule of one Empire by two Characters. A senior emperor (the Liege), and a junior emperor (the Co-Emperor).

They generate passive Influence for both themselves and their senior emperor. How much exactly scales up every … years in the job, including any time they spent as Nominal Co-Emperor.

In practice, most power still rests in the hands of the Liege who actually holds the imperial title rather than their Diarch, but the Co-Emperor does have access to several powerful ways to affect the Realm & is a cheaper candidate to promote for Administrative positions.

Notably, Co-Emperors can use the Imperial Expedition Casus Belli at higher levels of Scales of Power swing.

Co-Emperors are able to Usurp their senior emperor via ritually maiming them.
name: Duumvirate

desc:
The Dynastic Cycle depicts the socio-political status of the Great Empire of China, which flows through Dynastic Cycle Eras of stability, instability, and chaos.

Key to the Dynastic Cycle is the Mandate of Heaven, a form of Legitimacy held by the Emperor. If it is ever lost, the Great Empire of China will shatter - until it is again united by someone worthy to be the Son of Heaven.
name: Dynastic Cycle

desc:
Certain Situations transition between Situation Phases when a Situation Catalyst occurs.

A list of which Situation Catalyst are important in each Situation Phase can be found in the Situation window.
name: Dynastic Cycle Catalyst

desc:
The socio-political state of the Dynastic Cycle.

Eras:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStable Era: …, …
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUnstable Era: …
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETChaotic Era: …
name: Dynastic Cycle Era

desc:
There are three Era Types in the Dynastic Cycle, they categorize the Dynastic Cycle Eras and place each into the three-part repeating nature of the Dynastic Cycle.

Era Types: Stable Era, Unstable Era, Chaotic Era
name: Dynastic Cycle Era Type

desc:
A Dynasty is a group of Noble descendants of a Landed ancestor; the founder of the Dynasty. The original House can split into new ones (Cadet Branches), all still members of the wider Dynasty.

When your Character dies, you must have a Player Heir, or the game will end (though you can pick another ruler and continue playing in the same world).

Much like Prestige for characters, dynasties have Renown.
name: Dynasty

desc:
A Dynasty Head is the House Head that heads the entire Dynasty and all of its Houses.

The Dynasty Head wields certain unique powers over the members of the Dynasty, known as Dynasty Head Interactions. The Dynasty Head also picks Dynasty Legacies for the Dynasty.

Normally, the Dynasty Head is the House Head that can have the most Soldiers. If all House Heads have the Administrative Government, the Dynasty Head is instead whoever has the highest Powerful Family Rating.
name: Dynasty Head

desc:
Interactions that are uniquely available to the Dynasty Head of a Dynasty, against other members of that dynasty.

They cost Renown to use.
name: Dynasty Head Interaction

desc:
Dynasty Legacies are unlockable boons that provide powerful effects to all members of a Dynasty.

The Dynasty Head unlocks Dynasty Legacies by spending Renown, with each Legacy in the same track being progressively more expensive and powerful.

Dynasty Legacies are slow to get, but stay with the Dynasty forever.
name: Dynasty Legacy

desc:
An Earthquake is a type of Natural Disaster which causes grievous and sudden destruction in a small number of Counties.
Earthquakes can only occur in regions which are more prone to seismic activity.
name: Earthquake

desc:
An Empire Title that can be created by the holder of the Roman Empire.

The title is created by taking the Cleave the Empire Decision.
name: Eastern Roman Empire

desc:
A Ruler's Economic Archetype affects how they decide to spend their Gold Gold. It is in large part based on their Traits.

The Economic Archetypes are:
•Warlike
•Cautious
•Builder
•Unpredictable
•Conqueror
name: Economic Archetype

desc: Economic Buildings are Buildings whose primary function is to increase their holding's Domain Income.
name: Economic Building

desc:
All Children between age 6 and 9 can be given an Education Focus geared towards one of the five Skills.

The Education ends with an Education Trait upon reaching Adulthood.

The quality of the Education Trait they receive will depend on how well their Childhood Trait matched their Education Focus as well as the relevant Skill of their Guardian.

When setting the Education Focus, you can also specify whether or not the child should be raised in the Guardian's Faith and/or Culture.
name: Education Focus

desc:
Upon reaching Adulthood, every character receives an Education Trait.

There are five types of Education Traits, each of which directly corresponds a specific Skill.

The quality of the Trait a character receives will depend how well their Childhood Trait matched the Education Focus as well as the relevant Skill of their Guardian.

A characters Education Trait improves how fast they will progress in the corresponding Lifestyle.
name: Education Trait

desc:
An Elder is a Character with one or more Disciples, who follow the Elders' teachings. 

A Disciple and an Elder:
•Obtain more Merit
•Are less likely to use Hostile Schemes against each other
•Are more likely to accept Interactions sent by the other
•Are more likely to use friendly Interactions on the other (i.e. Send Gift, Council Invitation, etc.)
•Will both belong to the Elder's Movement
name: Elder

desc:
As Characters grow older, they can gain age-related Traits like Faltering Heart or Fragile Bones. These normally appear around age 50, but may show up earlier.

You're less likely to get these traits if you have:
•Good Health
•Athletic, Hale, or Whole of Body
•For Withering Mind: Family First, Seducer, knowing Languages, many Friends and Lovers

You're more likely to get them if you have:
•Bad Health
•Drunkard or reclusive
•Obese or Malnourished
•High Stress
•Parents or grandparents with the traits
name: Elder Health Traits

desc:
Certain Traits, such as Pneumonia, are more dangerous for those of at least … years of age.

Any penalty to Elderly Health stacks with regular penalties to Health, even from the same Trait.
name: Elderly Health

desc: Electors are the characters who get to vote on their preferred Title Heir under Elective Succession Laws. The specific Law determines who is considered an Elector.
name: Elector

desc:
Elephant Cavalry are mounted, often armored Men-at-Arms.

While each kind of Elephant Cavalry is unique, they are generally a strong Counter to infantry units, and are in turn Countered by Spearmen.

Elephant Cavalry are also often strong in Jungle Terrain.
name: Elephant Cavalry

desc:
Eligible Children are, by law, allowed to inherit their parent's Titles.

Bastards are not considered eligible, as well as children of certain genders under specific Gender Laws.
name: Eligible Child

desc:
An Army will automatically Embark onto a Fleet when given a move order into a Sea Zone, or when there is no land path to the targeted Barony.

Embarking costs a sum of Gold, symbolizing the procurement and construction of ships. For every 100 men Embarking, a cost of … Gold is paid.
name: Embarking

desc: A Decision that enables you to improve your Capital at the cost of a recently conquered County
name: Embellish Capital Decision

desc: A Decision that allows a character to gain the Celibate Trait at will.
name: Embrace Celibacy

desc:
An Emperor is a Ruler whose Primary Title is an Empire.

Their Rank is directly above Kings and directly below Hegemons, and as such they can have Kings and below as Vassals, and only a Hegemon as their Liege.
name: Emperor

desc:
An Empire is a Title one Tier below a Hegemony and one above a Kingdom.

The Holder of an Empire has De Jure rights to its constituent territory and can have Kings as Vassals.

Empires can be dormant and have no current Holder. Such Titles can be created by a Ruler who controls more than 80% of the Counties within.
name: Empire

desc: 1453 AD is the End Date, and upon reaching it the game will end.
name: End Date

desc: An Ending Decision is a unique Decision that ends a Struggle. Such decisions are often only available during particular Phases.
name: Ending Decision

desc: An Ending Phase is a special type of Struggle Phase that ends the Struggle when it is triggered. Involved and Interloper Characters can progress towards the ending phase in the normal way, using Catalysts.
name: Ending Phase

desc:
This is a special type of Interaction available to Involved Rulers which ends a War in a White Peace and establishes Truces.

It may only be used to end wars between other Involved Rulers of lower Rank in which at least one side is Independent or part of the same Realm.
name: Enforce Truce

desc:
It's dangerous to go alone, so you should bring along some companions in your Entourage. Everyone who Travels with you is part of your Entourage and share in the challenges you may face on your journey.

Your Caravan Master is the leader of the Entourage and manages your travel plans.

Some Characters are added to your Entourage by default when planning to travel. Travel Options and Activity Options offer additional ways to add characters.
name: Entourage

desc: An Entrant is a character testing their mettle against the Civil Service Examination Activity.
name: Entrant

desc:
If a Regency lasts too long, it may become Entrenched, and the Regent becomes even more powerful compared to their Liege.

The benefits the Regent gets from the Scales of Power become much more powerful.

To end an Entrenched Regency, the Regent must accept a gift from their Liege, or the Liege must tip the Scales in their favor.
name: Entrenched Regency

desc:
Innovations can only be discovered if the Culture has reached the requisite Era. The next Era can only start past a certain year, and if at least 50% of the Innovations of the previous Era have been discovered.

Rulers with Tribal Government and Nomadic Government can only make use of Tribal Era Innovations.
name: Era

desc: The Escalated Peasant Faction is populated by Counties with low Popular Opinion that already enforced demands of a Peasant Faction on one of your Vassals. Lead by an infamous leader, the faction is dangerous and capable of breaking away from your Realm.
name: Escalated Peasant Faction

desc:
An Estate is a type of Domicile held by the House Head of notable Noble Families within Administrative Realms. They represent private landholdings untied to any particular Landed Title.

Estate Buildings may be constructed here to expand the family's wealth and Influence, and the Estate will be inherited by future generations.
name: Estate

desc:
Estate Buildings are unique and persistent improvements to a Noble Family's Estate.

A large variety of structures are available for construction and may be built by the Estate's owner to generate private income, expand the family's Influence, and gain access to a number of Decisions, Interactions, and more.
name: Estate Building

desc:
The Ethos of a Culture defines its core values, guiding principles, and general attitude of its members towards life in general.

In addition, the Ethos greatly affects the cost for a Culture Head establishing new Traditions.…
name: Ethos

desc:
This Faith is considered anathema.
Intermarriage rarely happens, Holy Wars can be waged.

Effects:
…
name: Evil

desc: Exam Advantage improves the chances of various actions during an Civil Service Examination, such as when answering questions and demonstrating skills.
name: Exam Advantage

desc: An Exam Cheat unlock options that may be used to bypass the upcoming exam. Beware though, getting caught is costly.
name: Exam Cheat

desc:
The Exam Score determines how likely an entrant is to pass a Civil Service Examination

The initial score is based on the entrant's Confucian Education Trait, as well as their Learning, Stewardship and Martial Skills depending on the focus of the Examination.

Only the top ten entrants in the Capital Examination Activity may attempt the Palace Examination.
name: Exam Score

desc: Astounding treasures can be gained, the greatest profits can be made, and ideas and innovations spread the widest when times are good on the Silk Road.
name: Exceptional Bounty

desc:
A Family Epic written through the Commission Epic Decision has a chance of being an Exceptional Epic, which confers greater bonuses than a normal epic.

The chance of the Epic being Exceptional can be affected by event choices.
name: Exceptional Epic

desc:
In an Excommunication War, the attackers are fighting to remove an Excommunicated ruler from power.

If victorious, the attackers will gain a large amount of Piety and the approval of their Head of Faith, while the Excommunicated ruler is forced to abdicate to their Heir.

However, if the Excommunicated ruler wins, their Head of Faith is forced to revoke their Excommunication, as they have proven their righteousness on the battlefield.
name: Excommunicated Ruler

desc:
Characters who are Excommunicated by their Head of Faith are seen as Criminals by other characters of their Faith.

Independent Rulers who have been Excommunicated may have an Excommunication War declared on them.

Excommunication can be removed either by asking the Head of Faith for forgiveness or by switching to a different Faith.
name: Excommunication

desc:
Imprisoned Characters can be Executed. This is considered Tyrannical unless their imprisoner has an Execution Reason.

Executions increase your Dread and are never well received by the Close Family of the unfortunate target.
name: Execute

desc: A Execution Reason gives a Liege the opportunity to freely Execute a subject they have in their Dungeon. They are most often gained from the subject being a Criminal.
name: Execution Reason

desc:
The Increase Development in County steward task suffers from diminishing returns. The more Development a … already has, the more Development Growth is penalized.

By default, … reach the maximum … penalty at 10 Development. Each Era has an Innovation which significantly increases this limit, going all the way up to 90 Development in the Late Medieval ….

Innovations that affect the Existing Development modifier:
• Public Works
• Communal Government
• Urbanization
• Renaissance Thought
name: Existing Development

desc: A Decision that enables you to increase the number of Buildings available in a City Holding.
name: Expand Cities Decision

desc:
A special war for Nomadic Rulers for either an area within their De Jure lands, or to expand their De Jure area to new frontiers.

All Nomadic Rulers of a Duchy Tier or higher can start the war within their De Jure. On a victory they will attempt to either Vassalize the defender or force them to become a Tributary, or conquer their lands altogether if they hold land outside of the target lands of the war.

To expand their dominion to foreign lands, a Nomadic Ruler has to be of a Kingdom Tier or higher. On a victory they will still attempt to Vassalize, Tributarize, or conquer the lands, but the lands will also immediately shift De Jure to the primary title of the Nomadic ruler.
name: Expand Dominance

desc:
The Expansion Decree dictate that all Subjects focus their efforts on expanding the Realm.

Increasing soldier count, military accommodations and supporting any eventual Wars directed by their Mandala Ruler is imperative.
name: Expansion Decree

desc:
The Legitimacy Level that Vassals expect of their Ruler, based on their historical relationship. Some factors that lower the Expectations are:
•Being the De Jure Liege of the vassal
•Being part of the Close Family of the vassal
•Being the Preferred Heir of the vassal
•Being the same Dynasty that the vassal has served for longer than 50 years
•The vassal not being a Powerful Vassal

If the actual Level is below their Expectations they may become unruly: their Opinion will be lower and they may join Factions against their Liege.

Expectations increase with the level of their Primary Title, as well as with the Era.
name: Expected Legitimacy

desc: A Decision allowing you to accelerate your Scheme. Grants Advantages in exchange for Stress.
name: Expedite Schemes Decision

desc:
The Extended Family of a character includes:
•Cousins
•Uncles
•Aunts
•Nephews
•Nieces
name: Extended Family

desc: A Decision offering different opportunities to demand extra Gold from subjects, at a different cost...
name: Extort Subjects Decision

desc:
Not every Character can pull off a Scheme with Skill alone — when the Target is too tough, paying for Extra Measures can help to compensate for one weakness at the expense of another.

Measures are optional: use them tactically.
name: Extra Measure

desc:
If they are discovered, two characters engaged in extramarital sex will suffer consequences depending on their Faith's Doctrines.

•Each character will become known as either a Fornicator or an Adulterer, depending on their own marital status
•If a man and a woman sleep together, it may result in a Bastard pregnancy
•If the characters are of the same gender, consequences are determined by their Faith's Same-Sex Relations Doctrine
•Any sexually transmitted Diseases held by one character may infect the other
name: Extramarital Sex

desc: This Game Rule makes the game significantly more difficult.
name: Extreme Game Rule

desc:
A Councillor Task performed by the Court Chaplain.
Targets a County, and builds progress over time. At 100% Progress, a Claim can be fabricated for a cost of Gold.
name: Fabricate Claim on County

desc:
A Faction is a group of Vassals with common political interests. The local population of Counties can also join certain types of Factions, such as the Peasant Faction.

Factions become dangerous once their Discontent reaches a certain point, at which time they will issue an ultimatum.

If the Liege does not comply, the Faction will rise up in revolt, sparking a Civil War. If the Faction dissolves, the Liege must have at least … War Score to win the War.
name: Faction

desc:
The likelihood of a Character supporting a Faction against their Liege.

It can be affected by a multitude of reasons, the most common being Personality, Opinion, and Culture.
name: Faction Commitment

desc:
Faction Military Power is a measure of the total military strength of a Faction relative to their target.

Each individual faction member adds their full strength to the Faction as long as they remain in the Faction. If the faction target is the Liege of a member, the strength of the member is also subtracted from the relative power of the liege.
name: Faction Military Power

desc:
A Faith is a specific denomination of a larger Religion. All characters and Counties have a Faith just as they have a Culture.

Each Faith is defined by a set of Doctrines with far-reaching consequences for its adherents.

Each Faith also has a Fervor value which controls how vulnerable it is to Heresy (Rulers and Counties converting to other Faiths within the same Religion).
name: Faith

desc:
All Faiths have a relation towards each other Faith that is determined by how closely related they are.

Closeness is decided by several factors, such as if they share Religion, Religious Family, or if the Faith has special Doctrines.

If two Faiths are far apart, they are often able to Holy War each other.

The following relations exist: …, …, …, and ….
name: Faith Hostility

desc: Each point of Fame a character gets increases their progress towards the next Level of Fame. When a character gains Prestige they also gain an equal amount of Fame.
name: Fame

desc: A Fame Trait is a special Trait gained from specific circumstances and affects others' Opinion of them. One can gain these traits as the results of accomplishing a positive deed, or when one's dark Secrets are exposed. Others are the result of one's circumstances at birth.
name: Fame Trait

desc: A character's family consists of their Close Family Members and Extended Family Members.
name: Family

desc: During Battle, many (but usually not most) Soldiers are killed or too badly wounded to ever fight again. These are permanent Casualties as opposed to merely Routed Casualties.
name: Fatal Casualties

desc: Characters that have perished as a direct result of an Plague or Natural Disaster.
name: Fatalities

desc:
Characters can owe each other Favors, which is considered a type of Hook.

Favors can be gained in many ways, but often through various scripted events. Every child born to a Noble House also owes the House Head an initial Favor.
name: Favor

desc: If the main target of the Great Holy War is already held or claimed by a member of the aggressor faith, they will be considered the rightful recipient of the title being fought over, unless the main Contributor decides to give precedence to their Beneficiary.
name: Favored Candidate

desc: The Favored Era is the will of Heaven manifested by Son of Heaven about the course of the Dynastic Cycle. It determines which Stable Era will be enacted after Unstable Era is over.
name: Favored Era

desc:
The Favored Movement is the Movement that has gained the support of Son of Heaven.
• Members have higher Candidate Scores for any Titles in …
•Petitions from Make Movement Petition Decision are more likely to be accepted
•Dynastic Cycle's Catalysts are triggered based on which Movement is favored
•Gains access to Shape the Dynastic Cycle Decision

To become a favored movement you have to defeat the current favored movement leader in Debate Activity.
name: Favored Movement

desc:
A Favorite Child is a direct descendant of the same Dynasty that a Player ruler can choose to favor. They will have a higher Opinion of you and when you die, you can choose to continue your legacy as them, instead of your heir.

Your favorite child can be any children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, as long as they are in your dynasty.
name: Favorite Child

desc: Fertility measures how able a Character is to produce children.
name: Fertility

desc:
Fertility Equilibrium is a prediction of how fertile the County will become over a longer time. It is a value toward which County Fertility will arrive over time.

If the current County Fertility is below the Equilibrium, it will grow, and decline if it's above it.

The Fertility Equilibrium and the speed of change are mostly dependent on the ratio of Growth and Consumption modifiers for the County. If both Growth and Consumption are relatively small, any change will have a much greater effect on the Equilibrium.
name: Fertility Equilibrium

desc:
The Fervor of a Faith ranges from 0 to 100%. Low Fervor makes it easier for Rulers to create new faiths of their own and increases the likelihood of Counties and characters converting to other faiths, including Heresies. High Fervor increases County conversion speed.

Fervor changes naturally with time. Smaller Faiths tend to have higher Fervor. Larger Faiths tend to have low Fervor.

Waging Great Holy Wars and successful Holy Wars will decrease Fervor. Being the target will increase Fervor. Outbreaks of Heresy will increase Fervor significantly.
name: Fervor

desc:
Sometimes, a rivalry can grow into a vendetta against a particular House.

Killing, Torturing, cuckolding, robbing, and winning Wars against members of the target House will increase your House's score, while falling victim to these actions will reduce it.

While a Feud is ongoing, all House members receive a Hostile Schemes bonus against members of the target House, and will be more likely to target its members.

When the Feud ends, your House will be rewarded based on the relative damage inflicted on its enemies, ranging from Pathetic Family to Formidable Family.
name: Feud

desc: Under the Feudal Government Form, a Liege gives their Vassals Land to govern in exchange for Levies and Taxes, regulated by individual Vassal Contract between Vassal and Liege.
name: Feudal

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

In Fidchell:
• Learning counters Prowess
• Prowess counters Diplomacy
• Diplomacy counters Learning
name: Fidchell

desc:
Find Secrets is a Councillor Task performed by the Spymaster.

It targets a Ruler's Court, and tries to uncover Secrets about the characters there.
name: Find Secrets

desc:
Armies who move into a Sea Zone will automatically Embark onto a Fleet. … costs a sum of Gold, symbolizing the procurement and construction of ships.

While on a Fleet, … will be able to traverse water at a rapid pace, though they will cost 25% more maintenance and will start losing Supplies after … days at sea.

Fleets do not engage each other in Battles.

When an Army disembarks, the Fleet will disappear and the Army will become Recently Disembarked.
name: Fleet

desc:
A Flood is a Natural Disaster which causes growing damage in a large number of Counties.
Floods can only occur along the banks of major rivers.
name: Flood

desc:
Each Lifestyle contains a number Focuses, one of which must be chosen upon selecting the Lifestyle.

Focuses provide passive bonuses and influence the types of events that appear. (E.g., having the Temptation Focus will boost Fertility and increase the chances of Seduction-themed events appearing.)

Characters can switch between Focuses within the same Lifestyle without losing the ability to gain experience in that Lifestyle.
name: Focus

desc:
A Follower is an Unlanded character who accompanies an Adventurer.

Mechanically, they are equivalent to Courtiers, though they are under less obligation to show respect or hang around if they dislike their leader.

The collective Opinion of a character's Followers determine their Camp Temperament.

Followers can:
•Serve as Officers
•Serve in Armies as Commanders or Knights
•Let their Adventurer press their Claims in War
name: Follower

desc: Allows to invest Gold Gold in order to motivate the Peasant Faction in another Realm, if they have Counties with negative Popular Opinion.
name: Foment Revolt

desc:
A Casus Belli allowing for the forceful Vassalization of a neighboring independent Ruler of lower rank. Unlocked by the Forced Vassalage Perk.

You can Vassalize any Ruler that does not have more than … Counties in their Realm.

This limit is increased by +… for each of the following innovations:
•Casus Belli
•Chronicle Writing
•Divine Right
•Rightful Ownership
name: Forced Vassalization Casus Belli

desc:
A Councillor Task performed by the Chancellor.
For an Independent Ruler, it increases the opinion other independent rulers have of them. For a vassal, it increases the opinion that other vassals of the same Liege have of them.
name: Foreign Affairs

desc:
You can only comfortably remember a set amount of Languages. If you exceed this limit, you will either have to forget a Language or suffer from Stress.

The Language spoken by your Culture does not count towards this limit.

The limit is determined by:
•Everyone has a Base of 1
•Every … points of Learning Learning increases it by 1
•The Open-Minded Perk increases it by 2
•The Smooth Operator Perk increases it by 1
•The Language Scholars Dynasty Legacy increases it by 1
name: Foreign Language Limit

desc:
Some Holdings are fortified and need to be Besieged and Occupied in order to gain control of the County.

The Fort Level of such Fortified Holdings determines how long the Siege can be expected to last.

A high Fort Level will require Siege Weapons in order to be Besieged efficiently, although each Siege Weapon is only effective up to a certain Fort Level.

Increasing the Fort Level of a non-fortified Holding has no effect.
name: Fort Level

desc: Fortification Buildings are Buildings whose primary function is to either increase their holding's Fort Level or provide bonus Advantage for defenders.
name: Fortification Building

desc:
A Fortified Holding is a Holding with Buildings that increase its Fort Level. County Capitals are always Fortified.

In order to fully Occupy a County, all its Fortified Holdings must be Occupied.
name: Fortified Holding

desc:
A Friend is a Special Relation indicating close friendship and support, and can be had by both Children and Adults.

Friends with a deep connection might become Best Friends.
name: Friend

desc: An Activity in which a Host invites various Characters to offer their respect after a recent Character Death. Funerals often result in increases in Legitimacy, decreases in Stress, and opportunities to show Piety.
name: Funeral

desc:
The game ends when your current lineage dies out.

However, even if the game is over for your lineage, you can still choose to play as another Ruler anywhere in the world.

The game can end in two ways:
•You die without Player Heir
•You reach the year 1453
name: Game Over

desc:
The Garrison of a Fortified Holding protects it from being Besieged by smaller Armies.

The besieging Army needs to have more Soldiers than the Garrison in order for the Siege to progress.

When a Siege is lost, the Garrison is set to …. From there, the Garrison refills every month depending on the Garrison Reinforcement Rate until it reaches its max capacity.

When a Siege begins, the manning of the Garrison affects the required amount of Siege Progress.
name: Garrison

desc:
The Garrison Reinforcement Rate of a Fortified Holding defines how fast the Garrison recovers after losing a Siege.

Every month, the Garrison will regain a percentage of its maximal capacity equal to the current rate. It can be increased by upgrading the Holding.

During a Siege however, the reinforcement is frozen and the rate set to 0.
name: Garrison Reinforcement Rate

desc:
These Doctrines determine which Gender Laws are available to characters of the Faith.

It also determines certain additional rules, such as what Claims can be inherited, who can be Commanders and Knights, and to which of their parents' House a Bastard will belong.

The Gender Doctrines are:
•Male Dominated
•Equal
•Female Dominated
name: Gender Doctrines

desc:
Every Ruler has a main Gender Law that determines who their Titles can pass to on Succession. Gender Laws also affect who can command Armies and the eligibility of having multiple Spouses or Concubines.

Available Gender Laws depend on the 'View on Gender' Doctrine of the Faith.
name: Gender Law

desc:
Sending a Gift to another character will increase their Opinion of you in exchange for GoldGold .

The greedier the recipient, the more Gold you will have to send, and the more Opinion you will get.

The higher your Diplomacy, the more Opinion you will get.
name: Gift

desc:
An Accolade's Glory increases its Accolade Rank.

Glory is gained by the Acclaimed Knight winning Battles, defeating warriors, competing in Grand Tournament Contests, and attending Activities.

However, the Accolade's Glory is lowered when the Acclaimed Knight is involved in losing battles, and may also diminish on Accolade Succession if the Acclaimed Knight did not die in battle, a duel, or some other honorable fashion.
name: Glory

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

In Go:
• Learning counters Martial
• Martial counters Intrigue
• Intrigue counters Learning
name: Go

desc: 'Gold' really represents all liquid assets of a Character; their wealth. It can be spent on many things, most notably constructing Buildings, paying for Regiments, and creating Titles.
name: Gold

desc: A character in University Visit can get up to all sort of mischief when embracing the life of the student. The consequences of their adventures are unpredictable, and include Skill points, lifestyle and stress Traits, lifestyle experience, diseases, and wounds.
name: Goliardic Shenanigans

desc:
A Governance Issue is a task for a Governor to perform.

Issue appears within a Province every few years or so, and often revoles around a problem the Governor must solve. Issues can, however, present opportunities as well.

Successfully solving Issues typically awards Gold, Influence, and experience in the Governor Trait. Depending on the Issue at hand, other rewards may be available as well.

Each Governance Issue has a Tier which affects the rewards it provides.
name: Governance Issue

desc: Every Governance Issue has a Governance Issue Tier, which reflects the overall rewards of an Issue when successfully solved. Solving an Issue with a higher tier will typically result in larger amounts of Gold or Influence, as well as a greater amount of experience gained in the Governor Trait
name: Governance Issue Tier

desc:
A Ruler's Government Form determines what kind of Laws they have access to, as well as what Obligations they have to their Liege if they are not Independent.

The Government forms are: Feudal, Tribal, Clan, Theocracy, Republic, Administrative, Nomadic and Herder.
name: Government

desc:
A Governor is the primary vassal of a Liege with a Bureaucratic Government. They are appointed by their Liege to preside over the lands within the Realm, utilizing their Governor Efficiency.

A Governor's Title, as well as the Counties it includes, is referred to as a Province. Governance Issues may appear inside a Province, which the Governor has to solve.

Governors can accumulate Influence and manipulate the Succession of other Governorships.
name: Governor

desc:
Governor Efficiency is a measurement of how good a Governor is at their job, and how well they manage the Holdings they are assigned to.

The Efficiency affects how much Taxes and Levies a Holding provides, and the effectiveness of Title Men-at-Arms.

A character's Governor Efficiency is mainly decided by their Skills and the Governor Trait.
name: Governor Efficiency

desc: In Administrative Governments that distinguish between Gold and Treasury, Governors receive a Salary in Gold.
name: Governor Salary

desc: Governors can have their appointments formally and publicly confirmed by their Liege.
name: Governorship Confirmation

desc:
Most Schemes have a grace period of around ~… months before they can be discovered monthly.

After the grace period is over, Schemes may be discovered monthly, causing a Breach. This is at a far reduced rate than when the scheme is executed, but checked significantly more frequently.
name: Grace

desc:
Splendid displays of wealth and magnificence, Grand Activities are by nature larger and grander than regular Activities. They may have multiple Activity Phases and offer more chances for customization in planning.

Tours provide the opportunity to visit multiple Vassals in your Realm while Tournaments offer a variety of Contests to host.
name: Grand Activity

desc:
The Grand Chancellor is the highest ranking Minister and is in charge of diplomatic matters. They are typically assigned the position of Secretary Director.

The Chancellor can be the designated Secretary Director, depending on the Grand Secretariat Control Law.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse the Shape the Dynastic Cycle Decision
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETInvite any type of Courtier with the Summon Courtiers for the Celestial Bureau Decision
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options, and at a reduced cost
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Compel Religious Uniformity Great Project
name: Grand Chancellor

desc:
The Grand Marshal is the highest ranking commander in the Realm and commands an Army of Title Men-at-Arms.

The Marshal can be the designated Secretary Director, depending on the Grand Secretariat Control Law.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Grand Campaign Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Construct Great Barracks Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Seize Hegemonic County and Seize Hegemonic Duchy Casus Bellis in … and … Eras
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
name: Grand Marshal

desc:
A Betrothal with the promise attached that a Grand Wedding will be celebrated for the union of the two characters involved.

The Grand Wedding Promise will expire after 3 years. Not organizing a Grand Wedding in time or breaking the Betrothal will bear punishing consequences.
name: Grand Wedding Promise

desc:
Great Buildings are unique Buildings, and are constructed as a result of Great Projects. One famous example is the Great Walls of China.

Great Buildings are usually very powerful, but their utility is tied to specific conditions.
name: Great Building

desc:
A Great Holy War is a special type of War that only the Head of Faith of certain Faiths can declare, with the goal of bringing an entire Kingdom under the rule of their Faith.

Great Holy Wars target all Rulers of another Religion within a chosen Kingdom, forcing them to defend together. If victorious, all Titles within the targeted Kingdom will be seized and divided between the attackers.

Depending on its Doctrines, a Faith might have access to Directed Great Holy Wars, Undirected Great Holy Wars or no Great Holy Wars at all:
•The Armed Pilgrimages, Struggle and Submission, or Warmonger Tenets are required to access to Great Holy Wars in general
•Faiths with a Temporal Head only have access to Directed Great Holy Wars
•Faiths with a Spiritual Head only have access to Undirected Great Holy Wars
•Faiths without a Head of Faith cannot declare any Great Holy Wars, even if they would normally be eligible

Some Faiths have special names for their Great Holy Wars such as 'Crusade' or 'Jihad'. These Great Holy Wars differ in name only, and function as any other Great Holy War.
name: Great Holy War

desc:
Great Projects are massive undertakings that call on all the resources of the Realm.

Some Great Projects involve constructing a Great Building, while others involve recovering from a Natural Disaster.

While the Realm's Ruler oversees the development of the Great Project, Subjects can offer Contributions to assist its progress.
name: Great Project

desc:
A Grudge is a Special Relation indicating unilateral hatred and resentment. The target of a grudge does not return the feelings and may not even know.

Grudges are most commonly formed when one Character does something horrible to another without even realizing they exist — for instance, a king leaving a peasant in their Dungeon for forty years.
name: Grudge

desc:
A Guardian is a Character assigned to Educate a Child (called their Ward).

Guardians tend to pass on their Personality Traits to their Wards, as well as their Culture and/or Faith, if so specified in the Education Focus.

The Guardian can reside in a different Court. Entrusting a Close Family Member to the mercy of another Ruler in this way will increase their Opinion of you.
name: Guardian

desc:
The biggest threat of The Great Steppe. The Gurkhan is that Nomadic Ruler with the biggest Herd in the entire region, marking them as a powerful ally or a dreadful enemy.

Only the Gurkhan may reach the highest level of Dominance, allowing them to become the Greatest of Khans and marking them as a target.
name: Gurkhan

desc:
Characters of most Islamic Faiths can choose to undertake an Activity to go on a Hajj to Mecca as part of their Pilgrimage Doctrine once a year.

Such a journey may be filled with both opportunity and peril, but upon reaching the holy city characters will earn Piety and may receive other rewards.
name: Hajj

desc:
Handgunners are Men-at-Arms who are armed with potent gunpowder weapons.

While each kind of Handgunner is unique, they generally Counter Heavy Infantry, and are in turn Countered by Heavy Cavalry and Light Cavalry.
name: Handgunner

desc: From war, calamity, and unpredictable twists and turns of fate, the Silk Road is at an absolute standstill. Neither money nor ideas are moving, and the only thing gained from following the Silk Road's routes is misery and poverty.
name: Hardship

desc:
Norman rulers and the recently-deposed Anglo-Saxon nobles are locked in a fierce battle for control over England. Such a contest won't end until one or both groups have been wholly removed from power.

As the situation progresses, actions they and other characters take will govern the Resistance and Pacification levels of the region.

Higher Resistance will lead to:
•Lower Cultural Acceptance
•Lower County Control
•A higher chance of Claimant Factions or even a Civil War.

Higher Pacification will lead to:
•Higher Cultural Acceptance
•Rising Dread for the ruler of England
•Access to the Embrace English Culture Decision.
name: Harrying of the North

desc:
A Head of Faith is the formal leader of a Faith. The powers and nature of the Head of Faith depends on the Doctrines of the Faith.

Some Faiths have a Spiritual Head of Faith (e.g. the Pope), some a Temporal Head of Faith (e.g. a Caliph), and some do not have a Head of Faith at all.
name: Head of Faith

desc: Rulers who are also Heads of Faith have an additional realm Succession law, requiring that their Heir be of the same Faith as them. This can never be changed, and Head of Faith Titles cannot have separate Title Succession. The only way to remove this type of realm law is for an external force to destroy the Head of Faith Title.
name: Head of Faith Succession Law

desc:
Health measures how likely a Character is to die by Illnesses and old age.

Old characters have a chance to lose health every year, increasing the older they are.
name: Health

desc:
A Health Trait is a Trait that directly affects one's physical and mental Health, such as Diseases. Temporary traits that affect one's bodily capabilities, such as pregnancies and wounds also falls under this category.

Old Characters may gain Elder Traits.
name: Health Trait

desc:
Heavy Cavalry are mounted, heavily armored Men-at-Arms

While each kind of Heavy Cavalry is unique, they generally Counter Archers, and are in turn Countered by Spearmen.

Heavy Cavalry are also often strong on flat Terrain.

In comparison with Light Cavalry, they are usually stronger at raw Damage and Toughness.
name: Heavy Cavalry

desc:
Heavy Infantry are Men-at-Arms who fight on foot, with heavier armor and weapons.

While each kind of Heavy Infantry is unique, they generally Counter Spearmen, and are in turn Countered by Skirmishers.
name: Heavy Infantry

desc:
A Hegemon is a Ruler whose Primary Title is a Hegemony.

Their Rank is the highest possible, directly above Emperors. As such, they can have any non-Hegemons as their Vassals, and they can never have a Liege.
name: Hegemon

desc:
A Hegemony is a Title of the highest Tier.

The Holder of a Hegemony has De Jure rights to its constituent territory and can have Emperors as Vassals.
name: Hegemony

desc:
An Heir is a Character that stands to inherit one or more Titles.

Every held Title has an Heir, determined by the Succession Laws of its current Holder. When the current Holder of the Title dies, or otherwise triggers a Succession, the Title's current Heir will inherit it.

Note that Titles held by the same Ruler can have different Heirs. Most notably, the Primary Title is inherited by the Primary Heir and players will keep playing as their Player Heir.
name: Heir

desc:
Herd represents a Nomadic Ruler's people and flock of animals like horses, sheep, and goats.

It can be obtained through holding Counties with high County Fertility, Vassals, or Tributaries. Cultural Traditions, Dynasty Legacies, Legitimacy, and certain Nomadic Capital Yurt Buildings can offer bonuses to Herd gain.

A fraction of the Herd gets converted into Nomadic Horde when a ruler raises their Armies, and they can then be turned into Men-at-Arms at a reduced cost. Once these armies are disbanded, the remaining horde will convert back into herd.

Herd provides a small trickle of Gold, and can also be used as a currency for taking certain Decisions or increasing Migration acceptance.
name: Herd

desc:
Herder realms are removed from all aspects of rulership. They do not command Armies, own Buildings, create Alliances, or declare Wars. When Nomads Migrate a Holding, herders will slowly replenish the local County Fertility by virtue of their smaller flock.

They are intimidated by proper Nomad Rulers and will immediately surrender their land when challenged.
name: Herder

desc: A Herder Settlement is the smallest of the Holding Types. They represent the presence of Herders in the area, and provide bonuses to the County Fertility.
name: Herder Settlement

desc:
When the Fervor of a Faith is low, an outbreak of Heresy might occur. When that happens, a Ruler of the low-Fervor Faith will convert to another Faith, becoming a Heresiarch. They will then spread their new Faith to their Counties and Vassals.

If an outbreak is minor, it will stop there. If it is a major outbreak, more rulers in the same area will convert. If you're in that area, you also get the choice to convert, should you so desire.
name: Heresy

desc:
A Heritage is a Cultural Pillar that represents the common ancestry of several Cultures.

Cultures of the same Heritage generally have high Acceptance of one another.
name: Heritage

desc: In Crusader Kings III, this character is attracted to characters of the opposite gender.
name: Heterosexual

desc: High is the middle level of Dominance. At this level Migration can target De Jure Kingdom Titles within the The Great Steppe and the liege can Retract a Vassal's vassals.
name: High

desc:
High Crown Authority is the second to highest level. Vassals have a -20 Opinion penalty toward their Liege.

At this level — in addition to the powers the liege gets at Limited Crown Authority — vassals under the same liege can no longer wage war against each other, the ruler can change between all available Succession Laws, and vassals' Titles cannot be inherited by rulers outside the liege's Realm.

Lastly, refusing title Revocation or vassal Retraction is considered a Crime even if the liege lacks sufficient justification.
name: High Crown Authority

desc:
High Tribal Authority is the second-highest level of Tribal Authority. Vassals have a -20 Opinion penalty toward their Liege.

At this level, as well as the ability to Imprison Characters, the liege may Revoke Titles and Retract a vassal's vassals.
name: High Tribal Authority

desc:
Set out on a solitary expedition to take a break from the pressure of courtly existence.

Anticipated rewards:
•Opinion
•Stress Loss
•Fame
•May gain Mystic Trait or Trait Experience
name: Hike

desc: Hired Soldiers are either Mercenaries or Holy Orders.
name: Hired Soldiers

desc: A Hireling Contract typically involve hired muscle work such as guarding rulers, merchants, and bolstering garrisons.
name: Hireling Contract

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

In Hnefatafl:
• Intrigue counters Martial
• Martial counters Prowess
• Prowess counters Intrigue
name: Hnefatafl

desc:
An Activity where Vassals and Courtiers in a Realm gather at a Royal Court to petition their Liege and air their grievances.

Situations the Liege will be called to pass judgment upon can range from petty disputes and misunderstandings to realm-wide catastrophes. Most issues will have a solution that is beneficial – if not for the involved parties then at least for the liege.
name: Hold Court

desc:
A Title's Holder is the character who owns the title. Barony and County titles will always have Holders once settled, whereas Duchy, Kingdom and Empire titles might not have been created yet. As a further caveat, the Holder of a high-level Title might not actually control any territory within the Title's De Jure area.

Holding higher-tier Titles allows you to have higher-tier Vassals. For example, Dukes can have Counts as Vassals, and Kings can have Dukes.
name: Holder

desc:
A Holding is the central settlement of a Barony or County Capital.

It provides Taxes and Levies to its Holder, depending on its Holding Type. The collection of Holdings personally owned by a Ruler is called a Domain.
name: Holding

desc: There are four types of Holdings: Castles, Cities, Tribes, and Temples. Each type allows different types of Buildings. A Ruler's Government Form determines which types of Holding the Ruler can personally own without penalty. In the case of Temples, the Doctrines of their Faith may also play a role.
name: Holding Type

desc:
Holy Orders are independent military organizations that work to defend and expand the influence of their Faith.

Rulers of their Faith may hire them if they are at War with a … or … Faith, at a cost of Piety. Once this War ends, they no longer fight for that Ruler.

A Holy Order may have a Holy Order Patron, who does not need to pay to engage their services.
name: Holy Order

desc:
A Holy Order's Holy Order Patron is a King or Emperor who shares their Faith and whose Realm contains their Capital.

The Holy Order Patron may call upon the support of the Holy Order against religious enemies for free, instead of paying Piety.

Not all Holy Orders have a Holy Order Patron.
name: Holy Order Patron

desc: A Holy Site is a County which contains a place of religious significance to a Faith. Holy Sites held by a Character of the correct Faith will provide an effect to everyone of that Faith, and can also allow the creation of Special Buildings or Holy Orders. Each Faith has a different set of Holy Sites.
name: Holy Site

desc:
A Holy War is a special type of War waged by a Ruler of one Faith against a Ruler of a different Faith.

Holy War are usually quite destructive, with the winner of a Holy War typically seizing all Counties in the targeted area for themselves. However, if attacker's Faith is Pluralist or the defender has Vassals of the attacker's own Faith in the targeted area, some or all Vassal Rulers in the targeted area may simply be transfered to the attacker instead.

Unlike other wars, Rulers of the same Faith as the target may choose to join in their defense without the need of an Alliance.

Holy Wars may be allowed or restricted depending on the different Religious Families
name: Holy War

desc:
An Activity where Vassals can formally display their allegiance to their Liege.

Homage can be paid in a variety of ways, and can grant Opinion, Prestige, and Renown to both parties.
name: Homage

desc: A Ruler who is a Close Family Member of a Hostage and has sent them to a Warden as an assurance of peace or submission.
name: Home Court

desc: In Crusader Kings III, this character is attracted to characters of their own gender.
name: Homosexual

desc: A Feast can have an Honorary Guest, in whose honor the celebration is held. The central part of the banquet, the toast, will grant them Prestige due to this prominent position. But beware — it can also be a trap... Murder Feast hosts have a tendency for killing their Honorary Guest.
name: Honorary Guest

desc:
A Hook is a general term for a relationship between characters where one can get the other to do their will.

There are two types, Weak Hooks and Strong Hooks, which are acquired in different ways.

Hooks can be used to force through many interactions, for example Marriage proposals and Vassal Contract changes.
name: Hook

desc:
A Close Family Member of a Ruler, sent away from their Home Court as an assurance of peace or submission.

The reputation of Rulers who declare War despite sending or receiving a Hostage will be dramatically damaged, and Wardens may freely execute the Hostages of their enemies.

Well-treated Hostages are likely to become loyal to their Warden, who may gain a Hook, or even become Friends with them.

Hostages must be landless children, siblings, nieces, nephews, or grandchildren of their Home Court's Ruler.

Wardens have a chance to gain a Perpetual Hook on a child Hostage when they come of age, based on personality, opinion, and years spent at the Wardens court.
name: Hostage

desc: An Activity Phase during a Royal Tour in which a Vassal is expected to entertain their Liege, which often results in an increase in mutually forming Hooks and Special Relations.
name: Hosted Dinner

desc:
This Faith deviates significantly.
Intermarriage may still happen, Holy Wars can be waged.

Effects:
…
name: Hostile

desc:
A Hostile Army can be engaged just as if you were at War with the owner, though no War Score will be given.

Hostility is caused by you having conflicting interests, including:
•Enemies of your Liege
•Vassals of your enemies
•Rulers attacking the same enemy
name: Hostile

desc:
Hostile Schemes are Schemes that aim to cause harm to a Character. Most Hostile Schemes make use of Secrecy.

Examples of Hostile Schemes are:
•Murder
•Abduct
•Claim Throne
•Fabricate Hook
name: Hostile Scheme

desc:
Tensions flare and tempers fray in this Phase. Repeated acts of malice and escalated misunderstandings during the Opportunity Phase have lead to rising hatred of Characters with differing Cultures, Faiths, or worse: both.

Such bloodshed cannot persist forever, though. Eventually, either cooler heads or simple exhaustion bring the peninsula to the Compromise Phase.
name: Hostility Phase

desc:
A House is a branch of members on the bigger tree of a Dynasty. Houses are created by Rulers who no longer wish to answer to their current House Head and would rather be the Head of a new House.

Although Houses have their own names and Coats of Arms, they still share Renown, and other members of the Dynasty can still be your Player Heir.
name: House

desc:
House Arrest is a lenient form of Prison where Characters suffer from no ill effects except boredom. However, Rulers may throw them into the Dungeon, though it lowers the Opinions of the Prisoner's Close Family.

Captured Nobles are automatically put in House Arrest.
name: House Arrest

desc:
If you hold an Artifact for long enough, your whole House will get an Artifact Claim on it – a House Artifact Claim.

You can only act on a House Artifact Claim if the Artifact is not held by a member of your house.

When a Cadet Branch is formed, any existing House Claims on Artifacts held by the members of the new House are transferred to the new House.
name: House Artifact Claim

desc:
A House Aspiration represents the goals and methods of a Japanese House, and each provides different bonuses and opportunities.

The House Head can choose which Aspiration to pursue, and spend Prestige to further commit to it, gaining access to more powerful boons.
name: House Aspiration

desc:
In certain Governments, Houses can have a House Attribute which affects the members of the House.

The different House Attributes are:
•Powerful Family Attribute
•House Aspiration
•Mandala Aspect
name: House Attribute

desc:
A House Bloc is an defensive alliance of Houses within a Realm. Any Member House who is attacked will be defended by all other Member Houses.

House Heads decide whether to become Bloc Member Houses, with all ruling members of their House in the Realm following them.

Blocs always have a Leading House, whose House Head may expel other members, is the favored Ruling Regent of all members, and whose House Aspiration determines the bonuses granted by higher levels of Cohesion.

Only Leading House's House Head may create Factions against the Top Liege, and all Bloc Member Houses members will join all Factions they create.
name: House Bloc

desc:
Every House within a Dynasty has a House Head, who wields certain unique powers over the members of the House.

Notably, the House Head can legitimize Bastards, call the members of the House to War and demand conversion of Landed members. The House Head also gets a Weak Hook on all members of their House that are born while they are in power.

When they die, their Primary Heir becomes the new House Head.

Clan House Heads have special rules and privileges.
name: House Head

desc: Special Interactions that can be made by a House Head against members of their House.
name: House Head Interaction

desc:
When two Houses interact they may develop a positive or negative House Relation, which remains over the generations.

Beyond affecting the Opinion of all House members, each House Relation level may have extra effects, such as making Alliances and Wars easier or harder to effect.

The House Relation remains at the same level until the sum of all actions reach either +100% or -100%. Then, the House Relation is moved to the next level, either positive or negative.
name: House Relation

desc:
In Clan Realms the current House Unity Level dictates which Succession Law is used.

Clans can switch to a Single Realm Heir Succession Law, which will prevent House Unity from changing it, but doing so is much harder than normal.
name: House Succession Law

desc:
House Unity represents the state of internal relationships within a Clan House, and the attitude members have towards each other.

There are several House Unity Levels, which provides the members of a House with various benefits and penalties.

House Unity changes depending on the actions House members take towards one another. Unifying Actions will generally increase House Unity, while Divisive Actions will decrease it. The House Head generally have a greater degree of influence over their House's Unity.
name: House Unity

desc:
House Unity Level is the current state of House Unity. Active level changes as Unity increases through Unifying Actions or decreases through Divisive Actions, and each level provides the members of a House with various benefits and penalties.

There are five different levels:
…

Each level entails its own House Succession Law.
name: House Unity Level

desc:
The unpredictability of even gentle wild beasts, coupled with the frenzy of the chase, has undone many a mighty warrior.

More Perilous animals will grant greater Prestige to the hunter.

The remoteness of the wilderness and abundance of opportunity should also not be ignored when choosing guests...
name: Hunt Peril

desc:
A Hunt Sighting is a report of specific prestigious animals spotted in a County, which may be pursued in a Hunt held there.

Master of the Hunt Court Position will search for Sightings.
name: Hunt Sighting

desc:
When setting out on a Hunt there is no guarantee you will corner your quarry. The main factors are:
•Hunter Trait Experience
•Master of the Hunt Aptitude
•Buildings, Terrain, and Development
•Animal Sightings

Hunt Success Chance can never be higher than 80.

Successful hunts end with slaying the quarry, where trophy Artifacts may be gained and great Prestige conferred on the hunter.
name: Hunt Success Chance

desc: A Hunting Contract typically involves assisting the local ruler to cull wildlife and help bolster supplies.
name: Hunting Contract

desc: A Decision that allows a non-Involved Ruler to end the Iberian Struggle.
name: Iberian Foothold

desc:
This is a special type of War available to Involved Rulers of the Iberian Struggle.

The attacker aims to conquer a Duchy which contains any Involved Counties held by an Interloper or Uninvolved Ruler, or Vassalize them if they hold no land outside that Duchy.
name: Iberian Reclamation

desc: The Iberian Struggle depicts the centuries of fractious relationships on the Iberian Peninsula. Though born of the Umayyad Conquest of Iberia in the 8th Century, the Struggle shifts between Phases of hate-fueled violence, wary truces, and pragmatic cooperation. There are few permanent allies in such a situation, and Rulers should be wary of relying purely on a shared Faith or Culture.
name: Iberian Struggle

desc: Illnesses are a kind of negative Traits that lower a Character's Health. Illness Traits can last for varying amounts of time and differ greatly in lethality.
name: Illness

desc:
Imperial Bureaucracy represents an Administrative Realms level of centralization and the general power that the Ruler wields over their Vassals.

Only the Top Liege can change Imperial Bureaucracy. Administrative Vassals use the same level as their Liege.

There are four levels of Imperial Bureaucracy:
•Decentralized Realm
•Limited Administration
•Centralized Bureaucracy
•Absolute Autocracy

Increasing Imperial Bureaucracy costs an amount of Prestige depending on Realm Size and the ruler's Learning Skill.
name: Imperial Bureaucracy

desc:
The Imperial Censor is the Minister in charge of matters of intrigue and intelligence.

Beware of having a disloyal Censor, for they can easily conceal and participate in Schemes against you and your Close Family!

The Censor can be the designated Secretary Director, depending on the Grand Secretariat Control Law.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Find Secrets (Scheme) Interaction to find Secrets in Vassal Courts, which you can use to get a Gold Gold reward from your Liege or gain Hooks
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETDoing Blackmail will trigger 'Imperial Censor Blackmailed a Governor' Dynastic Cycle Catalyst
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
name: Imperial Censor

desc:
An extremely powerful Casus Belli usable by Co-Emperors in Duumvirates.

An Imperial Expedition may be launched against any Realm that either borders the Empire or holds lands that De Jure belong to the senior emperor.

It can (and generally will) target all Duchies that de facto border the Empire or De Jure belong to it.

Further, every Governor bordering the defender will be forcibly called to War as an Ally. Remote Governors with military Province Administrations may optionally join the conflict.

If the War is won, the Co-Emperor must decide between:
•Turning the conquered lands over to their senior emperor for Influence and Opinion
•Keeping the territories for themselves (costing Opinion)
•Handing over most of them whilst keeping the best Duchy (slightly reduced Influence and Opinion)
•Appointing local interim Governors who will be indebted to them

All rewards scale to the land taken: a large conquest earns significantly more Influence than a small border war.
name: Imperial Expedition

desc: The Imperial Family is the top House in an Administrative Realm.
name: Imperial Family

desc:
Imperial Grace represents the status bestowed onto a Tributary by Son of Heaven.

High Imperial Grace may result in special privileges being granted to the Tributary during Tribute Missions. At low levels of Imperial Grace, the Son of Heaven may exact tribute from you, and if it reaches zero it could mean the end of the relationship.
name: Imperial Grace

desc: The Imperial Policy is a Law set by the Top Liege of Japan that applies to all Vassals. Different policies may restrict or allow actions, or bestow Realm-wide effects.
name: Imperial Policy

desc: The Imperial Policy Faction seeks to change the Imperial Policy of the Realm, adopting a new Law selected by the faction leader.
name: Imperial Policy Faction

desc: Implicit Claims are Claims that are given to Eligible Children on all Titles held by their parents. If a parent loses a Title, the child's Implicit Claim will be removed too.
name: Implicit Claim

desc: A Imprisonment Reason gives a Liege the opportunity to freely Imprison a subject. They are most often gained from the subject being a Criminal.
name: Imprisonment Reason

desc:
The Children of two closely related Characters risk being born with a Congenital defect, the most serious of which is the Inbred Trait.

This is rare in the first generation, but successive Inbreeding increases the risk.

Generations of Inbreeding can, however, also result in the beneficial Pure-blooded Trait, which (if both parents share it) makes offspring immune to birth defects due to all flaws having been Bred out of the bloodline.
name: Inbreeding

desc:
Incest refers to sexual activity between close relatives.
What relations are incestuous is determined by the Consanguinity Doctrine of a character's Faith.
name: Incest

desc: There are many sources of Gold, but the two most important ones are Taxation of your own Holdings and of your Vassals.
name: Income

desc:
Increase Control in County is a Councillor Task performed by the Marshal.

It targets a County, where it increases Control, and removes County Corruption over time.
name: Increase Control in County

desc: A Councillor Task performed by the Steward. It targets a County, where it speeds up Development Growth and reduces the construction time for Buildings.
name: Increase Development in County

desc: The Independence Faction seeks independence for all its members. If successful, they will go Independent from their Liege.
name: Independence Faction

desc:
Independent Rulers have no Liege and thus enjoy greater freedom of action (e.g. in declaring Wars).

However, unlike Vassals they can also be directly attacked by foreign Rulers.
name: Independent Ruler

desc:
Baronies affected by Plagues have an Infection Rate that handles their severity and the strength of its effects.

The Infection Rate will always progress towards its maximum value if nothing is done to fight it. Minor, Major and Apocalyptic Plagues will progress at different velocities, marked by their intensity.

In order to mitigate the impact of the Infection, Rulers can improve the Plague Resistance of their Realm.
name: Infection Rate

desc:
Influence represents a Character's political reach and authority in a Realm that has the Administrative Government.

Influence is an essential tool and can be acquired in numerous ways. For example by becoming a Governor, upgrading an Estate, or being allied to the House Head of a Noble Family.

The main way to spend and make use of Influence is to acquire a Governorship, but is also a valuable resource to sway other Characters to do your bidding.

Every time a Character gains Influence, they also progress towards their next Level of Influence.
