name: Influence

desc: An Interaction where one can attempt to influence a Ward to pick up a Personality Trait akin to one's own.
name: Influence Ward's Personality

desc:
The Legitimacy a Character has when they become landed.

It is calculated based on Level of Splendor, relation to their predecessor, Court Grandeur, gender, Bastardy, years as a Ruler, the Legitimacy Dynasty Legacy, Diplomacy, Virtues, Sins and other special Traits, like Sayyid, Diplomat and Just.

Heirs will inherit … of the previous ruler's Legitimacy if inheriting a higher Tier Title.
name: Initial Legitimacy

desc:
Innovations are technologies and other advances that benefit all characters of a certain Culture. Innovations are grouped into the Eras when they can be discovered.

Through contact with neighboring Cultures, each Culture is always Spread to one specific Innovation which will be discovered much quicker.

In addition, the Culture Head can set another (or the same) Innovation as the Cultural Fascination for an additional boost.
name: Innovation

desc:
An activity where the Liege travel to a County in the Realm to oversee the local magnates and nobles.

They will have opportunities in one of the following focus areas: •Claims & Offer Vassalization Acceptance
•Taxes, Development, & Control
•Levies, Opinion, & Popular Opinion
name: Inspection

desc:
Success is not a given when undertaking an Inspection. The main factors affecting these odds are:
•Skills
•County Control
•Bordering Foreign Realm

Inspection Success Chance can never be higher than 95.
name: Inspection Success Chance

desc:
Inspired Characters are skilled artisans with a Project that could come true if you become their Sponsor.

You can use the Commission Artifact Decision to hire such a Character, in order ot create an Artifact.…

When their Project is complete, the Sponsor gets to keep the result, normally an Artifact.
name: Inspiration

desc: Allows you to wage a War in order to install a Supporter of Caliphal Authority of the Caliphate at the head of the targeted Realm
name: Install a Supporter

desc: A Councillor Task performed by the Chancellor, which accelerates the De Jure Drift process of a Title.
name: Integrate Title

desc: An Intent represents what a character personally seeks to accomplish at an Activity; the host and guests each have their own motives and ends.
name: Intent

desc:
Actions taken by one character towards another. They can have a wide range of purposes and effects.

Some interactions require the target character's approval, while some can be performed without it.

Usually they are accessed by right-clicking on a character to access the Interaction Menu for the target character, but sometimes they are available through special interfaces.
name: Interaction

desc:
When a Character is tangled up in a specific Struggle but not yet considered fully Involved, they're an Interloper.

Interlopers have their Capitals within the Struggle Region, but do not have both an Involved Faith and an Involved Culture.

Fully Involved Characters think of them as nosy, troublesome outlanders who don't understand where they're not wanted. Interloper Rulers thus generally take some penalties in Counties they hold inside a Struggle Region.
name: Interloper

desc:
Some Domicile Buildings can be improved with Internal Upgrades.

An Upgrade, while similar to other Domicile Buildings, may only be constructed within a specific building. Every building with access to Upgrades have their own unique set of Upgrades available.
name: Internal Upgrade

desc:
Characters who greatly fear another character are Intimidated by them. This is usually caused by Dread and/or a cowardly personality.

Intimidated characters are less likely to initiate hostile actions against the character they fear, including joining or starting Factions.

Characters who are even more fearful are marked as Terrified.
name: Intimidated

desc: A Tour Type in which you attempt to intimidate your Vassals, gaining Dread and forcing them out of Factions.
name: Intimidation Tour

desc: A Intrigue Contract typically involves assisting with matters ranging from reconnaissance to jailbreaks.
name: Intrigue Contract

desc: The Intrigue Lifestyle is suitable for Characters who want to succeed in Schemes, gain Dread, or Seduce others with ease.
name: Intrigue Lifestyle

desc:
Intrigue is a Skill representing a Character's ability to understand and manipulate other characters, and to organize elaborate plots.

It is mainly used to further — and defend against — Intrigue Schemes.

The corresponding Lifestyle is the Intrigue Lifestyle.
name: Intrigue Skill

desc:
Inventory Artifacts are Artifacts that a Character wears or carries with them, such as a weapon or a crown.

There is no limit to how many Artifacts a Character can have, but only those equipped in a slot of its type has any effect.

You can create new Inventory Artifacts from Inspired Characters, or from the Commission Artifact Decision.
name: Inventory Artifact

desc:
This is the maximum a character may invest in their own or anyone else's Candidate Score for a Governorship.

Age, Family Rating, Level of Influence, and Estate Buildings are the main factors that determine this limit. Children have a small scaling malus to this limit, while adult's limits rise as they age.
name: Investment Capacity

desc:
When a Character or a County is Involved, it means they're considered a natural and integral part of a Struggle by the people of a particular Struggle Region. They benefit fully from the fluid advantages of Phases, and are the primary activators of Catalysts.

Cultures and Faiths that are considered Involved are those that have or had significant presence in the Region.

To be Involved, a Character must have both their Culture and Faith be Involved and have their Capital within the Struggle Region.
name: Involved

desc: Some Cultures start already Involved in the Struggle. Others may become involved due to changing circumstances.
name: Involved Culture

desc: Some Faiths start already Involved in the Struggle. Others may become involved due to changing circumstances.
name: Involved Faith

desc:
The Iranian Intermezzo depicts the tumultuous decline of the Abbasid Caliphate, in which Mesopotamia was ravaged by rebellions and power struggles and several Persian rulers asserted their independence.

Though Involved Characters can have many agendas, most will want to either become a Supporter of Caliphal Authority and work towards restoring the power of the Caliphate, or a Detractor of the Caliphate and try to destroy it.

The Struggle shifts between two Phases - Unrest and Stabilization.
name: Iranian Intermezzo

desc:
Japanese Bureaucracy represents a Ritsuryō Government Realm's level of centralization and the general power that the Ruler wields over their Vassals.

Only the Top Liege can change Japanese Bureaucracy. Japanese Vassals use the same level as their Liege.

There are four levels of Japanese Bureaucracy:
•Autonomous Governors
•Limited Oversight
•Powerful Ministries
•Centralized Governance

Increasing Japanese Bureaucracy costs an amount of Prestige depending on Realm Size and the ruler's Learning Skill.
name: Japanese Bureaucracy

desc: The Ten'nō is the official Emperor of all Japan, though true power is generally in the hands of the Ruling Regent, who administers the state on their behalf.
name: Japanese Emperor

desc:
A Manor - or … - is a type of Domicile held by the House Head of notable Noble Families within Ritsuryō and Sōryō Realms. They represent private landholdings untied to any particular Landed Title.

Japanese Manor Building may be constructed here to expand the family's wealth and Influence, and the Manor will be inherited by future generations.
name: Japanese Manor

desc:
Japanese Manor Buildings are unique and persistent improvements to a Japanese Manor.

A large variety of structures are available for construction and may be built by the Manor's owner to generate private income, expand the family's Influence, and gain access to a number of Decisions, Interactions, and more.
name: Japanese Manor Building

desc: A Justicar Contract typically involve culling criminals while bringing justice and adhering to local law.
name: Justicar Contract

desc:
… is, de facto, the highest position in the Ritsuryō bureaucracy, exercising significant control over the organs of state in the Ten'nō's stead.

Though generally dominated by the … family, with enough Influence and Prestige, any family might rise to the occasion.
name: Kampaku

desc: A Decision that enables you to kindle a royal fire, gaining bonuses to Health and Renown.
name: Kindle Royal Fire Decision

desc:
A King is a Ruler whose Primary Title is a Kingdom.

Their Rank is directly above Dukes and directly below Emperors, and as such they can have Dukes and below as Vassals, and an Emperor or above as their Liege.
name: King

desc:
A Kingdom is a Title one Tier below a Empire and one above a Duchy.

The Holder of a Kingdom has De Jure rights to its constituent territory.

Kingdoms may be dormant and have no current Holder. Such Titles can be created by a Ruler who controls at least half of the Counties within.
name: Kingdom

desc:
A Kinslayer is a Character who is known to have slain a Family Member. Some Faiths view kinslaying as Criminal.

The three Kinslaying traits are:
•Kinslayer — Given to those who kill Close Family
•Familial Kinslayer — Given to those who kill Extended Family
•Dynastic Kinslayer — Given to those who kill a member of their Dynasty
name: Kinslaying

desc:
A Knight is a Vassal, Courtier, or Follower that fights directly in your Army.

During Battles, Knights use their Prowess Skill to fight more effectively. A high Prowess means that they will be able to inflict more damage on the enemy, and are more likely to survive or even emerge from Battle unscathed.

……Knights can be known by different names depending on … or …. For example, Champions, Fāris or Baghaturs.

Knights represent both the character and their retinue of troops.
name: Knight

desc:
An effect applied to any Army which contains the pertinent Acclaimed Knight.

The Knight need not be their Army's Commander for their Knight Army Modifier to apply.
name: Knight Army Modifier

desc:
A Ruler's Knight Effectiveness determines how well their Knights fight in Battle.

At 100%, Knights fight as normal, but at 200% they fight as if their Prowess was doubled.
name: Knight Effectiveness

desc:
The winner of a Knock-Out Contest is the last one remaining after three Contest Rounds between Qualifying Contestants.

Knock-Out Contests:
•Wrestling
•Duel
•Joust
•Board Games
name: Knock-Out

desc:
The Kurultai replaces the Council for the Nomadic Government. The Kurultai members are among the elite of the realm, and should either be appeased or forced into Obedience to assure a smooth Succession.

After the event of a chaotic succession, they may steal some Herd, abandon their new Liege, they will gain a Claim on the Realm Title.
name: Kurultai

desc: A Landed Character is a Ruler who owns Holdings. Except in Theocracies and Republics, Commoners automatically become Nobles when they are landed, founding a new Dynasty.
name: Landed

desc:
A Language is the Cultural Pillar that determines what language the general populace of a Culture speaks. Cultures which speak the same language gain a permanent bonus to their Cultural Acceptance Baseline.

A Character can know one or more Languages. Knowing a language cuts the Cultural Acceptance Opinion penalty in half towards Characters and Counties that speak it. It also discourages Independence and Claimant Factions.

Characters can learn additional languages by using the Learn Language Scheme. Characters can comfortably learn languages up to their Foreign Language Limit.
name: Language

desc:
A Realm's Laws are what determine how that Realm is structured.

The most fundamental of these is the Realm's Crown Authority (or Tribal Authority for Tribes, Imperial Bureaucracy for Administrative and Dominance for Nomads), as those Laws determine how Lieges and Vassals interact on a regular basis.

Though less impactful on the day-to-day life of Rulers in a Realm, Succession Laws and Title Laws are still very important to consider for Succession.
name: Law

desc: A Leading House is a House that is the agreed leader of a House Bloc.
name: Leading House

desc: A Learning Contract typically involves copying texts or facilitating actions of solidarity.
name: Learning Contract

desc: The Learning Lifestyle is suitable for Characters who want to live long and healthy lives, gain Piety, or gain additional bonuses from their Faith.
name: Learning Lifestyle

desc:
Learning is a Skill measuring a Character's literacy and wisdom. The Learning Skill of a Ruler affects the cost of increasing Crown Authority, and also yields an amount of monthly Piety.

Characters with high Learning can be expected to have extensive knowledge of all common scholarly endeavors, including theology, philosophy, language and mathematics.

The corresponding Lifestyle is the Learning Lifestyle.
name: Learning Skill

desc:
Minor Baronies can be Leased out to Holy Orders or Clergy. Leased baronies provide Taxes and Levies to the Lessee rather than the Holder.

A holy order can lease Castle Holdings, while clergy can lease Temple Holdings.

Leased Holdings are still considered part of the holder's Realm. County Capitals cannot be leased.
name: Leasing

desc: A Tenet emphasizing legal practice and tradition in theology and devoutness. It affects law costs and Vassal Faction membership based on the number of Sins or Virtues a Ruler has.
name: Legalism

desc:
A Legend represents the important deeds that a Character achieved in life, and are created from Legend Seeds.

Legends are powerful ways to obtain Legitimacy, and other possible rewards like Skill increases, Opinion bonuses, Renown, Prestige or Piety. Baronies in which a Legend has spread may also receive additional effects, if held by the Legend owner or a Legend Promoter.

Legends have a Legend Type that governs those rewards: they can be Legitimizing, Holy or Heroic. Each Legend also has a Legend Quality level, which influences the strength of those rewards, as well as its spread.
name: Legend

desc:
The Legend Library holds completed Legends that have spread to your Domain, you created, or were actively promoting.
You can also actively add completed Legends if you are traveling through the spread area of the legend.

You can remove Legends from your library at will.
name: Legend Library

desc:
A Legend Promoter is a Ruler that supports another ruler's Legend.

A Legend Promoter gets extra bonuses that vary depending on the Legend Type and Legend Quality of the Legend in exchange for a monthly Gold contribution.
name: Legend Promoter

desc:
The Legend Protagonist is the main character of a Legend, whose the deeds are therein described. The owner of a Legend can also be its Legend Protagonist, but so can any member of their family — dead or alive, as long as they are 16 years old.

Legend Protagonists get no direct extra bonuses themselves, but the content about the Legend will be focused on them. They will, however, grant additional Legitimacy to the Legend Owner, based on how many Virtuous Traits they hold.

The Legend Protagonist must be an adult, for stating that an infant killed a dragon might be controversial.
name: Legend Protagonist

desc:
The Quality of a Legend marks both the strength of its effects and the reach of its spread, as well as affecting its final rewards. Legends can be Famed, Illustrious or Mythical — for there is no such thing as a common Legend.

The Quality can be increased by spreading the Legend to more Baronies and paying an upgrade cost.

When the owner of a Legend dies, their family can continue it, with no damage to its Quality.
name: Legend Quality

desc:
A Legend in the making. Legend Seeds are the basis of a Legend and, by founding them, a Ruler may start a Legend.

Legend Seeds can be earned by fulfilling some criteria like being the heir of Charlemagne or by performing legendary deeds: Major Decisions, winning a Great Holy War, becoming a King or Emperor, organizing a Grand Activity, hunting a legendary animal, et cetera.

Inactive Legend Seeds have no cost, but bear no effects. Founding a Legend Seed for the first time has a Gold cost to it.
name: Legend Seed

desc:
A Legend has a Type that influences the category of the effects it will grant, as well as the theme of its content.

The Legend Types are Legitimizing, Heroic and Holy, granting Legitimacy, Prestige and Piety, correspondingly.
name: Legend Type

desc:
Legitimacy is the representation of the right to reign of a Ruler. Vassals also generate Legitimacy Expectations that the Liege is supposed to meet.

Only Rulers have Legitimacy, which is calculated at the moment they become rulers and results in their Initial Legitimacy. A fraction of the Legitimacy of the previous ruler is also inherited by their Heir.

Legitimacy affects many of the game systems, making Marriage proposals, Vassalization and Alliances more likely to be accepted, and Claims cheaper, as well as swinging the Scales of Power in a Regency.

Legitimacy typically has 5 Legitimacy Levels and one Illegitimate bottom level.……
name: Legitimacy

desc:
Legitimacy Levels can be gained through various means: winning Wars, releasing Valuable Prisoners, creating Legends, holding Court, or attending Activities.

They can, however, also be lost: Plagues ravaging the Capital, losing wars (especially Faction wars), losing Titles, or an exposed Hostile Scheme are some of the main ways for Legitimacy to decrease.…
name: Legitimacy Level

desc: Children born of Married parents are considered Legitimate, as opposed to Bastards who may not inherit any Titles. The children of Concubines are also considered Legitimate, though of slightly lower status.
name: Legitimate

desc:
A Bastard may be Legitimized, either at birth, or as a Character Interaction later, depending on approval from their House Head.

A Legitimized Bastard has the same right of inheritance as Legitimate children, but the stain of bastardy will follow them throughout their life.
name: Legitimized Bastard

desc:
A Character's Level of Devotion is a measure of how virtuous and devout they are, as well as their standing with other members of their Faith.

Every time a Character gains Piety, they also progress toward the next Level of Devotion.

…

The Levels are:
•Sinner
•Dutiful
•Faithful
•Devoted Servant
•Paragon of Virtue
•Religious Icon…
name: Level of Devotion

desc: Level of Devotion Impact increases or decreases the Modifiers gained from your current Level of Devotion.
name: Level of Devotion Impact

desc:
A Character's Level of Fame measures their general reputation, and how well perceived they are by everyone.

Each time a Character gains Prestige, they also progress towards the next Level of Fame.

The Levels are:
•Disgraced
•Established
•Distinguished
•Illustrious
•Exalted Among Men
•Legendary Figure
name: Level of Fame

desc: Level of Fame Impact increases or decreases the Modifiers gained from your current Level of Fame.
name: Level of Fame Impact

desc:
A Character's Level of Influence measures their overall political power and reach.

Each time a Character gains Influence, they also gain progress towards the next Level of Influence.

The Levels are:
•Impotent
•Influential
•Persuasive
•Controlling
•Authoritative
•Imperious
name: Level of Influence

desc: Level of Influence Impact increases or decreases the Modifiers gained from your current Level of Influence.
name: Level of Influence Impact

desc:
Level of Splendor is a measure of how famous a Dynasty is. Level progress is made whenever your Dynasty gains Renown. Characters get an amount of initial Prestige when they are born depending on their Level of Splendor. Similarly, Spouses gain some Prestige from each other's Dynasty when they Marry.

The levels are:
•Base Origins
•Obscure
•Insignificant
•Noteworthy
•Reputable
•Well-known
•Significant
•Famous
•Glorious
•Fabled
•Legendary
name: Level of Splendor

desc:
The bulk of most Armies is made up of Levies.

Each Holding provides a set number of Levies to their Holder. Vassals in turn provide a part of their Levies to their Liege.

Levies are made up of mostly poorly-armed fighters (peasant militias, ruffians, local sellswords, destitute nobles, minor landowners, etc.) and are considered their own unit type.

A Levy has … Damage and … Toughness. The other type of Soldiers in the game are Men-at-Arms — expensive trained professionals.
name: Levies

desc: The Liberty Faction seeks to lower the Crown Authority and, if applicable, their own Vassal Contracts. If successful, their Liege will be unable to change the Crown Authority of the Realm for some time.
name: Liberty Faction

desc: A Liege is a Ruler with at least one Vassal. Lieges may themselves be Vassals to even higher ranked Rulers, and so on.
name: Liege

desc:
Your Liege Taxes are the Taxes that you must pay to your Liege as part of your Obligations. You do not pay any Liege Taxes if you are Independent.

From your Liege's point of view, these same taxes are instead called Vassal Taxes to distinguish them from any taxes they may owe to their own Liege.
name: Liege Taxes

desc:
Life Expectancy is the number of years a character is expected to live before dying of natural causes.

A high Life Expectancy will make characters visibly age slower and be able to produce Children for longer.
name: Life Expectancy

desc:
Adult Rulers may choose a Lifestyle, which will in turn allow them to select a Focus and start gaining Perks.

Each Lifestyle has its own type of Experience, which is used to purchase Perks. For example, Experience in the Intrigue Lifestyle is necessary to gain Perks such as Dreadful or Like Weeds in a Garden.

The Lifestyles are:
• Diplomacy Lifestyle
• Stewardship Lifestyle
• Martial Lifestyle
• Intrigue Lifestyle
• Learning Lifestyle
• Wandering Lifestyle
name: Lifestyle

desc:
Lifestyle Experience is accumulated passively by having a Focus selected, or granted by events. There are different types of Lifestyle Experience, one per Lifestyle category.

Gaining enough Lifestyle Experience within a category will award a Perk.
name: Lifestyle Experience

desc:
A Lifestyle Trait is the result from picking certain Lifestyle perks, Decisions, or Interactions.

Some Lifestyle traits are upgradeable as the character improves their mastery of the skill. The levels range between 1-3, and the stars on the trait icon indicate the current level.
name: Lifestyle Trait

desc:
Light Cavalry are mounted Men-at-Arms who excel at scouting and pursuing the enemy.

While each kind of Light Cavalry is unique, they generally Counter Archers, and are in turn Countered by Spearmen.

Light Cavalry are also often strong on flat Terrain.

In comparison with Heavy Cavalry, they are usually better at Pursuit and Screen.
name: Light Cavalry

desc:
When fighting a Single Combat, your Likelihood of Success is how well you are doing in the Duel. To win, you must get your Likelihood of Success far above your opponent's.

As rounds go on, it becomes easier to win, meaning you need less lead over your opponent.

The counterpart to Likelihood of Success is Risk of Injury.
name: Likelihood of Success

desc:
Limited is the second-lowest level of Dominance. Migration can target De Jure Duchy Titles within the The Great Steppe, Titles can be revoked and the liege may now Imprison Characters in their Realm.

Can use the Forsake Nomadism Decision
name: Limited

desc: 'Limited Crown Authority' is the second to lowest level of Crown Authority. Vassals have a -10 Opinion penalty toward their Liege, and the liege may Revoke Titles and Retract a vassal's vassals. The Ruler can change between available Partition Succession Laws.
name: Limited Crown Authority

desc: Limited Tribal Authority is the second-lowest level of Tribal Authority. Vassals have a -10 Opinion penalty towards their Liege, and the liege may now Imprison Characters in their Realm.
name: Limited Tribal Authority

desc: The Line of Succession is the order in which certain characters stand to inherit certain Titles, determined by the Succession Law.
name: Line of Succession

desc: A Decision that lets a character improve a County in their current location.
name: Local Arbitration

desc:
You may choose how you explore the Grand Tournament while the Contests are being prepared.

Each Locale offers opportunities to socialize with guests, improve Progress to Victory, or sabotage Contestants.

If a Locale is not selected, you will visit one at random after a short period of time.
name: Locales

desc: Every Character has a location indicating where they currently are in the world. To get from one location to another, you must Travel.
name: Location

desc: Long Hike is an Activity Option for the Hike Activity. The character will spend a significantly longer time with the activity, and will be given more opportunities.
name: Long Hike

desc:
'Long Reign' is an increasing Opinion bonus that all characters in a Realm get with a Liege who has ruled over them for a long time.

Similarly, subjects have a decaying Short Reign Opinion penalty with new Lieges.
name: Long Reign

desc:
If a Holding is Raided, Occupied in a Siege, or engaged in Bartering, the attacker or Barterer will get an amount of Gold equal to the Loot. The more prosperous a Holding is, the more Loot it will have.

A Holding which has been Raided, Sieged, or Bartered with recently will not have any Loot.
name: Loot

desc:
A Lover is a Special Relation indicating an ongoing amorous and sexual association between two Characters.

As they often take place outside the bonds of Marriage or Concubinage, most Lover Special Relations begin as Secrets.

If a man and a woman are Lovers, the woman may become pregnant with the man's child. If they are not Married (and one is not the Concubine of the other), the child will be a Bastard, secret or otherwise.

Lovers who are deeply loyal and affectionate might become Soulmates.
name: Lover

desc:
A Diarch's Loyalty decides how likely it is they will abuse their powers, at their Liege's or the Realm's expense.

Selfless Diarchs refrain from using Borrowed Powers, try to fulfil the Mandate set for them dutifully, and give up their power willingly when asked.

Self-Interested Diarchs use Borrowed Powers liberally, try to fulfil their Mandate in order to swing the Scales of Power in their direction, and may refuse to give up power if the Scales are swung heavily enough towards them.

Situational Diarchs might use Borrowed Powers, will generally either split Mandate benefits with their Liege or ignore their Mandate entirely, and might need bribing to give up their office if the Scales of Power suit them.
name: Loyalty

desc:
The Magnificence of a Coronation determines the outcome of the Activity; a higher Magnificence score leads to a better outcome for the Host.

Magnificence can be gained through Intents, Activity Options, and events in the activity. Supporters and Detractors may affect the value as well.
name: Magnificence

desc:
In the Main Phase of a Battle, Soldiers and Knights from the two sides fight each other.

The Main Phase ends when all troops of one side have become Casualties or one side has decided to Retreat.

After the Main Phase the combat enters the Aftermath.
name: Main Phase

desc: A Tour Type in which you attempt to sway your Vassals by increasing their Opinion.
name: Majesty Tour

desc:
Increase Control in County is a Councillor Task performed by the Marshal.

It increases Knight Effectiveness and lowers Hostile Scheme Success Chance against the councillor's Liege.
name: Manage Royal Guards

desc:
Under the Mandala Government Form, the Domain Limit and amount of Direct Vassals are limited. Instead the Liege and Suzerain are reliant on Tributaries for expanding their realm. 

A Mandala Ruler can aspire to be seen as a God King, or Devaraja, and then relies on Mandala Radiance to acquire and keep Tributaries.

A Ruler must maintain Opinion and grow relations with their Tributaries to keep them long-term. On succession Tributaries may scatter unless the Ruler is a worthy Devaraja Successor.
name: Mandala

desc:
In order for a Mandala Ruler to achieve ever-lasting reverence and divinity, they need to align with one of the Aspects that identify them as a god.

The available Aspects are: 
•Aspect of Creation
•Aspect of Serenity
•Aspect of Destruction
•Aspect of Trickery

These Aspects will impact certain expectations and actions undertaken by the Ruler.
name: Mandala Aspect

desc:
The Mandala Decrees are the three Decrees mandated by the Mandala Ruler — signified by Prosperity, Expansion and Reverence.

Generally the Mandala realm has a very centralized authority, where the power over Subjects and Laws lies with the associated Ruler who can change them as required with little to no objection from its denizens.
name: Mandala Decree

desc:
The magnetism to attract and maintain Subjects for a Mandala Ruler is referred to as Mandala Radiance. It is a blend of their Level of Devotion, Ornate Temple Great Building level as well as Mandala Aspect level.

Higher rewards, more Subjects and more power await those who combine the three to become more Radiant.
name: Mandala Radiance

desc:
Mandala Rituals are tasks that appear occasionally for Mandala Rulers — it is a sign that a particular part of your Realm is in need of your guidance and divine uplifting.

Being more skilled in your Mandala Aspect will increase any gains from making appearances for your Subjects.
name: Mandala Ritual

desc: The Ritual Tier of a Mandala Ritual indicates just how much that destination would benefit from your admonition as well as the rewards for you, personally.
name: Mandala Ritual Tier

desc:
When a Mandala Ruler passes on, and has chosen a Mandala Aspect, their Heir faces the Mandala Succession Trials. In these Trials, the Heir is subject to Skill Challenges which test their mettle in the associated Aspect Skill but also two other Aspect Skills.

Succeeding these trials means the Heir managed to convince their followers that they are a worthy successor and the Realm remains stable.

Failing however, will incur increasing penalties:

•1 Failed Challenge: Losing a Level of Devotion and a small amount of Tributaries break free.

•2 Failed Challenges: Losing two Level(s) of Devotion and all Tributaries break free.

•All Failed Challenges: Losing three Level(s) of Devotion and the shattering of the Realm.
name: Mandala Succession

desc:
Mandates are useful tasks a Liege can set for their Diarch when Sharing Power.

Similarly to Councillor Tasks, the Liege selects a Mandate and then slowly receives benefits from it.

When a Diarch does their job well, they both swing the Scales of Power towards themselves and generate Strife with their fellow Vassals.

How much benefit the Liege receives depends on their Diarch's Diarch Aptitude and Loyalty.
name: Mandate

desc:
The Mandate of Heaven is a special type of Legitimacy only available to Son of Heaven. It represents the monarch's right to rule, and who is considered the supreme ruler under all of heaven.

The Mandate is closely connected to the Dynastic Cycle. The Cycle affect how the reigning monarch gains Legitimacy and may also change Dynastic Cycle Era based on the monarch's level of Mandate.
name: Mandate of Heaven

desc: The Maneuver phase occurs at the start of a Battle and indicates the time it takes before the Main Phase begins, and Armies engage each other in combat.
name: Maneuver

desc: Manipulation is a form of Hook where you have managed to manipulate the mind of another character in some way in order to get them to do your will.
name: Manipulation

desc: Adventurers and Nomads may recruit Men-at-Arms, but they do not reinforce automatically as Landed Ruler's do. Instead, recruits must be enticed using interactions.
name: Manually Reinforce

desc:
Marriages are a union between two Spouses, and are (alongside Betrothals) the main way to forge an Alliance with another Ruler.

Spouses may also produce Legitimate children, who can be Bred and raised as suitable Heirs.

Marriages only end when one Spouse dies or Divorces the other.…
name: Marriage

desc: The Marshal is your chief Commander and the Councillor in charge of military matters in general.
name: Marshal

desc:
Martial Custom is the Cultural Pillar that determines what genders can act as Commanders or Knights.

Some Traditions and Doctrines can modify these rules for certain Characters.
name: Martial Custom

desc: The Martial Lifestyle is suitable for Characters who want to improve their Men-at-Arms and Knights, boost Control in their Domain, or increase their chances to win Wars.
name: Martial Lifestyle

desc:
Martial Skill indicates how good a Character is at waging War and leading Armies in Battle.

A high Martial Skill is important for Army Commanders, since it improves their Advantage in Battle.

The corresponding Lifestyle is the Martial Lifestyle.
name: Martial Skill

desc: The Master Assassin is a Court Position enabled by Faiths with the Fedayeen Tenet. The Master Assassin is a dangerous fanatic who works together with lesser assassins to slay perceived enemies of the faith.
name: Master Assassin

desc:
A Decision unlocked from the Wandering Lifestyle tree, where you can choose a Terrain to specialize in, based on the group one chose in Designated Terrain.

This decision will give significant boons for the terrain chosen, giving bonuses such as increased Advantage, improved Battle Roll, reducing Attrition, and increased Prestige and Fame from Battle.
name: Master Terrain

desc:
A board game consists of two players trying their luck and skill against one another in a game of wits and chance. They may be played as friendly matches, or with a wager of some kind.

There are many different Board Game Types, though the ways to Win and play each remain the same. Only the skills used differ.
name: Match

desc: In a Matrilineal Marriage, children will be born into their mother's House instead of their father's.
name: Matrilineal

desc: The Maximum Level of Devotion represents the highest Level of Devotion that a Ruler may achieve in their lifetime. By default, this level is Religious Icon.…
name: Maximum Level of Devotion

desc:
When a character becomes Ill or Wounded a Medical Treatment can help them recover faster.

The one responsible for treating you and your Courtiers is the Personal Physician. Try to always have one employed if you can afford their salary.

The more treatments a Personal Physician performs, the more their skill will grow, granting them Physician Traits.
name: Medical Treatments

desc:
Men-at-Arms are professional Soldiers superior to Levies.

The player has direct control over the composition and size of their Men-at-Arms Regiments.

Different types of Men-at-Arms are good or bad in different types of Terrain. Each type also Counters another type.

Men-at-Arms can be Stationed in Holdings to increase their effectiveness.
name: Men-at-Arms

desc:
Most Men-at-Arms are able to Counter another type of Men-at-Arms.

When a Regiment is Countered, its effectiveness during a Battle is decreased. The more a Regiment is outnumbered by its Counter, the higher the penalty.
name: Men-at-Arms Counter

desc:
When Stress overwhelms a character they will experience a Mental Break — a personal crisis in which they feel that they must do something to lower their Stress, no matter the cost.

Characters suffering from a Mental Break will have several ways that they can deal with the situation, though many of them will have negative consequences.

At low Stress Levels these consequences are minor and easily managed. As Stress Level increases however, so do these consequences, eventually leading to insanity and even death.
name: Mental Break

desc: Mentors are Characters that help to improve the Skills of their Student. They can be gained through events when your Lifestyle Focus is set to a particular Skill.
name: Mentor

desc:
Mercenaries are Soldiers for hire who fight in exchange for Gold. Mercenary Armies come in various sizes, with different types of Men-at-Arms and a number of Knights.

Mercenaries sign up for … month contracts that can be extended for another … months if you are still at War. Mercenary contracts persist even if their Regiments are dismissed — they can be raised again without further cost.

You are allowed to go into Debt in order to hire Mercenaries (up to … months).
name: Mercenary Company

desc: Establishing a Mercenary Contract incurs a one-time cost which allows the use of their troops for … months.
name: Mercenary Contract

desc: A Mercenary Contract involves aiding a Character in either an on-going War, or else one they intend to start with your help. Pay is awarded based on War Contribution, as well as the actual result.
name: Mercenary Contract

desc:
A Character's Merit tracks their progress to the next Merit Rank. All characters with an Elder or Disciples produce a passive Merit gain.

Governors can increase their Merit by constructing Buildings in their assigned Holdings, going on an Inspection Activity, participating in a Debate and attending Examinations.

Available Administration Types governors increase their monthly merit gain by paying more Taxes to their Liege, while Available Administration Types governors increase it by creating Men-at-Arms.

Non-Governors can attempt to increase it by attending Examinations.
name: Merit

desc:
A Character's Merit Rank indicates how appropriate they are as a Governor in East Asian Administrative Governments.

It represents their documented achievements and moral conduct according to Confucian ideals through the amount of Merit they have gained.

An official with a high Merit Rank has a higher Candidate Score and Governor Salary.

The Ranks are:
•No Rank
•9th Rank
•8th Rank
•7th Rank
•6th Rank
•5th Rank
•4th Rank
•3rd Rank
•2nd Rank
•1st Rank
name: Merit Rank

desc:
Meritocratic is a Bureaucratic Government Form similar to Celestial, in which the Liege appoints characters as Governors, of which there are two types, Civil and Military.

Characters have access to Influence, Noble Families, and Family Estates.

Independent Rulers have Legitimacy, while Vassals focus on obtaining Merit.
name: Meritocratic

desc:
Meritocratic Bureaucracy represents a Meritocratic Realm's level of centralization and the general power that the Ruler wields over their Vassals.

Only the Top Liege can change Meritocratic Bureaucracy. Meritocratic Vassals use the same level as their Liege.

There are four levels of Meritocratic Bureaucracy:
•Autonomous Provinces
•Limited Civil Service
•Centralized Ministries
•Divine Mandate

Increasing Meritocratic Bureaucracy costs an amount of Prestige depending on Realm Size and the ruler's Learning Skill.
name: Meritocratic Bureaucracy

desc:
Meritocratic Khanate is a Bureaucratic Government Form similar to the Celestial and Meritocratic, but originating from a Nomadic Government Form. The Liege appoints characters as Governors, of which there are two types, Civil and Military. They still maintain Tributaries, enforce Obedience, and have a higher maximum Dread.

Characters have access to Influence, Noble Families, and Family Estates.

Independent Rulers have Legitimacy, while Vassals focus on obtaining Merit.
name: Meritocratic Khanate

desc:
The third level Civil Service Examinations. Held by the Celestial Government through the Capital Examination Activity.

When passed:
….
name: Metropolitan Examination

desc:
A powerful Casus Belli that may only be used once per campaign, total, to conquer all territories held by the target within Pannonia.

On victory, all Mogyërs in the attacker's Realm will move with them to Pannonia, Counties and Vassals, displacing Avar Counties. Other vassals outside of Pannonia are abandoned, while Counties formerly occupied or held by Mogyërs are left to local petty warlords and rival steppe tribes.
name: Migrate to Pannonia Casus Belli

desc:
Migration is essential to Nomads. When the County Fertility in their Realms is low they will often move in search of greener pastures.

Migration can only target De Jure Titles and the accessible Tiers are limited by a Ruler's Dominance.

A proposal will be sent to the Nomad with the biggest Herd in the desired area, and they can decide whether to leave their lands willingly, or to go to war to defend them.

Herders will always leave their lands, as they do not have the means to defend themselves.
name: Migration

desc:
This is a special type of Interaction available to Involved Rulers of the Iberian Struggle, allowing them to join other Involved Ruler's Wars in exchange for Gold.

Payment is made on conclusion of the War, whatever the outcome, as long as the contractor made a War Contribution of at least 100.
name: Military Assistance

desc: Treasury sent to military Province Vassals from the central government, for the purposes of funding additional military activities. It is based on the periodically calculated allocation of the Treasury income of the Top Liege.
name: Military Budget

desc: Military Buildings are Buildings whose primary function is to increase the number of Levies they provide to their Holder.
name: Military Building

desc: Rulers who pursue a Military Career Path focus on martial skills over administrative tasks. They are appointed to Military Circuits and their Merit will grow based on their ability to recruit and maintain Title Men-at-Arms.
name: Military Career Path

desc:
A Military Governor is a Governor with military Vassal Obligations. They are able to field Title Men-at-Arms, unlike Civilian Governors, and will use them to protect the Realm from foreign incursions and support other Governors in need of military aid.

Characters who pursue a Military Career Path can become Military Governors.
name: Military Governor

desc:
Ministers are a type of Councillors serving on the Council, or Ministry, of Son of Heaven.

Each minister has a number of responsibilities, such as funding Great Projects and helping Governors in different ways.
name: Minister

desc:
The Minister of Justice is the Minister in charge of legal affairs and assisting Son of Heaven to maintain a righteous rule.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Establish Control Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Imprison Interaction on Vassals and Courtiers, who cannot refuse
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Grant Pardon Interaction on Characters who have committed Crimes
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Find Secrets (Scheme) Interaction to find Secrets in Vassal Courts and Imprison or pardon known Criminals
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETExposing Secrets will trigger Minister of Justice exposed a Governor Dynastic Cycle Catalyst
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
name: Minister of Justice

desc:
The Minister of Personnel is the Minister in charge of all matters related to Appointments and can greatly impact the Candidate Score of other Characters.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Request Retirement Interaction to fire Governors regardless of the Retirement Age Law
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETInvite any type of Courtier with the Summon Courtiers for the Celestial Bureau Decision
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETCompel acceptance of the Offer Courtier and Demand Courtier Interactions
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options, and at a reduced cost
name: Minister of Personnel

desc:
The Minister of Revenue is the Minister in charge of Taxation and aids Son of Heaven with the Treasury.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAid Vassals who can Request Treasury Funds
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse the Suggest Treasury Audit Decision
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Conduct Census Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Debt Relief Interaction to pay Treasury Debt of Civilian Governors triggering 'Minister or Son of Heaven cleared Treasury Debt' Dynastic Cycle Catalyst
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
name: Minister of Revenue

desc:
The Minister of Rites is the Minister in charge of religious and spiritual affairs, and can assist Governors in hosting Examinations.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Assimilate Area Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Compel Religious Uniformity Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAid Vassals in hosting Examinations
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETCompel Conversion on Characters of Hostile or Evil Faiths
name: Minister of Rites

desc:
The Minister of War is the Minister in charge of the administration and management of troops. When subject Governors are in need of military aid, it is the Minister of War who can send Military Governors to help.

The minister is not an active Commander and does not lead troops. That is the purview of the Grand Marshal.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETSend aid to Vassals at War who can Request Military Aid
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETOrder Military Governors to join the Wars of other Governors
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Military Operation Exercise Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETUse Debt Relief Interaction to pay Treasury Debt of Military Governors triggering 'Minister or Son of Heaven cleared Treasury Debt' Dynastic Cycle Catalyst
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
name: Minister of War

desc:
The Minister of Works is the Minister in charge of construction and development throughout the Realm, and may start Great Projects.

The minister can, for example:
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Develop Communities Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the The Grand Canals Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETStart the Improve the Great Wall Great Project
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETCan construct Buildings and Holdings inside the Realm
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETCan construct Buildings and Holdings inside Tributaries of Son of Heaven in … Era
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAccess special Influence Career Interaction options
name: Minister of Works

desc:
The Ministry is a type of Council only available to Son of Heaven.

There are nine Ministers, each one representing the highest level of government and is the head of their own department. These are sorted into a hierarchy, allowing a Minister of a lower rank to be promoted to a position of higher rank, based on the Prominence of the Title.

The Ministers are:
•Grand Chancellor
•Imperial Censor
•Grand Marshal
•Minister of Personnel
•Minister of War
•Minister of Revenue
•Minister of Justice
•Minister of Rites
•Minister of Works
name: Ministry

desc: Treasury sent to Vassals from the central government, for the purposes of funding Ministries. It is based on the periodically calculated allocation of the Treasury income of the Top Liege.
name: Ministry Budget

desc:
Ministry Obligations is a unique set of Vassal Obligations only available for Ministers.

All civil ministers have a specific option set as their default, while the Grand Marshal has a unique option that provides the Marshal with Title Men-at-Arms.

These obligations cannot be changed.
name: Ministry Obligations

desc:
While it's not possible to prevent Clouded Eyes from progressing, you can slow it down by:
•Avoiding Travel
•Avoiding locations with Desert or Desert Mountains Terrain
•Avoiding locations with Normal Winter or Harsh Winter
name: Mitigate Clouded Eyes

desc:
While it's not possible to prevent Fragile Bones from progressing, you can prevent large Trait Path increases by:
•Avoiding Travel and Activities
•Avoiding Commanding Armies
name: Mitigate Fragile Bones

desc:
Staying healthy is the main way to stave off infirmity.

The Infirm Trait progresses by a full level when contracting an Illness, and by a small amount every year.

If you are sick for a prolonged amount of time, the Trait Path will progress much faster each year. It will also progress much faster if you're more than 65 years old.
name: Mitigate Infirmity

desc:
While it's not possible to prevent Withering Mind from progressing, you can slow it down by:
•Having Friends (the more, the better)
•Having Lovers (the more, the better)
•Keeping your Stress low
•Having the Family First or Seducer Traits
•Traveling and partaking in Activities

Many of these factors also reduce the chance of getting the Trait in the first place.
name: Mitigate Withering Mind

desc:
A Modifier is an effect that changes a value over a longer period of time. It may for example change the value of a character's Skills, or the Success Chance of a Scheme.

Modifiers typically appear for Characters, Schemes or Counties.
name: Modifier

desc:
An Empire Title that can be created by a powerful tribal ruler on the Steppes. It enables the Mongol Invasion Casus Belli.

The title is created by taking the Become Greatest of Khans Decision.
name: Mongol Empire

desc:
A powerful Casus Belli available only to the Ruler of the Mongol Empire.

It can target an entire Kingdom Title at once, and allows for rapid expansion across large swathes of land.
name: Mongol Invasion Casus Belli

desc:
An activity where a character chooses to travel to a famous monument or landmark to improve themselves, by delving into its history, knowledge, and mysteries.

Anticipated rewards:
\t• Skill Points
•Court Position Excellent-Aptitude Court Positions
•Prestige
name: Monument Expedition

desc: Group of Characters with shared interests and vision of the Dynastic Cycle. Each Movement member can have access to different Interactions and Decisions to nudge the cycle. A Movement Leader is a spokesperson that represents the Movement's interests with Son of Heaven.
name: Movement

desc:
A character leading the Movement, delegated as the only member allowed to directly speak with Son of Heaven to further the Movements agenda using Make Movement Petition Decision.

To become a leader you either have to have the highest amount of Movement Power Movement Power on previous leader's death or defeat the current leader in Debate Activity.
name: Movement Leader

desc: After an Army has completed more than half of a given move order, it will not be possible to change it until they arrive at their destination.
name: Movement Locked

desc:
Movement Power represents the political clout of a group involved in the Dynastic Cycle. It is the sum of Personal Movement Power of all of the characters in the group.

… unlocks Dismiss Hook Interaction, Request Permission to Raid Interaction and Raid Estate Scheme

Power is derived from:
•Merit Merit Rank
•Influence Level of Influence
•Age
•Movement Power of Disciples
•Current Military Strength (less important in …)
•Confucian Education Trait Experience (less important in …)
•Governor Trait Experience (less important in …)
name: Movement Power

desc:
When the Scales of Power favor the Diarch during Power Sharing, some Interactions the Liege takes may begin to cost Prestige.

The affected actions are:
• Revoking a Title
• Retracting a Vassal
• Imprisoning Characters
• Executing Characters (unless the Liege's Faith practices some form of human sacrifice)
name: Mundane Actions

desc: Death finally catching up to you by being murdered — a death in deceit. The way you lived; the way you died.
name: Murder

desc: Passing on peacefully is the key to dying of Natural Causes. For this purpose, old age and chronic diseases are the main ways to leave this world.
name: Natural Causes

desc: An Interaction which allows a Ruler to grant settle an unruly Adventurer in their Realm
name: Negotiate Settlement

desc: A Nemesis is a Special Relation indicating utter (and mutual) contempt and hatred. It is a stronger Special Relation than a Rival. A character can only have one Nemesis.
name: Nemesis

desc:
The Nerge is a special type of Hunt that can be undertaken by Nomadic Rulers. Instead of hunting a single animal, it is a large scale hunt where hundreds, if not thousands, of animals are slaughtered.

Instead of using the regular Hunt Success Chance, it instead tracks a Nerge Outcome score based on how many animals are killed, which decides the kind of rewards the Host and Guests will get.

A successful Nerge will usually reward:
•Legitimacy Legitimacy
•Prestige Prestige
•Dread Dread
•Gold Gold
And in some cases it may reward:
•Martial Martial
•Command Modifier Commander Trait or Trait Experience
name: Nerge

desc:
Nicknames, Epithets, and Cognomens are all secondary names either taken by or attributed to Characters (e.g. Charles 'the Bald'). Nicknames are purely aesthetic, though the circumstances surrounding their acquisition are often dramatic or noteworthy affairs.

Bad Nicknames will sometimes be overridden by good ones (such as William 'the Bastard' becoming William 'the Conqueror').
name: Nickname

desc: Nobles are characters who are members of a Dynasty. Characters without a Dynasty are considered lowborn Commoners.
name: Noble

desc:
Noble Families are powerful Houses in an Administrative Realm. They own an Estate, controlled and managed by the House Head, and remain an integral part of the Realm at all times, as they will attempt to gather Influence and secure Provinces for themselves.

An influential Noble Family may become a Powerful Family or a Dominant Family.
name: Noble Family

desc:
Nomadic Rulers graze County Fertility to grow their Herd. They can use Herd as Nomadic Horde, which can be upgraded to Men-at-Arms. They have a Nomadic Capital.

Nomads can Migrate to find more fertile lands, though large nomadic Realms can grow their herd through Tributaries or by reaching a high Fertility Equilibrium.

Nomads have a higher maximum Dread.
name: Nomadic

desc:
Nomadic Capitals are moving sets of tents, livestock, people and horses. They can go from just a few sheep to a roaring horde.

Nomadic Rulers have a Nomadic Capital that they grow through Yurt Buildings and take with them when they Migrate. They cannot construct regular Buildings in Holdings.

The Nomadic Capital has a Faith and Culture representing the majority of the migrating people, which can be different from that of the Ruler.

Their whole Court travel with them, as well as their Family, Kurultai and Knights.
name: Nomadic Capital

desc:
The Nomadic Horde is the representation of a Nomadic Ruler's military strength. It is obtained as a fraction of their Herd, and it only appears when the Ruler raises their Armies.

They are converted into Horde Riders that can be upgraded to other Men-at-Arms by paying a Gold cost.

Certain Cultural Traditions, Dynasty legacy perks and Yurt Buildings can increase the conversion rate.
name: Nomadic Horde

desc: Nomadic Settlement represent the existence of a Nomadic Capital on the map. They are a Holding Type used by Nomadic Rulers and provide small amounts of County Control and Popular Opinion.
name: Nomadic Settlement

desc:
A Duumvirate is the rule of one Empire by two Characters. A senior emperor (the Liege), and a junior emperor (the Nominal Co-Emperor).

They are considered to be Nominal Duumvirates when the junior emperor is a Child who cannot effectively rule, but will transition into being full Duumvirates when they reach adulthood.

Nominal Co-Emperors generate passive Influence for both themselves and their senior emperor. How much exactly scales up every … years in the job, carrying over when they become a full Co-Emperor.

Appointing a Child Nominal Co-Emperor marks them as being trained to one day likely be the senior emperor. The more practice they get, the more training they receive.

This is represented as additional Skill distributed to them when they become an Adult, depending on their Scales of Power swing.

Children do not receive Mandate events.
name: Nominal Duumvirate

desc: Under Elective Succession Laws, each Elector can Nominate their preferred Title Heir. Valid candidates and Elector voting preferences differ depending on the specific Law.
name: Nominate

desc:
Oaths are sworn during the Coronation Activity by the Host, and play an important role in securing the Legitimacy of a new Ruler as they step up to take the throne.

Oaths will unlock special time-limited Decisions which the ruler will have to complete to prove themselves worthy of their Title. The rewards gained will be affected by the Magnificence of the coronation.
name: Oath

desc:
In Nomadic Realms, obedience determines the loyalty of a Character to their Liege, Suzerain or owner of their Court. Characters can only be obedient to one Ruler at a time.

Obedient characters are less likely to participate in Hostile Schemes, join Wars or join Factions against their liege. They will always support their liege's preferences during Succession and won't press their Claims on them. Non-obedient Tributaries may try to break free.

When a character's score surpasses the Obedience Threshold they become obedient.
name: Obedience

desc:
The Obedience Threshold is the score that Characters need to achieve in order to be considered Obedient.

The threshold is affected by a series of factors: if they are Close Family of the Overlord, if they are the Primary Heir, their Friendship or Rivalry, their Traits and whether you employ them or not in your Kurultai or Court. Children are more likely to be obedient than adults.

Nomadic Rulers can use the Desperate Times Decision to make everyone obedient, the Impose Obedience Intent during a Hunt to target one character and the Demand Obedience Character Interaction if they have high enough Dread.
name: Obedience Threshold

desc:
Certain parts of an enemy Realm (usually the Realm Capital and the Holdings in the War Target region of a War) are considered Objectives. By Occupying Objectives, you start gaining 'ticking' War Score.

For the Defender, War Score starts to tick up (after an initial period of time) if the Attacking side can be prevented from Occupying any Objectives.
name: Objectives

desc:
Occupied Holdings are temporarily under the control of a hostile Ruler during a War. An Army standing in a Barony with a hostile Fortified Holding will start to Besiege it if the number of Soldiers in the army outnumbers the Garrison.

If the Siege is successful, the Holding is Occupied, which will give War Score to the Occupying side in the War.

Occupying a Holding does not mean it is now yours! Only territory specified by the War Target can actually change hands, and only if the Attacker Wins.
name: Occupation

desc: Being the main attacker in a war will gradually cause your Vassals to dislike you after … months. Civil Wars and Great Holy Wars are excluded from this. Once no longer in such a war, the penalty will slowly decay.
name: Offensive War Opinion

desc: An interaction offering Vassalage to an Independent Ruler of lower Rank, peacefully adding them to the realm.
name: Offer Vassalization

desc:
Officers are specialized roles Followers can be granted in order to aid their Camp.

Mechanically, they operate very similarly to Court Positions. As with them, the benefits you gain from Officers are dictated by the holder's Aptitude for the position.

Unlike Court Positions, appointing Officers is free and they are not paid a monthly salary, though revoking them still costs Prestige.

Officers are unlocked by many different Camp Upgrades.
name: Officer

desc:
Every Character has a one-way Opinion of every other Character, represented by a value ranging from -100 to +100.

The Opinion that another character has of you is of crucial importance, for it will drive their behavior!

You should be especially wary of the Opinions of your Powerful Vassals, Spymaster and Spouse.
name: Opinion

desc:
After a long period of relatively peaceful coexistence during the Conciliation Phase, complacency begins to set in. Peasantry and nobility alike are comfortable that things just work, allowing more shrewd Characters to take advantage of their naivety.

Eventually, fresh abuses will either cause an escalation into the Hostility Phase, or else savvy politicking reaches an uneasy equilibrium through the Conciliation Phase.
name: Opportunity Phase

desc: A Councillor Task performed by the Marshal. It increases Garrison Size and Levy Reinforcement Rate in the Realm of the councillor's Liege.
name: Organize Army

desc:
An Organized Faith has a religious hierarchy. Worship and practices are more organized and scriptures are formalized.

Unreformed Pagan Faiths can become Organized by reforming, while other Faiths are always considered Organized.
name: Organized

desc:
When you have more than … Counties in your Realm as a Duke, you suffer an Overextension Penalty, reducing your Tax income.

Becoming King or Emperor Rank removes this penalty.
name: Overextension

desc: An Overlord is a Ruler to whom another ruler has pledged obedience, either as a Vassal or as a Tributary. Both Suzerains and Lieges are overlords.
name: Overlord

desc:
An Owned Legend is a Legend owned by a Ruler, who is the main beneficiary of its effects.

The owner of a Legend can be its Legend Protagonist, but it's not necessary.

A Legend can also be supported by Legend Promoters, who pay a monthly contribution to also get part of its bonuses.
name: Owned Legend

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

In Pachisi:
• Diplomacy counters Intrigue
• Intrigue counters Stewardship
• Stewardship counters Diplomacy
name: Pachisi

desc:
Pacification tracks how effective the new Norman rulers of England are at subduing the resentful Anglo-Saxon population. Assuming Pacification is higher than Resistance, it bestows effects at the following levels:

Pacification above 5
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: +… per month

Pacification above 8
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: +… per month
•Adds Dread 1 Dread to the ruler of England per month

Pacification above 11
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: +… per month
•Adds Dread 2 Dread to the ruler of England per month

Pacification above 14
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: +… per month
•Adds Dread 3 Dread to the ruler of England per month
•Enables the Embrace English Culture Decision
name: Pacification

desc:
Paiza, or a gerege, is a small metal tablet issued by powerful Characters in the The Great Steppe, which extends the Khans' power to the carrier.

Mechanically, they are Artifacts that a powerful Nomadic ruler issues to their favorites via the Paiza Character Interaction.
After taking the Establish Paiza System Decision, you get access to Summon Wealthy Visitors: Paiza Decision that allows you to engage in trade with settled people, improved by the various Internal Upgrades to the … Yurt Buildings

However, Characters carrying Paiza Artifacts bearing the name of a living Gurkhan have access to Abuse Gurkhan's Authority Decision and Leverage Khan Authority Character Interaction

By the power of Eternal Heaven. By the protection of the Imperial Good Fortune. An edict of the Khan; any person whosoever who does not respect it shall be punished, shall die.
name: Paiza

desc:
The fourth and final Civil Service Examinations. The final … entrants at the Capital Examination are invited to a feast at the royal palace, to kowtow and show their worth to the Son of Heaven.

When passed:
….
name: Palace Examination

desc:
Paper Map
The Paper Map gives you a top-level overview of all independent Realms in the world.

In this mapmode, clicking the map will select Realms
name: Paper Map

desc: Participant Groups within a Situation are a collection of characters that share the same effects during each Situation Phase.
name: Participant Group

desc:
Under any Succession Law with multiple Realm Heirs, a Character's Partition Share is which Titles that particular Heir will inherit upon Succession. Usually, this means dividing between the children of a Ruler, or, rarely, their siblings.

Typically, depending on what type of Succession is in place, Titles may be divided evenly between separate Realms, evenly within the same Realm, or given mostly to the main Heir while dividing the remainder evenly between any other Heirs.
name: Partition Share

desc: An Activity is in a passive phase when the host or the guests have all not yet arrived, or when they are between one Stop and the next on a Tour.
name: Passive

desc: In a Patrilineal Marriage, children will be born into their father's House.
name: Patrilineal

desc:
A powerful Casus Belli available only to the Ruler of the Roman Empire for the purpose of inaugurating a new era of ….

It can target an entire Empire Title at once, and allows for rapid expansion across large swathes of land.
name: Pax Romana Casus Belli

desc:
Wars can end in three types of Peace: Victory, Defeat, or White Peace.

At 100% War Score, the other side cannot refuse a Peace Offer and must accept Defeat.

The effects of Victory or Defeat depend entirely on the type of Casus Belli that was used to declare the war and its associated War Target.
name: Peace

desc: The Peasant Faction is populated by Counties with low Popular Opinion. Unlike other Factions, this one will always revolt even if Faction Military Power is low, as peasants are generally both optimistic and illiterate... Successful Peasant Revolts will significantly lower Control in your Realm.
name: Peasant Faction

desc:
Peasant Militias are Men-at-Arms who are armed with pitchforks and spears.

While each kind of Militia is unique, they generally Counter Heavy Cavalry and Light Cavalry, and are in turn Countered by Heavy Infantry.

Peasant Militias are strong in mountainous and fertile Terrain.
name: Peasant Militia

desc: Perks are unlockable boons that provide many useful and interesting effects. They are unlocked by selecting a Focus within a Lifestyle and spending the associated form of Experience (e.g. Intrigue Experience if you wish to unlock an Intrigue Lifestyle Perk.)
name: Perk

desc:
A Perpetual Hook is a Hook that you might have on a character who owes you a favor, or that you have manipulated to do your will.

They cannot be used to force someone to become your Agent in a Murder and do not provide a passive benefit (for that, a Strong Hook is necessary.)

Perpetual Hooks are not spent when used, but instead go on a cooldown before they can be used again.
name: Perpetual Hook

desc:
A Personal Artifact Claim is an Artifact Claim that is personal to you, as opposed to a House Artifact Claim.

When you die, your children get Claims on all your Artifacts.

You also get a Claim on an Artifact if it's stolen during a Siege or Raid.

Artifact Claims are never inherited.
name: Personal Artifact Claim

desc: Personal Movement Power is how much a member increases the overall Power of their Movement
name: Personal Movement Power

desc:
Personal Schemes are Schemes that aim to induce a status between the Scheme Owner and the Scheme Target.

Examples of Personal Schemes are:
•Sway
•Befriend
•Seduce
•Elope
name: Personal Scheme

desc: Characters will act towards you and others according to their Personality, which is primarily determined by their Personality Traits.
name: Personality

desc: A Personality Trait is a Trait that determine a person's world-view and what actions they are most likely to take. They also affect the Opinion others. One might both lose and gain new traits during one's lifetime. Acting against your own Personality causes Stress.
name: Personality Trait

desc:
An opportunity for Vassals to request aid from their Liege.

A variety of issues can be raised, and it is up to the Liege to decide whether to accept.
name: Petition

desc:
A Physical Trait is a descriptor of a physical Trait tied to their appearance or behavior, and the level of intellect a character has. Many physical features affect how Attracted others are to them.

They are often Congenital, thus gained at birth and permanent.
name: Physical Trait

desc:
Piety represents the virtue of a Character.

Acting piously (according to the Doctrines of their Faith) will increase a Character's Piety, such as going on a Pilgrimage.

Piety can be spent on various religious matters depending on Government Form, Doctrines, etc.

Each time a Character gains Piety, they also progress towards the next Level of Devotion.
name: Piety

desc:
Characters of most Faiths can choose to undertake an Activity to go on a Pilgrimage to a Holy Site. Each Holy Site has an individual grace period before you can revisit. 

Such a journey may be filled with both opportunity and peril, but upon reaching their destination characters will earn Piety and may receive other rewards.
name: Pilgrimage

desc:
A Pious Builder wants to invest all of their Gold into increasing their Piety.

They will spend their treasury to fund religious and ceremonial Buildings, Great Projects, Activities and Decisions, and often construct more Pious Buildings and Temple- or Temple Citadel Holdings. They only save up gold if directly threatened, such as by a strong Faction.

Pious Builders are more likely to create and promote holy Legends.

Zealous …Rulers with a penchant for Virtue and no particular inclination for War, tend to be Pious Builders.
Common Traits include Zealous, Forgiving, Improvident, Humble, Patient, Diligent, and Generous. Rulers with the Theology Focus also tend to be Pious Builders.
name: Pious Builder

desc: Pious Buildings are Buildings whose primary function is to increase their holding's Piety.
name: Pious Building

desc:
A Plague is an outbreak of a disease that spreads across the map, causing both local effects and infecting characters in its area. Affected Baronies have an Infection Rate that handles their severity and can be countered by improving the Plague Resistance.

A Plague can have different Plague Intensities, affecting its area of effect, duration and Fatalities.
name: Plague

desc: A Plague can be Apocalyptic, Major or Minor, affecting its area of spread, the duration and the Characters that get infected by it, causing Fatalities.
name: Plague Intensity

desc:
The Plague Resistance lowers the Infection Rate of a Barony or County, mitigating the effects of a Plague.

The Plague Resistance can be increased through Buildings like Hospices or Burial Site (Duchy Building), Court Position Tasks performed by the Personal Physician, Decisions or events.
name: Plague Resistance

desc:
The Player Heir is the Heir that a player will keep playing as on Succession.

The Player Heir is usually the same as the Primary Heir, but if the Succession Law of your Primary Title dictates that it should go to a character outside of your Dynasty, you will instead keep playing as the dynastic heir to your second highest-tier title (or third, fourth, etc.).

This situation is common when your Player Heir is voted out under an Elective Succession Law. If you are House Head of a Noble Family in an Administrative Realm you may lose your Realm to Primary Heirs outside of your House but retain your Noble Family Title.
name: Player Heir

desc: A Point of Interest is a location in the world that is worth visiting. When you visit that location for the first time, you will gain the benefits associated with it.
name: Point of Interest

desc:
Political Map
The Political Map gives you a comprehensive overview of Rulers in an area, and is ideal for planning Wars, managing Vassals and exploring Realms.

In this mapmode, clicking the map will select Realms
name: Political Map

desc:
The general populace of each County has an Opinion of the Character who holds their County. If the population is unhappy, they might start or join a Peasant Faction or Populist Faction, either of which can soon spread throughout an entire Realm.

The easiest way of controlling Popular Opinion is to ensure that the County Holder is of the same Culture and Faith as the population.

Popular Opinion from having a different Faith is modified by both the county's Faith Hostility and its Fervor, scaling linearly between 0 and 100 Fervor.
name: Popular Opinion

desc: The Populist Faction is populated by Counties with low Popular Opinion that share a common element, such as Culture or Faith. They seek to break free, and choose a new Ruler based on their Culture or Faith. This type of uprising is typically very dangerous.
name: Populist Faction

desc: A Councillor Task may have unexpected consequences over time. These may be good or bad, with positive effects being more likely the higher the Councillor's relevant Skill, and negative effects being more likely the lower the relevant Skill is.
name: Possible Side Effects

desc:
Power Sharing occurs when a Ruler shares some authority with one of their Vassals or Courtiers, who becomes their Diarch.

The Ruler who shares their power may set Mandates for their Diarch, while the Diarch may use special Borrowed Powers.

The Scales of Power measure whether the Ruler or the Diarch has the most authority.
name: Power Sharing

desc:
A Powerful Family represents one of the most influential Houses and Noble Families in an Administrative Realm.

A member of a Powerful Family is better at Political Schemes and is more likely to get what they want when Interacting with other Characters.

There can only be a limited number of Powerful Families at any given time, and it is the top rated Noble Families that are considered powerful based on their Rating. The House of the Top Liege is an exception, which is always considered Powerful.

A Family controlling a significant part of a Realm's land can become a Dominant Family.
name: Powerful Family

desc:
A Powerful Family Attribute is a set of bonuses associated with a House inside an Administrative Realm. The Attribute benefits the members of the House, as well as the Liege.

Attributes are only active as long as the House is considered a Powerful Family, and the Family Attribute of a Dominant Family does not benefit their Liege.

The House Head can freely replace the Attribute at any given time.
name: Powerful Family Attribute

desc:
Powerful Family Rating is a measure of how influential a Powerful Family is.

While there are many ways to increase a Family's Rating, the main factor is the number of held Governorships.

A House must have a Rating of at least … to be considered Powerful.
name: Powerful Family Rating

desc:
'Powerful Vassals' are the handful of Vassals with the most Soldiers and highest Income. You need to pay careful attention to these vassals, because they expect to hold a seat on your Council and will have significantly lower Opinion of you if they do not.

Changing a Succession Law requires all Powerful Vassals to either have a positive Opinion of you, be Terrified by you, or be Imprisoned.
name: Powerful Vassal

desc:
Many factors go into a successful Scheme, some of which can not be known until it begins and Agents are recruited.

Though any Scheme is possible, many can be costly.

The five levels of difficulty are:
•@aptitude:5:inherit_color!Very Easy — likely to be easy, fast, and silent
•@aptitude:4:inherit_color!Easy — minimal effort required
•@aptitude:3:inherit_color!Moderate — a few bribes may be needed
•@aptitude:2:inherit_color!Hard — success will be expensive
•@aptitude:1:inherit_color!Very Hard — success is unlikely and costly
name: Predicted Scheme Difficulty

desc:
The Preparation Phase is the time before an Undirected Great Holy War is declared.

During this time, Rulers of attacking Faith can choose to pledge military support to the war and/or donate to the War Chest.

A timer will count down until the Preparation Phase ends, whereupon the war will be declared.

Rulers of the defending Religions can choose to counter-pledge their military support during this time, giving an overview of the strength of the two sides.
name: Preparation Phase

desc: Pressed Claims are considered legally strong, and are inherited as Unpressed Claims by the children of the Claimant.
name: Pressed Claim

desc:
Prestige represents a Character's fame and social standing.

Prestige can be spent on various worldly matters depending on Government Form, Doctrines, et cetera.

Every time a Character gains Prestige, they also progress toward the next Level of Fame.
name: Prestige

desc:
Rarely, certain situations in the life of the Target of a Murder may cause the Scheme to fail in the final stages of its execution.

This overrides Success Chance.

Examples include intervention by a bodyguard, a foodtaster, a shieldmaiden, or a loyal pet.
name: Prevented Murder

desc: The Primary Heir is the character who will inherit the Primary Title of a Ruler on Succession. This is usually — but not always — the same character as the Player Heir.
name: Primary Heir

desc: In Polygamous Faiths, Rulers must choose one of their Spouses to be their Primary Spouse. A ruler's Primary Spouse gains increased Fertility with them, increased Opinion of them, and may serve on their Council.
name: Primary Spouse

desc:
A Ruler's Primary Title is their highest-ranked Title that they identify most closely with, determining their Coat of Arms and the name of their Realm.

If you control multiple titles of the same tier, you can choose which one should be your Primary Title.
name: Primary Title

desc:
Landed Rulers can keep other Characters as Prisoners, either in their Dungeon or under simple House Arrest. In a Camp all Prisoners are kept in the Stockade. Characters risk imprisonment in Battle or at the end of a Siege.

Characters can also arrest anyone inside their own Realm, or Camp. However, this is viewed as Tyrannical unless the Character is guilty of a Crime.

Prisoners are at your mercy and can be Executed, Tortured, Ransomed or simply Released.
name: Prison

desc:
A Prisoner of War is a Prisoner who's captured during a War, but not of importance to provide the captors with War Score.

Valuable Prisoners are released when the war ends, unlike prisoners of war, but can still be ransomed for release.
name: Prisoner of War

desc:
When a Camp is stationary, they can sustain themselves with bartering food for odd jobs, hunting, foraging, or fishing where allowed and possible, and generally just about treading water on their supply situation.

As soon as they have to start Traveling, they're entirely reliant on their Provisions to survive, since they cannot both move and obtain sufficient food. As Provisions run low (then run out), tempers will flare and Followers will starve.

When this happens, Characters will begin to leave the Camp, negative Modifiers are increasingly applied, and those who remain will eventually mutiny or die.
name: Privation

desc:
Prizes are Artifacts awarded to the victors of Grand Tournament Contests with a single winner.

The quality of the Prize depends on the options chosen by the Activity Host and the Era.
name: Prize

desc:
An abstraction of your likelihood to win a given Contest relative to the other contestants, based on your Skills, Health, and Traits. For example, a Giant with high Prowess has an advantage in physical contests fought on foot, such as Wrestling.

A minimum Progress to Victory is required to guarantee Qualification for a Contest. Visit Locales for opportunities to improve your chances and sabotage your opponents.

The Tournament Leaderboard displays all contestant's current Progress to Victory.
name: Progress to Victory

desc: A project is something an Inspired Character undertakes with the help of a Sponsor to realize their vision, normally in the form of creating an Artifact.
name: Project

desc:
Prominence reflects how desirable a Title is to eligible candidates.
