A candidate who already holds a Title will only be appointed to a new one of the same Tier if it has higher Prominence.

Prominence is typically based on local wealth and proximity to the Realm Capital, but other factors may apply depending on circumstance, such as the size of Title Men-at-Arms for Military Governors.
name: Prominence

desc:
Promote Cultural Acceptance is a Councillor Task performed by the Steward.

It increases the Cultural Acceptance between the target Culture and the Ruler's Culture.
name: Promote Cultural Acceptance

desc:
Promote Culture is a Councillor Task performed by the Steward.

It changes the Culture of a County to match its ruler's Culture.
name: Promote Culture

desc: An Promoted Legend is a Legend owned by a different Ruler that is being supported by Legend Promoters, who pay a monthly contribution to also get part of its bonuses.
name: Promoted Legend

desc:
With the Prosperity Decree, the Mandala Ruler is focused on stimulating and inspiring all Subjects to enact constructive changes.

Efforts are funneled into furthering Development, Buildings, amassing wealth as well as strengthening community via personal relations.
name: Prosperity Decree

desc:
A Province is a Title held by a Governor inside a Realm with the Administrative Government.

A Province has an associated Province Administration that greatly impacts the benefits the Province provides.
name: Province

desc:
Each Province of an Administrative Realm has a Province Administration, which may be set by the Liege and Governor to specialize the Province.

Only one Province Administration may be active per Province.
name: Province Administration

desc:
A Provincial Army is an army recruited and maintained by a Governor in a Realm with the Administrative Government.

They are exclusively made up of Title Men-at-Arms. The effectiveness of Men-at-Arms are affected by a …'s Governor Efficiency.

The Liege can spend Influence to gain control of Armies.

… may borrow troops from their peers under certain circumstances, such as being Allies or using a Hook.

A borrowed Army is returned if the … who borrowed them dies or when they end all of their ongoing Wars. Armies can also be returned manually.
name: Provincial Army

desc:
The second level Civil Service Examinations, taken via the Local Examination Activity.

When passed:
….
name: Provincial Examination

desc:
Provisions represent the total amount of food, water, and shelter a Camp can provide.

Camps lose Provisions while moving Location. Exactly how much is affected by size of their Men-at-Arms, the Terrain moved across, and what Officers are currently hired.

Camp followers running low on Provisions will start suffering Privation events: starting with Characters quickly losing Opinion of their leader, escalating rapidly to starvation and death.

Provisions can be refilled when stationary by requesting them from Patrons, taking a Decision, or as Contract rewards.
name: Provisions

desc:
Prowess is a Skill that reflects the Character's aptitude in personal combat.

A high Prowess Skill means they are more likely to survive and perform well both as Knights in Battles and in Duels.

Each point of Prowess gives a Knight:
•Damage: …
•Toughness: …

Increasing prowess through natural sources (not through Artifacts) will increase a Character's muscle mass.
name: Prowess Skill

desc: An Interaction allowing you to Duel criminals when you are Stressed.
name: Punish Criminal Interaction

desc: An Interaction which allows an Adventurer to buy land from a Ruler and settle in their Realm
name: Purchase Land

desc: An Interaction that allows Truces to be bought preemptively in exchange for Gold Gold.
name: Purchase Truce

desc: A victorious Army increases the amount of Casualties they inflict in the Aftermath of a Battle by their Army's combined Pursuit value, converting Routed Casualties into Fatal Casualties.
name: Pursuit

desc:
While a Grand Tournament will attract many eligible Contestants, only a small number will Qualify for each Contest, with a chance of winning glory and its Prize.

To guarantee Qualification, your Progress to Victory must be above the threshold when the Contest begins.
name: Qualification

desc:
Quality gauges the power of an Army relative to its number of Soldiers.

An Army that only contains Knights and Men-at-Arms will be of high Quality while an Army containing a large number of Levies will be of lower Quality.

This means that a smaller Army with a high Quality will punch well above their weight — carefully consider both the amount of Soldiers and Quality before engaging the enemy!
name: Quality

desc:
The winner of Race Contests is the Qualifying Contestant whose entered horse has taken first place at the end of the race.

Race Contests:
•Horse Race
name: Race

desc:
Armies can be raised as Raiders from Rally Points. Raiders can move into neighboring lands and pillage them for Gold.

In order to Raid, a Raiding Army must stop in a Holding owned by a foreign Ruler and choose to start Raiding — upon doing so they will be stuck Raiding for a some time, after which they will get Gold and pillage the Holding.

Gold will be stored on the Army, and only added to the treasury when they arrive home. If you defeat a Raiding Army carrying Gold you will take it, and they will be unable to Raid you for some time.

Only some Rulers are allowed to Raid, most notably Tribal and Nomadic Rulers.

Specific Raid Intents can be set to obtain different rewards.
name: Raid

desc:
This is a special type of War, started by a Ruler whose Faith practices human sacrifice. The primary goal of Raiding for Captives is to do battle and capture Prisoners for sacrifice, with either side able to get enough War Score through combat to win without ever having to Siege.

At the end of the War, if the victor (including the defender) follows a Faith practicing human sacrifice, then they will take several Prisoners from the Court of the loser. If both main combatants in a Raid for Captives follow the same faith, then the war is considered sacred, meaning that the loser still receives (reduced) Piety even in defeat.

You cannot conduct or continue a Raid for Captives if you have any Prisoners obtained through winning a Raid for Captives in your Dungeon.
name: Raid for Captives

desc: A Raid Intent may modify the types of rewards obtained from a Raid or an army's movement speed or Loot capacity. Apart from the regular raiding for Gold and Prestige, there are alternatives like attempting to destroy Buildings, or increasing the chance of Imprisoning Characters.
name: Raid Intent

desc:
A Rally Point is a mustering ground for the Levies and Men-at-Arms under your command.

In times of War, you can call up your Soldiers at a Rally Point to gather an Army.

The Levies assigned to a Rally Point must come from either your own Domain or your Vassals. Rally Points can be reorganized, split and merged as you see fit.
name: Rally Point

desc:
The personal equivalent of Title Tier, Rank determines the position of a Ruler within the hierarchy of the game.

All Title Tiers have an associated Rank, which determines the highest possible Rank of Vassals that the Holder can have.

Hegemon > Emperor > King > Duke > Count > Baron.
name: Rank

desc: A Realm is all the land that a Ruler controls either directly or through Vassals (in contrast to a Domain, which is only the Holdings personally owned by a Ruler).
name: Realm

desc:
The Realm Capital is the Holding where a Ruler and their Court resides. This Holding has a Tax bonus, and is always inherited by the Primary Heir.

Occupying the Realm Capital of an enemy in a war gives a significant amount of War Score and sometimes lets you Imprison members of the enemy's family.
name: Realm Capital

desc:
A Realm Heir is one of the Heirs of a Realm, and will receive either all or some of the Titles held by the Ruler of that Realm when that Ruler dies.

A Realm may have one or more Realm Heirs depending on its Succession Law.
name: Realm Heir

desc:
A Realm Priest is a Councillor in charge of religious and spiritual affairs in Faiths with the Theocratic Doctrine.

Unlike their Lay Clergy equivalent (Court Chaplains), Realm Priests automatically Lease all Temple Holdings in a Ruler's Domain, and also receive a portion of Taxes and Levies from Vassal Realm Priests.

Realm Priests provide their Liege with Levies and Taxes if they have a positive Opinion of them. The higher the Opinion of their Liege, the more they will provide.

Realm Priests with a low Opinion of their Liege will not provide them with any Taxes or Levies, and might cause problems.
name: Realm Priest

desc: A character's Realm Size is the number of Counties owned by them and their Vassals.
name: Realm Size

desc: The act of rebuilding a Ruined building, restoring it to its former glory.
name: Rebuilt Building

desc: Holdings acquired in the last year that put a ruler above their Domain Limit do not cause penalties to their other holdings, but also provide no Taxes or Levies.
name: Recently Acquired Holding

desc: An Army will become 'Recently Disembarked' whenever it disembarks after having been at sea. This will cause the Army to suffer from an Advantage penalty in Battles for a certain duration.
name: Recently Disembarked

desc:
Some Inventory Artifacts can be Reforged, turning them into Court Artifacts.

You need to have an Antiquarian and pay Gold to Reforge an Artifact, though older Artifacts are cheaper to Reforge.

Just like when you Repair an Artifact, its Durability is restored.

Only Weapons, Armors, Crowns and Regalia can be Reforged, and they always become Pedestal Items.
name: Reforge Artifact

desc:
The Culture Head is able to change certain parts of their Culture through Reformation. This is a process that takes a long time and can't be stopped once initiated. 

The reformable parts are:
•Traditions
•Ethos
•Martial Custom
name: Reformation

desc:
Refusing to convert will be considered a Crime if:
•The refusing Character is of the same Religion as the Character making the demand
•The Religion has Heresies
•The Faith of the Character making the demand is Hostile or more towards the refusing Character's Faith
name: Refuse Conversion

desc:
A Regency is a special form of Power Sharing for when the Ruler is not able to rule their Realm on their own.

It generally occurs if the Ruler is a Child, Imprisoned, Incapable, or attending an Activity outside their Realm.

A Regency that persists too long may become an Entrenched Regency.
name: Regency

desc:
In a Regency, the next Regent is picked based on which candidate has the highest Regency Succession Score.

If the Ruler of the Realm designates a Regent, they will override the succession order and be chosen instead.

This favors Characters related to the Ruler, especially landless Family at their Court and the politically savvy.
name: Regency Succession Score

desc:
A Regent is the name for a Diarch during a Regency.

A Ruler can designate a Regent before a Regency occurs. Otherwise, the candidate with the highest Regency Succession Score is automatically chosen.
name: Regent

desc: The Regent Family is the top House in an Realm with a Ruling Regent.
name: Regent Family

desc: A Regiment is a group of Soldiers of a single type (e.g., archers, footmen, or Levies). Although Levies are organized into Regiments, the ones of real interest are the Men-at-Arms.
name: Regiment

desc: A region constitutes a specific geographical area on the map. Unlike De Jure, regions are never subject to change.
name: Region

desc: An Interaction allowing you to Duel anyone when you are Stressed.
name: Release your Anger Interaction

desc: Being passed into the next world by heathens and the sacrilegious dispatching of your mortal coil — martyrdom, crucifixion — remaining true to your faith to the very end, what more genuine way is there to pass on.
name: Religion

desc: A Religion can consist of many different denominations, called Faiths. Religions, in turn, belong to one of four larger Religious Families; Abrahamic, Dharmic, Sinitic or Pagan.
name: Religion

desc:
A Religious Family is a group of Religions. The Religious Family affects how the various Religions, and Faiths therein, view each other.

The Abrahamic Family condones Holy Wars against everyone (including other Abrahamics). Religions are susceptible to Heresy.

The Dharmic Family only condones Holy Wars against other Religious Families.

The Pagan Family condones Holy Wars against everyone, but Faiths within the Religions must be reformed to access them.
name: Religious Family

desc:
A Councillor Task performed by the Court Chaplain.
Increases same-Faith Theocratic rulers' opinion of the character, and increases monthly Piety gain.
name: Religious Relations

desc:
Prisoners can be released in return for Renouncing all Claims on Titles within your Realm.

However, children of the current Holder can never lose their Claims as long as the Holder is still alive.
name: Renounce

desc:
Renown is much like Prestige, but shared by an entire Dynasty.

A Dynasty gains Renown for the following:
• The number of currently living members
• The number of Rulers
• The number of Spouses to other Rulers
Note that a Ruler will not generate Renown should they have any Liege of the same Dynasty.

As with Prestige, Renown also counts towards increasing your Level of Splendor.

Renown can be spent by the Dynasty Head in order to unlock Dynasty Legacies and influence the members of the Dynasty in various ways.

A Dynasty spread far and wide between several different Realms will generate more Renown than a Dynasty concentrated within a single Realm.
name: Renown

desc:
When an Artifact has low Durability, you can choose to Repair it.

You need to pay Gold to Repair an Artifact.…
name: Repair Artifact

desc:
Republican Government is an unplayable Government Form where an elected citizen rules for life — the Government Form of burghers and merchants.

Republican Vassals have static Obligations that cannot be changed, and thus always provide a dependable and predictable amount of Levies and Taxes.
name: Republic

desc: The Request Anointment Character Interaction is a special interaction that can be used by a Ruler on their Head of Faith to secure their support in an Anointment.
name: Request Anointment

desc: Ask your Head of Faith to honor you with a specific title
name: Request Honorary Title

desc: Ask your Head of Faith to steer your House Unity in a certain direction
name: Request House Unity Interference

desc: Finance any Turkic-heritage Ruler to conquer any of your neighboring rulers
name: Request Incursion

desc: A Casus Belli available to House Heads that forces the target to release every Imprisoned House member.
name: Rescue House Members

desc:
A Research Project is an Inspiration that relies on a Court Scholar's Aptitude to bring benefits to their employer.

In some rare cases the Research Project can uncover a new Innovation.
name: Research Project

desc:
Resistance measures the ongoing opposition to Norman rule in England from the pre-existing Anglo-Saxon population. Assuming Resistance is higher than Pacification, it bestows effects at the following levels:

Resistance above 7
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: … per month

Resistance above 10
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: … per month
•Slightly increased chance of Claimant Factions against the ruler of England

Resistance above 13
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: … per month
•Somewhat increased chance of Claimant Factions against the ruler of England
•County Control in all Counties reduced by … every 3 months for every Vassal of England

Resistance above 16
•Anglo-Saxon/Norman Cultural Acceptance: … per month
•Greatly increased chance of Claimant Factions against the ruler of England
•County Control in all Counties reduced by … every 3 months for every Vassal of England
name: Resistance

desc:
A Restored Emperor is a Ten'nō who governs independently of a Ruling Regent.

To become a Restored Emperor, a Ten'nō may be installed by a Restore Ceremonial Monarch Faction, or use the Restore Direct Imperial Rule Decision after becoming Ruling Regent.
name: Restored Emperor

desc:
Some Accolade Attributes give access to special Men-at-Arms. They are unlocked by having an Acclaimed Knight with progress in relevant Hastiluder Trait Path or a relevant Commander Trait.

Retinue Men-at-Arms are restricted to one Regiment. They are twice as effective at countering other Men-at-Arms.
name: Retinue Men-at-Arms

desc: The Retirement Age Law is the age, determined by the Top Liege of the Realm, beyond which Governors and Ministers may choose to retire via Decision or be compelled to do so with a Character Interaction, on the grounds of their impending decrepitude and diminished capacity to serve.
name: Retirement Age

desc:
At Limited Crown Authority or higher, Rulers can Retract the Vassal of a Vassal, but unless the latter is Imprisoned this is risky, for the Vassal may refuse and rise up in rebellion.

Vassal Retraction is considered Tyrannical unless the target is guilty of a fairly severe Crime.
name: Retract

desc: An Army will Retreat if it loses a Battle. Armies can also be ordered to Retreat during Battles. While Retreating, the Army cannot disband or be given new movement orders.
name: Retreat

desc:
The Reverence Decree mandates that the Mandala Subjects focus their efforts on furthering spirituality and worship.

Pilgrimages, rituals and Piety are the cornerstones of this Mandala Decree.
name: Reverence Decree

desc:
At Limited Crown Authority or higher, Rulers can Revoke the Titles of their Vassals, but unless the Vassal is Imprisoned this is a risky proposition, for the Vassal may refuse and rise up in rebellion.

Title Revocation is considered Tyrannical unless the Vassal is guilty of a fairly severe Crime.
name: Revoke

desc:
This Faith is considered legitimate.
Intermarriage is common.

Effects:
…
name: Righteous

desc:
The Rightful Liege of a Vassal is the Ruler who holds the direct De Jure Liege Title of the Vassal's Primary Title. If a Vassal is not under their Rightful Liege, they will contribute less Taxes and Levies as well as suffer an Opinion penalty towards their Liege. Holding a higher-Tier Title of the same De Jure results in lessened penalties.

An exception to this is Dukes that are part of an Empire's De Jure hierarchy and directly vassalized to their Emperor, which still contribute fully, exactly as if the Emperor held their De Jure Kingdom Title.

Example: The Count of Dunbar is a direct vassal of the King of England. Since the King is neither Duke of Lothian, King of Scotland, nor Emperor of Britannia, the Count of Dunbar only contributes a tiny amount of their taxes and levies.

The Count of Norfolk is also a direct vassal of the King of England. The King does not hold the Duchy of East Anglia, so the Count also contributes reduced taxes and levies. However, because the England is the De Jure Kingdom of Norfolk, the Count of Norfolk still contributes significantly more tax and levies to the King than the Count of Dunbar does.
name: Rightful Liege

desc:
Characters in Single Combats run the risk of hurting themselves, either by accidentally opening their guard to their opponent, or simply injuring themselves with their own weapon. As they fight, they also build Risk of Injury.

Duels that go on longer make it easier to hurt yourself.

The counterpart to Risk of Injury is Likelihood of Success.
name: Risk of Injury

desc:
Ritsuryō is a type of Administrative Government unique to Japan.

It is a centralized Bureaucratic Government Form where Characters are appointed as Governors on behalf of their Liege, have access to Influence, and Noble Family Heads have a Family Manor and House Aspiration.

A Kampaku governs the Realm on behalf of the Japanese Emperor, and may be elected from among Noble Family Heads, or imposed by Faction demand.

Ritsuryō Vassals generally govern only a single County, but may reject the centralized system and become local Sōryō lords to build their own power, though this is usually considered a Criminal act.

Ritsuryō House Heads may create and join House Blocs within the Realm, which will support the Leading House in becoming Kampaku.

Japanese Governments have a lower Domain Limit than others, which may be increased by upgrading the Family Manor.

The Ritsuryō system refers to the centralized administrative government of Japan, inspired by the Chinese Confucian bureaucracy.
name: Ritsuryō Government

desc:
A Rival is a Special Relation indicating life-long resentment, if not hatred.

Rivals who truly despise each other might become Nemeses.
name: Rival

desc:
By remaining loyal to his liege even in exile, El Cid may regain their favor and restore his advantageous position.

By becoming disloyal, El Cid may gain special options to raise himself as an independent ruler.
name: Rodrigo's Loyalty

desc:
Adventurers are without Land, but not without connections.

The Roll of Patrons is a list of every Character they have successfully completed a Contract for, as well as others that have some reason to support them — Family with high Opinion of them, Friends, Lovers, and so on.

Patrons can be milked for extra support via the Make a Request Character Interaction.
name: Roll of Patrons

desc: In Battle, most Casualties are actually Routed Casualties and not dead or badly wounded. Unlike Fatal Casualties, these Soldiers will live to fight another day and return to the Army after the Battle is concluded. They can still be ridden down by the winning side during the Aftermath of a Battle, including if the Army voluntarily Retreats.
name: Routed Casualties

desc:
Distinguished Rulers are famed enough to maintain a Royal Court, which gives access to a variety of bonuses and opportunities.

When a Feudal, Clan, or Tribal Ruler becomes King or Emperor, they gain access to their Royal Court.

Each Royal Court has a Court Grandeur Level, which gives benefits based on how famed the Royal Court is, and which Court Type the Royal Court is.

Petitioners, Vassals, and Courtiers may appear at your Royal Court, or you can Hold Court to invite anyone in the Realm to air their grievances.

A Royal Court also allows the Ruler to display Court Artifacts, and Inspired Guests may appear at the Royal Court, offering to create new Artifacts.

When you die, your Player Heir will inherit your Royal Court.
name: Royal Court

desc:
A building that has been Ruined has been shattered, defaced or pillaged for parts by external forces.

These external forces might be things like:
•Natural Disasters…
name: Ruined Building

desc: A Ruler is a Character who holds at least one Title.
name: Ruler

desc:
Ruling Regent is the general term for any Top Liege who rules de facto on behalf of a Ceremonial Monarch, such as the Japanese Ten'nō.

The name of the Ruling Regent's position may change based on the current political circumstances; in Japan they may be referred to as Kampaku or Shōgun.
name: Ruling Regent

desc:
Having a high Safety value will help you avoid Danger during your Travels. Your Safety is affected by your Skills as well as those of your Caravan Master.

A … contribution can never be lower than 0.
name: Safety

desc: Treasury sent to Vassals from the central government, which they receive as Gold to be used as their personal salary. It is based on the periodically calculated allocation of the Treasury income of the Top Liege.
name: Salary Budget

desc:
During Power Sharing, the balance of power between the Liege and their Diarch is measured on the Scales of Power.

As the Scales tip towards the Diarch, they unlock Borrowed Powers and may add costs to the Liege's Mundane Actions.

As they tip towards the Liege, it instead makes it easier for the Liege to end the Power Sharing.

The Scales can be swung by:
•Using the Swing the Scales of Power Character Interaction against the opposing party
•As the Diarch, serving your Liege well (however cynically) in Mandate events
name: Scales of Power

desc:
A Scheme is a long-term attempt to affect the world around you. Schemes can target Characters, Titles, Cultures and Faiths, and come in four types: Personal, Hostile, Political, and Contract Schemes.

Your Scheme's Success Chance grows over time depending on how proficient you are in the associated Skill, and can also be impacted by the Agents you plot your Scheme with.

Secret Schemes are hidden from their target but can be discovered if their Secrecy is low.
name: Scheme

desc: Advantages represent progress made towards the goal of a Scheme. They can be spent to convince Agents to join a Scheme, or to execute one with an increased Success Chance.
name: Scheme Advantage

desc:
A Breach represents a complication in a Secret Scheme. When a Scheme is breached, its Success Chance is reduced. The penalty to Success Chance increases for each cumulative Breach. Once a Scheme reaches 5 Breaches, it will automatically fail.

Schemes also check their Secrecy when they are finally executed — breaches have no effect on this one way or another.
name: Scheme Breach

desc:
This number is directly deducted from the Secrecy score of any Secret Scheme against you or your Courtiers.

Secrecy is checked when a Scheme is executed, and at a reduced rate once per month.
name: Scheme Discovery Chance

desc:
Every Phase, a Scheme's Success Chance is increased by this value, until the maximum current Potential is hit.

For instance, if a Scheme currently has 50% Success Chance, a Potential of 54%, and a Growth of 3%, then after one Phase has gone by, it'll have 53% Success Chance.

Since Growth is still capped by Potential, after the next phase, the Scheme would only have 54% Success Chance.
name: Scheme Growth

desc:
A Scheme's Owner is the Character scheming against the Scheme Target.

For example, the would-be killer in a Murder Scheme.
name: Scheme Owner

desc:
A Phase is the length of time it takes to boost Scheme Success Chance once.

Each Phase the Scheme will gain an Advantage. The Phase Length can be shortened by appointing Agents, and is increased by the Scheme Resistance of the target.
name: Scheme Phase

desc:
Phase Length refers to how many days it takes to complete a single Scheme Phase. Speed is affected by your Skill, Agents, and your Spymaster, as well as by the 'Support Schemes' Councillor Task if the Scheme is Hostile.

A lower Phase Length is beneficial because it will cause a Scheme to progress faster.
name: Scheme Phase Length

desc:
A Scheme has a Success Chance, a percentage value that determines its outcome, reached via Scheme Growth. This is limited by Scheme Potential, which serves as the upper bound of a Scheme.

Scheme Potential can be increased by hiring appropriate Agents, but can never exceed 95%, except for Contract Schemes.

Harmonious Agents may give further bonus Modifiers via events.

Excess Success Chance above a Scheme's Potential is lost.
name: Scheme Potential

desc:
The Scheme Resistance of a Character slows down Schemes against them.

The Scheme Phase Length of the Scheme Owner is reduced by this value, increasing the time it takes for the Scheme to gain Advantages.

Scheme Resistance is increased by the corresponding Skill of the Scheme Target and their Spymaster, as well as by the 'Disrupt Schemes' Councillor Task (if the Scheme is Hostile).
name: Scheme Resistance

desc:
The Success Chance of a Scheme determines how likely it is for it to succeed when executed.

A Scheme's Success Chance will grow over time, and is based on the assigned Agents as well as an associated Skill. Success Chance is limited by Scheme Potential. No Scheme can ever exceed a 95% Success Chance, except for Contract Schemes.

Secret Schemes have a risk of being discovered by target. If that happens your Success Chance will be heavily reduced.
name: Scheme Success Chance

desc:
A Scheme's Target is the Character being schemed against by the Scheme Owner.

For example, the potential victim in a Murder Scheme.
name: Scheme Target

desc: A defeated Army reduces the amount of Casualties they take in the Aftermath of a Battle by their Army's combined Screen value.
name: Screen

desc:
Simultaneously a legal document and a revered symbol of the grace of the Son of Heaven, the Seal of Investiture signifies the holder's special status as a loyal and favored Tributary of ….

A Seal of Investiture may be granted to Tributaries with high Imperial Grace during the closing ceremonies of a successful Tribute Mission.
name: Seal of Investiture

desc: A skillful Stargazer can predict the next Steppe Season in a region, offering helpful information to their liege in order to plan their next moves.
name: Seasonal Prediction

desc:
The Secrecy of a Hostile Scheme determines how likely it is for it to remain undetected from the Scheme target.

The Secrecy of a Scheme will have an initial immunity period where it is unable to be discovered. After this period, the Scheme will be at risk of being discovered every month through a Breach. Your Agents can greatly impact how well you are able to keep your Scheme secret.

A Scheme with a Secrecy of 80% has a 20% chance to be discovered on execution, and a 2% chance to be discovered each month it continues.
name: Secrecy

desc:
Secrets are things that characters do not wish others to know because they are embarrassing, immoral or outright Criminal.

Secrets can be discovered through the 'Find Secrets' Councillor Task for the Spymaster. Once you know someone's Secret, you can Blackmail the character to gain a Hook.
name: Secret

desc:
A Secret Scheme is a Scheme that progresses unbeknownst to the Scheme Target.

However, it can be discovered, causing a reduction in Success Chance, and increasing the likelihood that the Scheme Owner is discovered when the Scheme executes.

Agents that are recruited to a Secret Scheme have a chance of being Discovered.
name: Secret Scheme

desc:
The Secretary Director is a type of Diarch for Son of Heaven, helping the divine ruler to manage the Realm.

Who the Director is depends on the active Grand Secretariat Control Law. The position can be held by either the Grand Chancellor, the Grand Marshal, or the Imperial Censor.

The Director is able to start most Great Projects available to certain Ministers and Son of Heaven.
name: Secretary Director

desc: This type of Opinion affects all characters that are not Clergy.
name: Secular Opinion

desc:
A Casus Belli available to Rulers bordering a Realm governed by a Bureaucratic Government Form.

It allows the attacker to seize a neighboring Duchy that lies outside the defender's capital's De Jure hierarchy.
name: Seize Peripheral Duchy

desc: A Decision allowing for the sale of trivial titles — titles of a purely symbolic importance. Grants Gold in exchange for Prestige.
name: Sell Titles Decision

desc:
Settlement Issues are tasks given to a Nomad Ruler after finishing a Migration to new lands. They give the opportunity to handle conflicts and increase the local County Control in the new Domain.

These issues will continue to happen for the first years after a ruler has migrated, as long as the county has low county control.
name: Settlement Issue

desc: Every Settlement Issue has a Settlement Issue Tier, which reflects the overall rewards of an Issue when successfully solved. Solving an Issue with with a higher tier will typical in more rewards in addition to the County Control.
name: Settlement Issue Tier

desc:
A character's sexual orientation determines which other characters they are potentially Attracted to.

Sexual orientation has no impact on who they can Marry, but may reduce the Fertility of a wedded couple if either spouse fails to match the other's preference.

The limited sexual orientations modeled in Crusader Kings III include:
•Heterosexual
•Homosexual
•Bisexual
•Asexual
name: Sexual Orientation

desc:
'Short Reign' is a decaying Opinion penalty that all characters in a Realm get with a new Liege.

In a similar way, subjects get an increasing Long Reign Opinion bonus with Lieges who have ruled over them for a long time.
name: Short Reign

desc:
Many Faiths have Doctrines which designate certain behaviors as Shunned. Depending on the specific Doctrine, these behaviors may also be considered Criminal.

Characters who are caught practicing behaviors that are Shunned by their Faith lose a Level of Devotion and gain a corresponding Fame Trait; this Trait will be disliked by everyone whose Faith considers that behavior to be either Shunned or Criminal.

Examples of Shunned behaviors include:
•Fornicator
•Adulterer
•Deviant
•Sodomite
•Kinslayer
•witch
name: Shunned

desc: A Shōgun, or Dictator, is the de facto Sōryō Government ruler of all Japan, who has consolidated their position to the point their succession is hereditary, and reigns in the Ten'nō's stead.
name: Shōgun

desc:
Siege is when an Army surrounds a Fortified Holding in order to starve the citizens into submission so that it can be Occupied. A Siege starts automatically once an Army enters the location of a hostile Fortified Holding and stands still — if the Army outnumbers the Garrison.

The besieging Army can Assault the Holding if its walls are Breached.
name: Siege

desc:
The Siege Progress indicates how close a Siege is to being completed and how long the Siege is expected to last. When Progress is full, the Holding will become Occupied.

The amount of Siege Progress required is affected by Fort Level and the manning of the Garrison.

Progress is gained daily and is affected by Siege Events. It can also be increased by having Siege Weapons, or an Army that vastly outnumbers the Garrison.
name: Siege Progress

desc:
When an Adventurer successfully Sieges a Holding, a portion of their Men-at-Arms will be replenished.

All Men-at-Arms Regiments in the Army will be replenished by x2 times the Holding's Loot value.

The increase is made up of new recruits, the press-ganging of locals, and simply paying those who wandered off during the siege.
name: Siege Replenishment

desc:
Siege Weapons are Men-at-Arms that focus entirely on Sieges.

They do not have an impact on Battles, but will make a Siege complete much faster by increasing the Siege Progress.

However, Siege Weapons are only effective at besieging Holdings up to a certain Fort Level.
name: Siege Weapon

desc:
The Silk Road is not one road, but a whole network of routes that connect the furthest corners of civilization to exchange gold, goods, and ideas. To have access to the Silk Road is to have access to all the riches of the world.

Different levels of access to the silk road grant varying gold bonuses, and may provide unique opportunities to unlock exotic Innovations. The amount of gold and knowledge traveling on the Silk Road will change depending on its prosperity, which is influenced by many factors, including wars, events, and China's Dynastic Cycle.
name: Silk Road

desc:
Silk Road Innovations are Innovations that spread westwards along the Silk Road.

Every … years a Silk Road Innovation discovered by the Han Culture will be randomly assigned to the China Situation Region, with all other Silk Road Innovations moving west along the Silk Road.

Cultures with the Sinophilic Tradition have access to all Silk Road Innovations discovered by the Han Culture.

Rulers outside the Silk Road can attempt to bring knowledge back to their Culture via the Visit a Silk Road Market Decision. If successful, the Silk Road Innovation can be discovered like any other Innovation once they return.
name: Silk Road Innovation

desc:
Every Faith considers certain Traits to be Sinful. Characters with these Traits incur Opinion penalties from all characters who consider those traits Sinful, even if they do not share the same Faith. In addition, Characters who have Traits that their own Faith considers Sinful will lose Piety every month.

Exactly what traits are considered to be Sins varies from Faith to Faith, but is typically determined by a combination of that Faith's Tenets and the Religion the Faith belongs to.
name: Sin

desc:
In a Single Combat, two Characters fight, either to the Death or to first blood. Each round, both Characters select one randomly rolled option from a list, trading blows until one Character gets a solid strike in, with the options available depending on your Prowess and Traits.

Some options may give special effects, and most will increase your Likelihood of Success and Risk of Injury. As Duels go on, they grow more dangerous and uncertain, and it becomes easier to win or hurt yourself. After several rounds, Duels enter sudden death, ending immediately with the higher Prowess combatant winning.

When fighting Duels, you may gain temporary Duel Edge Bonus or Duel Edge Penalty Character Modifiers, increasing or reducing your Prowess until the Duel ends.
name: Single Combat

desc: Situations are medium to long term affairs that involve characters within a geographical Situation Region, switching between different Situation Phases.
name: Situation

desc:
Certain Situations transition between Situation Phases when a Situation Catalyst occurs.

A list of which Situation Catalyst are important in each Situation Phase can be found in the Situation window.
name: Situation Catalyst

desc:
Each Situation Phase has its own modifiers and conditions that affect the involved characters.

Some Situation Phases are triggered by specific conditions, while others simply follow the passage of time.
name: Situation Phase

desc: Situations may have more than one region, each of them with independent Situation Phases.
name: Situation Region

desc: Skill challenges are moments where a character has a chance to use one of their Skills to affect the outcome of an event. The higher the skill, or skills, the more likely the character will get their will or a beneficial outcome will happen.
name: Skill Challenges

desc:
The Skills of a Character measure how good they are at various things.

The five main skills are: Diplomacy, Martial, Stewardship, Intrigue, Learning.
name: Skills

desc:
Skirmishers are Men-at-Arms who are lightly armed and skilled in harassing the enemy.

While each kind of Skirmisher is unique, they generally Counter Heavy Infantry, and are in turn Countered by Archers.
name: Skirmishers

desc:
Soldiers is a collective term for the troops in a Regiment or an Army, whether they are Levies, Men-at-Arms, or Knights.

Having the most Soldiers helps win Battles and Sieges.
name: Soldiers

desc:
The Son of Heaven is the Hegemon of China and the Top Liege of the Celestial Government.

The Son of Heaven has a special form of Legitimacy, the Mandate of Heaven, and a unique Participant Group simply called Son of Heaven.
name: Son of Heaven

desc: A Soulmate is a Special Relation indicating a deep, profound, romantic love. It is a stronger Special Relation than a Lover. A Character can only have one Soulmate.
name: Soulmate

desc:
Spearmen are Men-at-Arms who fight on foot with various polearms.

While each kind of Spearman is unique, they generally Counter Heavy Cavalry and Light Cavalry, and are in turn Countered by Heavy Infantry.

Spearmen are also often strong on hilly and mountainous Terrain.
name: Spearmen

desc:
Special Buildings are unique Buildings that are present in a few predetermined places around the world.

Examples include ancient wonders, grand cathedrals, and notable mines. Some are already constructed at the start of the game, while others have to be constructed.

Special Buildings are usually very powerful, and well worth fighting for.
name: Special Building

desc:
Special Guests hold a special place of honor at Grand Activities. Honor someone at your Feast or select a Champion to represent you at your Grand Tournament!

They are more likely to accept your invitation and any activity to which they are invited will not begin until they arrive.
name: Special Guest

desc:
Special Relations are relationships a character has which are not bound by family or Vassalage. These Special Relations fall into several different categories, may carry Character Modifiers for the character involved, and determine what things can happen between them.

Standard Relations:
• Friend
• Lover
• Rival
• Guardian
• Ward
• Mentor
• Student
• Elder
• Disciple

Upgraded Relations:
• Best Friend
• Soulmate
• Nemesis

Childhood Relations:
• Bully
• Victim
• Crush
name: Special Relation

desc:
Special Soldiers are not like regular Armies, as they are not raised from a Holding. Special Soldiers can be gained through Events, and represent various things such as retinues, ravenous hordes and ambitious peasantry.

Normally they do not cost maintenance, and do not reinforce. Use them wisely if you have them.

Several historical Rulers start with Special Soldiers.
name: Special Soldiers

desc:
Any character who is not permitted to compete in a Contest will Spectate instead.

It is also possible to potential Contestants to opt-out instead of competing.
name: Spectator

desc:
Having a high Speed while Traveling will enable you to get to your destination faster. Your Speed is affected by your Skills as well as those of your Caravan Master.

A … contribution can never be lower than 0.
name: Speed

desc:
A Spiritual Head of Faith is Theocratic and does not have to be Landed (although they can be).

Spiritual Heads of Faith usually have access to interactions such as being able to grant Claims or Gold.

Should the Doctrines of the Faith allow for Great Holy Wars then they will be Undirected (e.g. Crusades).
name: Spiritual Head of Faith

desc: A Sponsor is Ruler who funds the Project of an Inspired Character.
name: Sponsor

desc: A Decision where you sponsor local Jewish scholars and reap the benefits.
name: Sponsor Jewish Sciences

desc:
A Spouse is a Character's husband or wife; the result of a Marriage.

In order to have legitimate offspring and produce Heirs, you should have a Spouse or Concubine (though Bastards can be legitimized).

The only way of forging an Alliance is through marriage or Betrothal; your own or that of a close relative.

Your (main) Spouse is also a member of your Council and can perform many useful Councillor Tasks.

Faith Doctrines determine how many Spouses you can have and how they can be Divorced.
name: Spouse

desc: The Spymaster is your Councillor in charge of matters of intrigue and intelligence. Beware of having a disloyal Spymaster, for they can easily conceal and participate in a Murder against you and your close family!
name: Spymaster

desc:
Each Accolade has Squires Aptitude metric, which modifies the Traits and Skills (principally, Prowess Skill, Martial Skill and Hastiluder Trait Experience) of its next Acclaimed Knight.

There are 5 levels of Aptitude for Squires:
•Accomplished
•Capable
•Inexperienced
•Feckless
•Pathetic

Having an Aptitude of Inexperienced or higher will cause the Acclaimed Knight to sporadically influence the Traits and Skills of young, martial-gender Courtiers, giving them priority to assume the Accolade upon Accolade Succession

Squires are principally improved by Glory gain, but also:
•The Acclaimed Knight's Prowess Skill
•The Acclaimed Knight's Martial Skill'
•The Acclaimed Knight gaining Hastiluder Trait Experience
•The Acclaimed Knight gaining Blademaster Trait Experience
•The Martial Skill of the Accolade's Liege
•The Prowess Skill of the Accolade's Liege

Each Accolade Succession resets the Accolade's Squires.
name: Squires

desc:
Despite the brewing troubles, the caliph still commands respect. Rebellions and factionalism are on the back foot, but the lords of Persia will not be brought easily to heel.

The tension might spiral into Unrest, which would mean more chaos to come.
name: Stabilization

desc:
Stable Era Types present times when the Empire is most prosperous and successful, and the Mandate of Heaven is strong.

Eras: …, …
name: Stable Era

desc:
State Faith is the Faith supported and condoned by an Administrative Government. This faith is attached to the Title and not to any one specific Character. It is easier to convert characters in the Realm to the state faith and very difficult to convert them away from it.

Only the Ruler of an Administrative Realm may change the State Faith, but Governors may freely convert to it.
name: State Faith

desc:
A Men-at-Arms Regiment receives bonuses to its effectiveness by being Stationed in a Holding.

Buildings can further increase these bonuses — sometimes for any type of Men-at-Arms, but most commonly for one or two. For example, Small Stables provides a bonus to Stationed Light Cavalry and Heavy Cavalry.

You can Station at any time except during War, or if the Holding is Occupied. If a Holding is lost, any Stationed Men-at-Arms will be unstationed.
name: Stationed Regiment

desc: Profits are made, deals are haggled over, and business continues as usual. There might be some more lucrative options elsewhere, but the Silk Road is more reliable.
name: Steady Trading

desc:
A Steppe Season represents the current climate of The Great Steppe, and the effects that this has on County Fertility, as well as the actions that are available to involved Situation Rulers.

Steppe Seasons are independent to each region, and Nomadic Rulers may want to move to those with positive active Seasons.

On occasion, the same Season may occur in more than one Situation Region at a time.
name: Steppe Season

desc: The Steward is the Councillor in charge of Domain administration, for example matters of Taxation, Culture and Development.
name: Steward

desc: A Stewardship Contract typically involves performing a census or even constructing buildings.
name: Stewardship Contract

desc: The Stewardship Lifestyle is suitable for Characters who want to improve their Domain, appease their Liege and Vassals, or gain a lot of Gold.
name: Stewardship Lifestyle

desc:
Stewardship is a Skill that helps Rulers manage their Domains. It directly increases Taxation, making it a very useful Skill for all rulers.

The corresponding Lifestyle is the Stewardship Lifestyle.
name: Stewardship Skill

desc:
Imprisoned Characters kept in the Dungeon or Stockade suffer from increasing Stress as well as a Health penalty. In time, they are likely to die from Illness or suffer mental breaks.

For Landed Rulers, Commoners are automatically imprisoned in the Dungeon, but can be moved to House Arrest.
name: Stockade

desc:
A Story is a personal situation tied to a Ruler.

There are many kinds of Stories — from owning a Pet Dog to becoming a Conqueror. Each is built from different elements, typically involving key Characters, Titles, or Decisions.
name: Story

desc:
Characters gain Stress when taking actions that conflict with their Personality Traits.

Characters who gain enough Stress will also gain a Stress Level, causing various negative effects on their mental health that persist until they manage to reduce their Stress.

A straight-forward way to relieve Stress is to partake in Activities such as a Hunt.
name: Stress

desc:
Every 100 Stress a character accumulates also causes them to gain a Stress Level. Stress Levels range from 0 to 3, with each level imposing increasing penalties to a character's Fertility and Health.

In addition, as long as a character has at least 1 Stress Level, they are vulnerable to Mental Breaks.
name: Stress Level

desc:
Strife is an Opinion penalty for fellow Vassals.

Strife occurs when a subject of the Liege takes an action against another Vassal. For example, Diarch uses their Borrowed Powers, or in Mandate events, as the Diarch does not have the same authority as their Liege
name: Strife

desc:
A Strong Hook is a very powerful Hook that you might have on a character who you have Blackmailed.

Strong Hooks are much more powerful than Weak Hooks, and can force someone to do terrible deeds for you — such as to become your Agent in a Murder (in addition to everything a Weak Hook can do!)

A Strong Hook also prevents the target from taking any hostile actions towards the holder.

Strong Hooks are not spent when used, but instead go on a cooldown before they can be used again. The passive effect is not lost when the Hook is used.
name: Strong Hook

desc: A Strong Vassal is a Vassal who approaches or exceeds their Liege in power, incurring an Opinion penalty. They see their liege as weak and ill-suited to rule the realm.
name: Strong Vassal

desc:
Struggles are long-term conflicts involving large Regions with many Faiths and Cultures. Within the boundaries of a Struggle, peculiar special rules and Modifiers may take effect, changing over time. Since they last decades to centuries, not all Characters in a Struggle are at War with each other all of the time.

Each Struggle consists of multiple Phases. As Characters within the Struggle Region act (e.g., declaring War, or Marrying), they may activate Catalysts that progress them between the different Phases.

Depending on the degree to which they're seen to be a part of the Struggle by other participants, Characters with Land in the area may be seen as Involved, Interlopers, or Uninvolved.
name: Struggle

desc:
Struggles transition between Phases when certain notable actions are taken, building their Struggle Region's consensus towards a particular mood. A list of which actions are important in which Phase can be found in the Struggle window.

Example: the Opportunity Phase of the Iberian Struggle can transition into either the Hostility Phase or the Conciliation Phase. Murdering an important Character might work towards the former, whilst forming a Marriage Alliance with someone of a different Faith would build towards the latter.
name: Struggle Catalyst

desc:
It's not uncommon for Rulers involved in a Struggle to get into border disputes and petty quarrels, changing with the nature of the current Struggle Phase. The ready availability of niche local disputes allows Rulers to conduct small-scale land grabs, conquering or vassalizing their targets.

Since Clashes depend on the environment of their Struggle, their Prestige cost scales with the current Struggle Phase.
name: Struggle Clash

desc:
Some Catalysts involve the successful completion of a major War by the attacker.

The following Casus Bellis are counted for this:
• Duchy Conquest 
• Individual De Jure Duchy 
• Imperial Reconquest 
• Invasion 
• Clan Invasion 
• Mongol Invasion 
• Major Holy War 
• Both Directed & Undirected Great Holy Wars 
• Subjugation
name: Struggle Large Conquest

desc:
A Phase is a general mood common to Involved Characters and Counties within a Struggle Region. It represents short-term societal trends and mores temporarily dominating the dialogue of the Struggle.

Example: in one Phase, the people of a Region may think that religious tolerance is paramount even if the rest of their faith disagrees.
name: Struggle Phase

desc:
Each Struggle is tied to a Region on the map. A Character's location within this Region (as well as their Culture and Faith) determines whether they are classified as Involved, an Interloper, or Uninvolved.

Counties within a Struggle Region are generally subject to different County Modifiers depending on the current ….
name: Struggle Region

desc: Students are Characters benefiting from the advice of a Mentor, who is helping them to advance one of their Skills. Mentors are gained through events when your Lifestyle Focus is set to a Skill they excel at.
name: Student

desc: A Decision allowing you to improve your Hostile Schemes. Grants Success Chance and Scheme Phase Length in exchange for Stress.
name: Study the Art of Scheming Decision

desc: A Subject is any Ruler that has sworn loyalty to another ruler. They can be of various types, like Vassals or Tributaries, each with their own specifications.
name: Subject

desc: Subject Standing represents the status bestowed onto a Tributary or Vassal by their Suzerain or Liege.
name: Subject Standing

desc:
Diarch Succession governs which of a Liege's direct Vassals or Courtiers is automatically made Diarch when one is needed.

This happens either because a Liege begins Power Sharing or because the current Diarch dies or is removed from office.

Different types of Power Sharing may calculate succession order differently — in a Regency, landless Characters with strong personal connections to their Liege tend to dominate.

Speaking the Liege's Language (and Court Language, if they have one) is almost always crucial.
name: Succession

desc:
Succession occurs when a Ruler dies, dividing their Gold and Titles among their Heirs according to the Succession Laws.

Players will keep playing as their Player Heir even if some titles are lost to other characters.

If there is no player heir, the game will end.

Some rare circumstances can force a Succession to occur even before a ruler dies, such as losing an Excommunication War. Legally speaking, however, Rulers may not choose to abdicate on their own.
name: Succession

desc:
Every Ruler has a main Succession Law that determines what happens to their Titles on Succession.

In addition, an individual Title can sometimes have its own Title Succession Law that takes precedence over the default one. For example, the Holy Roman Empire might be Elective even though the emperor has Partition as main Succession Law.

You can only change Succession Law when at the appropriate level of Crown Authority.
name: Succession Law

desc:
Supply is the amount of food and equipment an Army carries. Armies will begin losing Supply when their size goes above the Supply Limit of their current location.

Armies that are running low on Supplies will suffer an Advantage penalty in Battle, and when they run out completely they will begin suffering from Attrition.

Supply increases over time as long as the Army remains below the Supply Limit in friendly territory.
name: Supply

desc:
The Supply Limit dictates the amount of Soldiers you may have in a Barony, as determined by the Barony's Terrain and Development.

Should your total Army size go above the Supply Limit, your Armies will lose Supply and eventually suffer from Attrition.
name: Supply Limit

desc:
Supporters are Guests at the Coronation Activity supporting the Host in their ascension to the throne. They will have special opportunities to aid the Ruler in securing their Legitimacy.

They are directly opposed to the Detractors, guests who are attempting to foil the host.
name: Supporter

desc: A Suzerain is a Ruler with at least one Tributary. Suzerains may themselves be Tributaries to another Ruler, but they must never be Vassals.
name: Suzerain

desc:
Your Suzerain Taxes are the Taxes that you must pay to your Suzerain as part of your Obligations.

From your Suzerain's point of view, these same taxes are instead called Tributary Taxes to distinguish them from any taxes they may owe to their own Suzerain.
name: Suzerain Taxes

desc: At the cost of Prestige, Piety, or Gold, a Liege or a Diarch can move the Scales of Power in their favor.
name: Swing the Scales of Power

desc:
Sōryō is a type of Feudal Government unique to Japan.

Sōryō represents local lords who have discarded or supplanted the reach of the central Ritsuryō government and rule provinces as their own fiefs.

Sōryō Characters do not use Influence, but Noble Family Heads retain their Family Manor and House Aspiration.

Though they cannot be elected Ruling Regent, Sōryō Rulers may take power via the Install Ruling Regent Faction, and use the Formalize Shōgunate Decision.

Sōryō Ruling Regents govern the Realm on behalf of the Japanese Emperor, inherit by Primogeniture Succession, and may be overthrown by Faction demand.

Sōryō House Heads may create and join House Blocs within the Realm.

Japanese Governments have a lower Domain Limit than others, which may be increased by upgrading the Family Manor.

Sōryō refers to the early stages of Japanese feudalization beginning in the Heian-period, increasingly formalized under the Kamakura-period's first Shōgunate.
name: Sōryō Government

desc:
When playing a Board Game, different play styles counter your opponent. Countering their moves severely reduces the points they gain from them, even if successful. Skilled opponents may note your own skills and deliberately attempt to counter you.

In Tabula:
• Intrigue counters Learning
• Learning counters Stewardship
• Stewardship counters Intrigue
name: Tabula

desc:
A Tax Collector enables Tax Jurisdictions to function.

Their Aptitude determines the amount of Taxes and Levies they collect for their Liege.
name: Tax Collector

desc:
Each Tax Jurisdiction can have a different Tax Decree, modifying the Taxes and Levies contributed by its Taxpayers.

Tax Decrees will often change the Obligations in return of another penalty or boon.
name: Tax Decree

desc:
A Tax Jurisdiction is a group of Taxpayers made up of Clan Vassals. Each Tax Jurisdiction supports up to 12 Taxpayers.

Each Tax Jurisdiction can have a Tax Decree.

The number of available Tax Jurisdictions is determined by Rank, Traditions, and Innovations.

A Tax Jurisdiction requires a Tax Collector to be appointed.
name: Tax Jurisdiction

desc: A Tour Type in which you attempt to extract wealth from your Vassals, gaining Gold.
name: Taxation Tour

desc:
Taxes are the most important monthly source of Gold Income for Rulers.

Every Holding a ruler has provides them with some Domain Taxes every month. In addition, most Vassals have an Obligation to pay a portion of their own collected Taxes to their Liege in the form of Liege Taxes.
name: Taxes

desc: Taxpayers are Clan Vassals that have been assigned to a Tax Jurisdiction, and will contribute monthly Tax Income and Levies as long as a Tax Collector is appointed.
name: Taxpayer

desc:
In Teams Contests, all Qualifying Contestants on the team with the most combined points at the end of the contest receive rewards.

Teams Contests:
•Melee
name: Teams

desc: Temple Citadels are a pragmatic mix of the Castle fortification and the Temple worship — it is the standard Holding Type for Mandala Rulers. They provide an even amount of Levies, Piety and Taxes.
name: Temple Citadel Holding

desc:
Temples are a Holding Type that can be held by members of the Clergy as Church Holdings (the Theocratic Government Form). However, in Faiths with the Lay Clergy Doctrine, anyone can hold Temples without penalty.

Temples provide a fairly even mix of Levies and Taxes.
name: Temple Holding

desc:
A Temporal Head of Faith acts much like a normal Ruler, with the Head of Faith Title being destroyed should they lose all their land.

Should the Doctrines of the Faith allow for Great Holy Wars they will be Directed (e.g. Jihads).
name: Temporal Head of Faith

desc: While Doctrines represent issues a Faith must take a stance on, Tenets represent the Faith's unique quirks and rites.
name: Tenet

desc:
Each Barony has a specific dominant Terrain which can affect things like Supply, movement speed of Armies, the efficacy of the various types of Men-at-Arms Regiments in Battle and the Buildings that can be constructed there.

Many Commander Traits also deal with Terrain.
name: Terrain

desc:
Terrified Characters are paralyzed by fear of another character and will rarely take any hostile actions against that character, including starting Factions.

Characters are Terrified or Intimidated by Dread and/or a cowardly personality.
name: Terrified

desc:
By remaining loyal , Test Loyalty Value may increase their loyalty meter.

By becoming disloyal, debug_test_story may lower their loyalty meter.
name: Test Loyalty Value

desc:
The Great Steppe represents the endless sea of grass of the Eurasian Steppe, and the climate conditions that shape it, and is divided into three regions: Western, Central and Eastern.

The different Steppe Seasons depict these both positive and adverse events, offering opportunities for special actions only available during that time, and modifying the County Fertility of each region.

Only Nomadic and Herder Rulers take part in this Situation and the Gurkhan represents the most powerful ruler in the entire region.
name: The Great Steppe

desc: Theocracy is an unplayable Government Form available for some Faiths depending on Doctrines. They are usually lead by a Head of Faith or a Landed Realm Priest. A Bishop might also become an Independent Theocratic ruler in their own right.
name: Theocracy

desc:
Vassals who have the Theocratic Government form.

How they function is determined by a Faith's Doctrines.
name: Theocratic Vassal

desc:
The land equivalent of Title Rank, the Tier determines the position of a Title within the hierarchy of the game.

All Titles have a Tier, which determines the highest possible Tier of Vassals that the Holder can have.

Hegemony > Empire > Kingdom > Duchy > County > Barony.
name: Tier

desc:
A Title is essentially a certificate of land ownership.

The smallest unit of land on the map is the Barony. Baronies are organized into larger areas called Counties. Counties De Jure belong to a Duchy, duchies to a Kingdom, and Kingdoms to an Empire.

Duchies, Kingdoms and Empires do not always have a Holder, but are Titles that can be Created by a ruler who controls enough of the corresponding territory.
name: Title

desc: Vassals can owe Allegiance to a specific Title rather than the person of their Liege. This can only happen if the Title has its own Succession Law. On Succession, such Vassals will become vassals of the new Title Holder.
name: Title Allegiance

desc:
A Claim on a Title represents a legal right to own it and provides a Casus Belli to conquer it through War. Claims also provide a valid reason to Revoke Titles off Vassal Holders.

Claims are usually given to Rulers whenever they lose control of Titles to someone else, but can also be created through the Fabricate Claim Task.

Furthermore, each child (even Bastards) of a ruler has an Implicit Claim on all of that ruler's Titles. If they do not inherit that title from the … when they die, those … will convert to Pressed Claims, which can then be inherited by their own children as Unpressed Claims.
name: Title Claim

desc:
A Ruler who controls the majority of a not-yet-created Title's De Jure land will be able to create its associated Title. Creating a Title costs Gold, but gives Prestige.

Only Duchy, Kingdom or Empire tier Titles can be created.

The Issues widget contains a list of all Titles which you can currently create.
name: Title Creation

desc: The Title Heir is the Heir to a specific Title with its own Title Succession. They will receive that Title when the current Holder dies.
name: Title Heir

desc: Titles can be given a Title-Specific Law that is specific to that Title. This Law will dictate different rules for succession than other titles held by the same character.
name: Title Law

desc:
Title Men-at-Arms are Men-at-Arms that exists for a given Title. Instead of being personally owned by the Ruler, these troops always follow the Title they belong to. Meaning that whomever owns the Title will also own and control the corresponding troops.

Title Men-at-Arms are used by certain Government Forms, such as Administrative.
name: Title Men-at-Arms

desc: A Title Revocation Reason gives a Liege the opportunity to freely Revoke a Title from a subject. They are most often gained from the subject being a Criminal.
name: Title Revocation Reason

desc:
A Title can have its own Succession Law, which is different from that of the Holder's Realm.

Kingdoms and Empires are most likely to have a traditional Title Succession.

The Holder of the Title can add or remove Title-Specific Succession Laws, usually at the cost of Prestige

Domiciles also have their own Title Succession, which cannot be removed.
name: Title Succession

desc:
A Titular Title is a Title that has no De Jure land on the map. Non-Titular Titles can become Titular through De Jure Drift.

Mercenary, Head of Faith and Holy Order Titles are often Titular.
name: Titular Title

desc:
The 'Top Liege' is the Liege at the top of the Vassal hierarchy.

They are fully Independent Rulers and answer to no mortal.
name: Top Liege

desc: The 'Top Realm' is the Realm of the Top Liege.
name: Top Realm

desc:
Imprisoned Characters can be Tortured, damaging their Health or even maiming them in different ways.

Torture can relieve Stress for Callous and Sadistic Characters, but causes Stress for those of a kind nature.

Torturing Rulers can also increase your Dread.
name: Torture

desc:
A Soldier's Toughness determines how much Damage they can take in Battle before they become a Casualty.

A Levy Soldier has … Toughness.
name: Toughness

desc: A Grand Activity in which a Liege pays a royal visit to a collection of their Vassals to reap rewards such as Gold, Dread, Opinion, Control, and Cultural Acceptance.
name: Tour

desc: An Activity Phase during a Royal Tour in which a liege can either: attend a Hosted Dinner, Tour the Grounds of their Vassal, or enjoy a Cultural Festival.
name: Tour Stop

desc: A value which determines which rewards you will get at the end of your Grand Tour. You can gain and lose points by selecting certain options at the start of your tour and making decisions which align with your Tour Type.
name: Tour Success

desc: An Activity Phase during a Royal Tour in which a Vassal is visited by their Liege, which often results in an increase in Control in their Counties.
name: Tour the Grounds

desc: An option which determines what kind of Tour you're having and which rewards you gain. Tour types include Majesty Tour, Intimidation Tour, and Taxation Tour.
name: Tour Type

desc:
A Character's Traits describe their personality, quirks, deeds and state of being.

Traits can have many effects, but many affect the Skills of a Character.

Personality traits also greatly affect how characters can be expected to behave. Acting against your own Personality causes Stress.

Some Traits are Congenital and can be inherited by offspring.
name: Trait

desc: Experience is required in order to move further down a Trait Path and change the bonuses the Trait provides.
name: Trait Experience

desc:
Some Traits offer several paths, each of which will change the Trait in different ways.

Earning Trait Experience is required to move further down a path.
name: Trait Path

desc: Rulers can Transfer one of their Vassals to another Vassal, as long as the former is of lower rank than the latter. This is a good way of raising a Vassal's Opinion, particularly if the Transferred vassal is De Jure part of their Realm.
name: Transfer

desc: A Transport Contract typically involves transporting goods, like Artifacts, or escorting important character like Wards over intermediate distances.
name: Transport Contract

desc:
Travel is the means by which a Character gets from one Location to another, primarily to attend Activities.

There are numerous ways to plan your journey like choosing a Caravan Master to hire, selecting Travel Options, and customizing your route. You will meet many interesting characters along your path, but be wary of Danger that may lay in wait.
name: Travel

desc: An option you pick when planning your Travel to enhance or modify the journey you are about to set out on.
name: Travel Option

desc: Bring an old and withered adventurer to find their final treasure.
name: Treasure Map Contract

desc:
In certain Administrative Governments, Treasury represents assets that may only be used for governmental purposes, in contrast with your personal Gold.

EFFECT_LIST_BULLETAs a Vassal, you will receive Treasury from your Liege, based on your Tax contributions and other obligations
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETTreasury is created by the Top Liege, who converts a percentage of Taxation income into Treasury
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETYou can transfer Gold to the Treasury at will
EFFECT_LIST_BULLETThe Treasury stays with the Title if it gets a new Holder
name: Treasury

desc: When spending more than the Budget Capacity, an amount will be subtracted from the monthly Treasury income.
name: Treasury Budget Deficit

desc:
A system responsible for distributing central funds to specific Vassals and sub-vassals at specific allocation rates.

When a budget is enacted, a per-vassal Budget Base Rate is calculated for each Budget Category based on the available Budget Capacity.

 The calculated base rate will not be changed until a new budget is enacted in the future! So if you get more recipients, your budget costs will rise.
name: Treasury Budgeting

desc:
Treasury Debt is the state of having a negative amount of Treasury Treasury. This typically happens when a Governor at war hires Mercenaries without having enough Treasury to cover the full cost, when they are at war for too long, or if they pay too much in Salaries for what they collect from their Vassals.

 While in Debt you cannot declare new Wars, your Men-at-Arms that depend on Treasury do not reinforce, and your enemies will have an Advantage over you in battle. The deeper into debt you fall, the more penalties you will get — fewer Levies, reduced Popular Opinion, and your Vassals will like you less.

In addition to this, various other minor destabilizing events may occur, such as gaining County Corruption in your Domain Counties. 

It is generally a good idea to strike your enemies while they are in Debt, as they will fight with reduced Advantage!
name: Treasury Debt

desc:
In some Cultures, issues that cannot be settled through words or war are grounds for a Trial-by-Combat instead. If accepted, the two Characters engage in a Duel for a preselected settlement. If the offending party wins, they prove their innocence.

The general requirements for such a Trial are:
•Both of you must be of a valid culture.
•You must have an Imprisonment Reason against them (which will be used up).
•They must not be your Liege, Vassal, or the Guest or Courtier of yourself or one of your Vassals.

Characters that are not fit to fight themselves can still be challenged as long as they are Rulers, nominating a Knight to fight on their behalf instead.

A Combat may only opt to be fought to the Death if the aggrieved party is Tribal and both Characters are fighting personally in the Duel; if the offending party has to nominate a champion to fight on their behalf, then Death is not an option.
name: Trial-by-Combat

desc:
Tribal realms have stunted county Development, cannot advance past Tribal Era Innovations, cannot construct new Holdings, and are usually unable to change their Succession Law.

However, they can make use of Prestige rather than Gold to build their realms and hire Men-at-Arms, and have access to more Casus Belli compared to Feudal Realms. Non-Tribal armies suffer a Supply Limit penalty in hostile Tribal territory.
name: Tribal

desc:
Tribal Authority represents the general influence that a Tribal Ruler wields over their Vassals. Compared to Crown Authority, it offers fewer powers and at later levels.

There are four levels of Tribal Authority: Disparate Tribes, Limited, High, and Absolute. Increasing Tribal Authority costs an amount of Prestige depending on the level and the ruler's Learning Skill, but is generally more expensive than increasing crown authority.

Vassals dislike higher levels of Tribal Authority, and lowering it is the primary goal of any Liberty Faction.
name: Tribal Authority

desc:
Tribes are poor in Taxes but rich in Levies, Prestige, and Men-at-Arms upgrades. They have limited upgrade potential and, while strong early, quickly dwindle in power the longer time progresses. Only Tribal characters can hold them without penalties.

If a Tribe exists in a County, no other Holdings can be built. Feudal rulers will have to spend Gold to transform Tribes into Castles.
name: Tribal Holding

desc:
A Tributary is a Ruler who has reached an agreement with another ruler, their Suzerain.

The Tributary provides a periodic tribute in the form of Herd, Taxes, Prestige or even Piety (depending on their type) and, in exchange, gains a Truce with the Suzerain.

Tributaries are a looser form of subject that cannot join Factions, but can break free if their requirements aren't met.

If the Suzerain is no longer Landed nor Migrating, the Tributaries will break free after a short amount of time.
name: Tributary

desc:
Tributary Contract dictate the Obligations between a Tributary and their Suzerain.

All Tributaries have access to different Obligations, negotiated individually for each Tributary.

Tributaries pay a percentage of their total Taxes, Levies, Herd, Prestige or even Piety to their Suzerain, based on their Obligations.
name: Tributary Contract

desc:
Your Tributary Taxes consist of the Taxes that you receive from your Tributaries. The amount depends on each Tributary's Obligations.

From your Tributaries' point of view, these same taxes are called Suzerain Taxes to distinguish them from any Tributary Taxes they collect from their own Tributaries.
name: Tributary Taxes

desc:
As a Tributary, respects, as well as Tribute, needs to be paid to the Suzerain on a regular basis.

Failing to do so might have a various slew of consequences, of which the most benign one is to lose Legitimacy.
name: Tribute Mission

desc:
Trilateral Interactions require not only an approval of a recipient, but also of a third party.

An example would be Borrowed Powers, where a Liege may use their Diarchy Veto.
name: Trilateral Interaction

desc:
Every War ends with a Truce; a period when the Attacker may not declare War again on that same Ruler (the Defender is not bound by the Truce).

Truces can be broken, but there is a severe penalty.
name: Truce

desc:
The winner of a Turns Contests is the Qualifying Contestant with the most points at the end of the competition.

Turns Contests:
•Archery
•Recital
name: Turns

desc:
Many actions of a Ruler are considered Tyrannical — against the law or religious Doctrine. For example, Imprisoning or Revoking Titles off someone who has committed no Crime is considered Tyrannical.

Tyranny acts as a blanket Opinion modifier for all characters in the Realm.
name: Tyranny

desc: Any unallocated treasury budget will contribute to general … income.
name: Unallocated Treasury Budget

desc:
An Undirected Great Holy War is declared by a Spiritual Head of Faith with the intention of bringing a Kingdom under the rule of their Faith.

Undirected Great Holy Wars are not started immediately, instead they enter a Preparation Phase.

Before and during the war, rulers of the attacking Faith can choose to donate Gold to the War Chest.

If victorious, the targeted Kingdom will be taken and given to a character of the attacking Faith. Rewards for the attackers include Piety and potentially having their Dynasty become Landed within the conquered Kingdom.
name: Undirected Great Holy War

desc: A Casus Belli that allows a House Head to reclaim House members from another Realm as Vassal.
name: Unify The House

desc:
Unifying Actions towards your House members will increase your House Unity.

House Heads can use the Steer House Unity Decision and the Extol Virtuousness Interaction to greatly increase Unity.

Some examples of unifying actions are:EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Negotiate Alliance
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Offer to Join War
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Gift Artifact
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Pay Ransom
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Offer Guardianship
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Ask to Join Holy Order
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Restore Inheritance
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Abandon Hook
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Stop Vassal War
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Sponsor Inspiration
EFFECT_LIST_BULLET Swear Oath of True Friendship
name: Unifying Actions

desc:
For a Character to be considered Uninvolved in a particular Struggle, they need only have their Capital outside the Struggle Region.

This means they're considered an outsider, someone who not only doesn't have a serious stake in the ongoing Phases, but who shouldn't, because they clearly couldn't understand the local nuances.

As one of the only things people inside a Struggle can agree on is that Uninvolved Characters have no business in their lands, Uninvolved Rulers generally take harsh penalties in any Counties they hold within a Struggle Region.
name: Uninvolved

desc: This Game Rule significantly alters the gameplay experience.
name: Unique Game Rule

desc: Unlanded Characters have no Holdings in their Domain, but can theoretically still be Rulers of a sort. For example, this can be the case for Heads of Faith and the Grand Masters of Holy Orders.
name: Unlanded

desc: These are disabled Holdings that do not count toward your Domain Limit.
name: Unmanaged Holdings

desc:
An Unpredictable Ruler has no Traits pushing them towards any specific Economic Archetype and may decide upon any strategy.

They can choose to temporarily invest heavily in Buildings like a Builder, or to build up their Realm slowly with a buffer of Gold. They go to War at a regular pace.
name: Unpredictable

desc:
Unpressed Claims are legally tenuous, and are not inherited by the children of the Claimant.

However, Unpressed Claims become Pressed if they are used in a Casus Belli to declare War — even if the war ends in a White Peace.
name: Unpressed Claim

desc: Unreformed Pagan Faiths get a Battle Advantage in Counties of their faith.
name: Unreformed Pagan Combat Advantage

desc:
Beset by rebellions and intrigues, the Caliphate crumbles. Ambitious warlords and cunning governors alike grasp at whatever power they can usurp, squabbling constantly.

Over time, unless the situation is resolved by an Ending Phase, the realm will enter a Stabilization phase as desperate supporters claw back caliphal authority.
name: Unrest

desc:
Unrestricted is the highest level of Dominance. This level can only be obtained by one Character in the entire game, and they will become the Greatest of Khans.

Independent Rulers may use the Become the Greatest of All Khans and Reform the Great Khaganate Decisions
name: Unrestricted

desc: Unruly Nomads is the lowest level of Dominance. At this level, Migration can only target De Jure County Titles within the The Great Steppe and Characters cannot be Imprisoned.
name: Unruly Nomads

desc:
Unstable Era Types present times when the Empire is in turmoil due to internal or external forces, and the Mandate of Heaven is wavering.

Eras: …, …
name: Unstable Era

desc: An Untaxed Jurisdiction is a Tax Jurisdiction with Taxpayers, but without a Tax Collector. This means that the assigned Taxpayers will not give any Taxes or Levies to their Liege.
name: Untaxed Jurisdiction

desc:
Untaxed Vassals are Clan Vassals who are not assigned to a Tax Jurisdiction as Taxpayers, and therefore not contributing Taxes or Levies.

Once assigned to a Tax Jurisdiction with a Tax Collector, they will start paying monthly.
name: Untaxed Vassals

desc:
A Title held by a foreign Ruler can usually be Usurped if more than 50% of its De Jure Counties are within your Realm. This process gives the Title to you, which is particularly important for ensuring you are the Rightful Liege of your Vassals.

Usurpation is more difficult if the current holder's Faith is hostile to yours; in this case usurpation is only possible if the holder no longer possesses any of its De Jure Counties inside his Realm.
name: Usurp Title

desc:
A Valuable Prisoner is a Prisoner who provides War Score when captured during a War.

For a person to be deemed a Valuable Prisoner, they have to be third in line or higher to inherit their war leader's primary title.

Valuable Prisoners are released when the war ends, unlike Prisoners of War.
name: Valuable Prisoner

desc:
This is a special type of War, where the attacker intends to move their Realm to the War Target wholesale.
