If they win, they will immediately annex the appropriate Counties and move their Capital there. Their old vassals will go independent, and their old Counties will be given to upstart local warlords. Varangian Adventures are ONLY available to Duke and Count-Tier Rulers, becoming progressively more expensive with each successful Adventure.

This Casus Belli is NEVER available after the Tribal Era, and cannot be used against other Cultures that can Adventure or against neighboring Rulers.

North Germanics launching their first Varangian Adventure receive up to … bonus Special Soldiers, the amount going up with every same-Faith same-Culture county they completely control within Mainland Scandinavia.
name: Varangian Adventure

desc:
A Vassal is a Ruler who has sworn fealty to another ruler — their Liege.

The Vassal provides their liege with Levies and Taxes — their Obligations — in exchange for protection.

If a Vassal's Opinion of their liege is low, they may join Factions, or Scheme to replace their liege with someone else.
name: Vassal

desc:
Vassal Contracts dictate the Obligations between a Vassal and their Liege.

Vassals of the Feudal, Clan, Administrative and Nomadic Government Forms have access to different Obligations, negotiated individually for each Vassal.

All Vassals pay a percentage of their total Taxes and Levies to their Liege, based on their Obligations. These Contributions can in turn be modified by 'fine print' options such as Fortification Rights.

Some Special Contracts are limited to certain Ranks:
•Special Contract and Special Contract: Duke and above
•Special Contract: Count and above
•Special Contract: Count only

Note, Governor Obligations are also known as Province Administrations.
name: Vassal Contract

desc: Treasury sent to direct Vassals through their Liege, based on their tax contributions and other Obligations.
name: Vassal Development

desc:
As a Liege, you can issue Directives to your Vassals, influencing their Councillor Tasks and which Buildings they construct.

To issue a Directive, you need to enable it, such as by having 50 or more Opinion with the Vassal. Advanced Government Forms do not require this.
name: Vassal Directive

desc:
The Vassal Limit determines how many Direct Vassals you can legally have (excluding Barony-tier vassals).

Although you can go above your Vassal Limit, doing so will lower the Taxes and Levies your vassals provide, and you may be better off Transferring some vassals to stay below the limit.
name: Vassal Limit

desc:
Vassal Obligations define how much Tax and how many Levies a Vassal provides to their Liege. A Vassal's Government Form determines how their Obligations are modified.

For example, Feudal and Clan Vassals Obligations depend on their Vassal Contract, while Administrative Vassal's depend on their Province Administration.
name: Vassal Obligations

desc:
Every Vassal has a Vassal Stance which affects the Opinion they have with you as their Liege, and which Heir they prefer as successor to the Realm.

Vassals in the same stance will like and dislike the same things. For example; all Glory Hound Vassals dislike when you lose Wars.

Every Vassal Stance prefers one specific Heir. Upon succession, each preferred Heir will have lower Legitimacy Expectations with the Vassals of that stance.

The Vassal Stances are:
•Courtly
•Parochial
•Glory Hound
•Zealot
•Minority
•Minor Landholder
•Belligerent
name: Vassal Stance

desc:
Your Vassal Taxes consist of the Taxes that you receive from you Vassals. The amount depends on the each Vassal's Obligations.

From your Vassals' point of view, these same taxes are called Liege Taxes to distinguish them from any Vassal Taxes they collect from their own Vassals.
name: Vassal Taxes

desc: A Victim is a Child who is currently being harassed by another Child, often for reasons unclear to anyone but their Bully. Upon reaching Adulthood, they may become Rivals with their Bully, or learn to put the struggles of youth behind them.
name: Victim

desc:
Victory is one of three possible Peace Offers. The exact outcome of Victory in a War depends on the Casus Belli.

For the Attacker, it typically involves the seizure of Titles within the War Target region.

For the Defender, Victory usually means the attacker has to pay a large sum of gold as war reparations.
name: Victory

desc:
Every Faith considers certain Traits to be Virtuous. Characters with these Traits gain Opinion bonuses from all characters who consider those traits Virtuous, even if they do not share the same Faith. In addition, Characters who have Traits that their own Faith considers Virtuous will gain bonus Piety every month.

Exactly what traits are considered to be Virtues varies from Faith to Faith, but is typically determined by a combination of that Faith's Tenets and the Religion the Faith belongs to.
name: Virtue

desc:
A Vizier is a type of Diarch that Clan Rulers may voluntarily appoint to help boost their Income. They have less to Borrowed Powers but can be very difficult to remove.

Viziers grant their Liege bonus Tax Jurisdictions scaling to their Stewardship, and increase the Aptitude of Tax Collectors according to how much the Scales of Power favor them.

Crucially, Lieges can drain Viziers of their Gold Gold via the Mulct Vizier Interaction.

Being empowered civil servants, Viziers are not considered a prestigious position for Nobles despite their influence. Their successor is picked according to Vizier Succession Score.

As a Ruler can only have one Diarch at a time, they'll remain in the event that a Regency would occur.
name: Vizier

desc:
Whilst in office, Viziers will spend their Gold on increasingly ornate Extravagance Modifiers, pampering themselves and the other social elite of their Liege's Capital.

The Liege may loot these Modifiers by using the Mulct Vizier Interaction, transforming them into Gold the Vizier is forced to transfer.

When a Vizier stops Sharing Power, they lose the ability to maintain their extravagant lifestyle, and any remaining Modifiers are lost.

Looting more and later tiers provides more Gold — the four tiers of Extravagance are:
• Notable
• Remarkable
• Famous
• Illustrious
name: Vizier Extravagance

desc:
In a Vizierate, the next Vizier is picked based on which candidate has the highest Vizier Succession Score.

Prospective candidates may occasionally try to convince the Ruler to let them replace the incumbent in exchange for Gold.

This allows only landless and Baron-Tier Characters, favoring those with strong Diplomacy, Stewardship, and Intrigue, as well as Traits that make for a good civil servant.

Special Relations with the incumbent Vizier or the Liege's Spouses, Concubines, and Adult landless Children can drastically affect the score.
name: Vizier Succession Score

desc: Voter Strength represents the amount of influence that an Elector carries when voting in an elective Succession Law. This value usually increases depending on a ruler's Rank, but other factors may come into play depending on the Title's law.
name: Voter Strength

desc: Characters who do not belong to a Court or hold any Titles are called Wanderers. They travel the world, visiting Courts as Guests along the way. Wanderers might become Mercenary Captains, leaders of Holy Orders, Clergy members, or City holders.
name: Wanderer

desc: The Wandering Lifestyle is suitable for Characters who want to see Points of Interest, or gain additional bonuses from Traveling.
name: Wandering Lifestyle

desc:
The Wanua Government shares weaknesses with the Government, but also have reduced Domain Limit and Vassal Limit. While they use Gold to construct Buildings and recruit Men-at-Arms, they earn very little Gold from Buildings.

However, they can Barter Goods Barter, Raid, and have synergies with the Mandala Government as they gain Legitimacy from being a Tributary.
name: Wanua

desc:
Armed conflict is the most straightforward way to expand your Realm. However, declaring War requires a justification for doing so, called a Casus Belli. You cannot achieve more with a War than the selected casus belli permits.

Wars are won by defeating enemy Armies in Battle and Occupying enemy Holdings. Doing so will accrue War Score, eventually forcing the enemy to accept Defeat in the Peace Offer.

Regardless of the outcome of a War, the attacker gains a Truce toward the defender for a time, but the defender is free to declare a new war immediately.
name: War

desc:
The War Chest is a collection of Gold, Piety and Prestige. The contents are primarily used as rewards for successfully winning Undirected Great Holy Wars, where they are divided between the attackers based upon their participation in the War.

A certain portion of what's in the War Chest is also divided between the attackers as the War is declared.

If an Undirected Great Holy War is defeated, the defenders will divide the Piety and Prestige portion of the War Chest between them (the Gold is lost.)
name: War Chest

desc:
Rulers who are helping their Allies in a War gain War Contribution depending on the number and size of Battles they fight in, as well as the number of Holdings they manage to Occupy.

After a war ends, each Contributor is rewarded in relation to their Contribution. The exact spoils depend on the war's Casus Belli, but is typically Gold, Prestige or Piety.

Note that Contribution increases even from losing Battles.
name: War Contribution

desc:
The primary attacker and the primary defender of a War. Usually this is the character who instigated the war, and the Top Liege of the character who holds the War Target.

There are a variety of Casus Belli for many different kinds of war, some with different characters as the War Leaders.
name: War Leaders

desc:
A measure of which side is winning in a War. It goes from -100 to 100, with e.g. -25 for one side being 25 for the other. At 100 War Score, you can force the other side to accept your Peace Offer.

War Score can be gained by:
• Defeating Armies in Battle
• Imprisoning the enemy Ruler or their Heirs (not including their Allies)
• Occupying enemy Holdings (especially within the War Target)
• Occupying the enemy's Realm Capital
• Controlling all Objectives for an extended period of time
name: War Score

desc:
A region on the map targeted by a Casus Belli in a War. If the casus belli does not target a specific region, the Realm Capital of the defender is the War Target.

The attacking side gains more War Score by Occupying Holdings within the War Target. Conversely, the defender will — after an initial grace period — start accruing war score for holding on to all Counties in the War Target region.
name: War Target

desc: A Ward is a Child being Educated by a Guardian. Each Guardian can handle up to two Wards.
name: Ward

desc:
A Ruler who has been sent a Hostage by a foreign Home Court as an assurance of peace or submission.

A Warden will accrue Prestige over time for each Hostage in their Court.
name: Warden

desc:
A Warlike Ruler wants to be ready to declare War, always. They will save Gold for War before investing it in developing their Realm. If a Warlike Ruler is at peace for an extended period of time, they will use the Gold in their war chest to build Buildings.

Warlike rulers are more likely to create and promote heroic Legends.

Bold and greedy Rulers tend to be Warlike.
Common Traits include Wrathful, Impatient, Sadistic, Ambitious, Vengeful, Irritable, and Zealous.
name: Warlike

desc:
A Weak Hook is a fairly common Hook that you might have on a character who owes you a favor, or that you have manipulated to do your will.

While there are many interactions where a Weak Hook can be used, for example in Marriage proposals, they cannot be used to force someone to become your Agent in a Murder and do not provide a passive benefit (for that, a Strong Hook is necessary.)

Every child born to a Noble House also owes the House Head an initial Weak Hook.

Once a Weak Hook is used, it is spent.
name: Weak Hook

desc: The Activity Phase in a Grand Wedding in which the Spouses consummate the wedding, and the guests continue their celebration.
name: Wedding Night

desc:
A White Peace is one of three possible Peace Offers. Sometimes, both sides will agree that the War is no longer worth pursuing.

With a White Peace, the Attacker typically still loses some Piety or Prestige, but far less than with a humiliating Defeat.
name: White Peace

desc:
Winning at a Board Game is accomplished in one of two ways:
• Obtaining a dramatic lead in score over your opponent.
• Being the defending player if there's no clear winner after round ….
name: Winning

desc: Winter steadily drains Supply over time, making armies lose Supply while standing in a barony affected by Winter. The Supply penalty increases with each severity. Winter has three different severities; Mild, Normal, and Harsh.
name: Winter Severity

desc:
Yurt Buildings are unique improvements to the Nomadic Capital.

Mechanically, they are Domicile Buildings — though many represent social customs or simply areas of focus for the Nomad tribe, rather than being literal structures.

The bonuses they can confer include:
• Unlocking Court Positions and Nomadic Decisions and Character Interactions
• Various bonuses to Herd and County Fertility, including Terrain specializations
• Unlocking and improving Nomadic Men-at-Arms and boosting the strength of Nomadic Horde
• Unique nomadic Cultural Tradition bonuses
• Ways to manage your Vassals and Tributaries, as well as influence Characters at your court.
• Kurultai and Obedience bonuses.
name: Yurt Buildings
